This proposal seeks to implement Pivot Sacramento's Early Childhood Education (ECE) Pre-Apprenticeship Program, an innovative workforce development initiative designed to address the critical shortage of qualified early childhood educators in our community. This program provides a structured pathway for opportunity youth (ages 16-24) to gain foundational skills, earn wages, and progress toward full licensure as Associate Teachers.

RecipientName: South Bay Workforce Investment Board Inc
ProjectAbstract: The South Bay Workforce Investment Board (SBWIB) will launch a $1.6 million initiative to address barriers to career entry for 200 opportunity youth (ages 16-24) across California through pre-apprenticeship training. In response to a worsening shortage of healthcare professionals in Southern California-including an anticipated 36,000 nurse shortfall statewide source: UCSF Healthforce Center, 2023 -the program will provide training for high-demand occupations such as Certified Nursing Assistant, Pharmacy Technician, and Dental Assistant through our Health Flex pathway.

BAVC Media requests a Pre-Apprenticeship Implementation Grant to grow our existing Registered Video Editor Pre-Apprenticeship. In collaboration with our established partner, the San Francisco Office of Workforce Development (OEWD), our Pre-Apprenticeship builds an efficient pipeline for opportunity youth to access sustainable careers as multimedia content editors. The Pre-Apprenticeship offers rigorous technical and soft skill development while integrating support services, career and higher education exposure, mentorship, and hands-on learning for participants.

ProjectTitle: Miramar College Pre-Apprenticeship Fire Academy Implementation Grant
ProjectAbstract: The San Diego Miramar College Pre-Apprenticeship Fire Academy in partnership with California Firefighter Joint Apprenticeship Committee  (Cal-JAC) will prepare individuals with the skills and competencies needed for entry level firefighter positions and placement on the Statewide Eligibility List (SEL) for over 170 fire departments in CA. The program can include hands-on training to individuals in simulated lab experiences meeting all State Fire Training (SFT) Fire Fighter 1 Fire Academy requirements.

ProjectTitle: Canal Alliance Transportation Apprenticeship Planning Grant
ProjectAbstract: Canal Alliance proposes to expand upon its seven-year partnership with College of Marin (COM) by engaging with Marin Transit and Workforce Alliance of the North Bay (WANB) to develop a Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) to train opportunity youth living in Marin County as skilled maintenance technicians for diesel and electric busses.

The LegalTech Apprenticeship Program is a four-year apprenticeship for opportunity youth (ages 18-24) in Los Angeles County that integrates step-ladder legal credentials (Legal Document Assistant, Paralegal) with in-demand technology skills (Software Engineer, Product Designer, Data Scientist, Al Prompt Engineer). Through invention-based learning in classroom-based, hackathon-style sessions and structured mentor-guided on-the-job training, apprentices gain real-world experience at the intersection of law and technology.

ProjectTitle: International Rescue Committee in Oakland Optician Apprenticeship Program
ProjectAbstract: The California Opportunity Youth Apprenticeship (COVA) Planning Grant will formalize a partnership between the International Rescue Committee (IRC) in Oakland and California State Society for Opticians' (CSSO) to expand access to Optician Apprenticeship Program's Registered Apprenticeship Programs (RAP) for opportunity youth.

ProjectTitle: WellSpace Institute's Medical Assistant Training Program
ProjectAbstract: WellSpace Health will use COVA-AP Planning Grant funds to develop a trauma-informed, earn-and-learn Medical Assistant (MA) Registered Apprenticeship Program tailored to the unique needs of opportunity youth ages 18-24 in Sacramento County. The program will include classroom instruction, paid on-the-job training, and wraparound support services to reduce barriers and improve long-term employment outcomes. Youth will gain the technical, professional, and life skills needed to earn California MA certification and launch sustainable careers in healthcare.

Climb Hire's TechPath Apprenticeship Program will create a strong apprenticeship pathway in IT Support, with plans to expand into Network+ and Cybersecurity apprenticeships. This model integrates project?based industry training, offering participants valuable hands-on experience while pairing them with industry mentors for ongoing, real-world guidance. The goal is to establish a structured apprenticeship program that equips participants with the skills needed to transition into full-time, family-sustaining positions.

ProjectTitle: YouthBuild Charter School of California Pipeline to Advanced Manufacturing
ProjectAbstract: Youth Build Charter School of California (YCSC), a CTE high school, is partnering with Technical Employment Training (TET), Walker Manufacturing Group, and the CNC Career Network to develop an Advanced Manufacturing career pathway for opportunity youth in San Bernardino and Riverside Counties. This two-phase initiative will establish a DAS-registered apprenticeship with TET in Year 1 followed by a linked Pre-Apprenticeship at YCSC. Walker Manufacturing Group will serve as the hiring employer. The CNC Career Network will provide marketing, training tours, and structured interview access.

ProjectTitle: Pathway to Careers: Building the Future of Healthcare and Advanced Manufacturing Registered Apprenticeship Programs
ProjectAbstract: This proposal, "Pathway to Careers: Building the Future of Healthcare and Advanced Manufacturing Registered Apprenticeship Programs," outlines a strategic planning initiative to develop equitable Registered Apprenticeship Programs (RAPs) in two high-demand sectors: Advanced Manufacturing and Healthcare. Target occupations include Automotive and Mechatronics Technicians, along with Promotores de Salud, Community Health Workers, and Health Navigators that are responsive to regional labor market needs and crucial to California's economic and public health infrastructure.

ProjectTitle: What Opportunity Youth NECESITA (Network Engineering, Cybersecurity, Education Software, and IT Apprenticeship): Pathways to Tech, Purpose, and Prosperity
RecipientName: Los Angeles County Office of Education
ProjectAbstract: The Los Angeles County Office of Education (LACOE) Technology Services (TS) is launching the Network Engineering, Cybersecurity, Education Software, and Information Technology Apprenticeship (NECESITA) program to address urgent workforce needs in critical technology fields. Rooted in the Spanish word "necesita," meaning "need," this program reflects the collaborative spirit and mutual support essential to innovation within TS.

ProjectTitle: Innovators in Automation & Advanced Manufacturing : Apprenticeship Planning in Automation Technician Programming for Youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder and Other Opportunity Youth Groups
ProjectAbstract: The project aims to establish a robust, cutting-edge career pathway in advanced manufacturing for opportunity youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder and opportunity youth from other groups historically cut-off from educational and employment opportunities to address persistent shortages in skilled workforce in U.S. industry.

ProjectTitle: CHW Advance: A Pilot Apprenticeship Pathway for Opportunity Youth
ProjectAbstract: Reach Out proposes "CHW Advance," a one-year planning and pilot initiative to design an innovative apprenticeship approach that gives employers the community-rooted talent they need-and gives Opportunity Youth the living-wage career pathway they deserve. Focused on Community Health Worker training for youth ages 16-24 in San Bernardino and Riverside Counties, the project will develop three advanced training tracks-Behavioral Health, Alcohol & Substance Use, and Violence Interruption-paired with paid work experience.

ProjectTitle: Apprenticeship Program for Opportunity Youth in East Oakland
ProjectAbstract: Youth Beat, an Oakland-based nonprofit, seeks funding through the COYA Apprenticeship Planning Grant to design and develop a Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) focused on multimedia production and creative economy careers. Building on over a decade of experience in youth media training and current work with the Oakland Unified School District (OUSD) on a pre-apprenticeship pathway, this new initiative will provide a structured, equitable career ladder for opportunity youth in the East Bay.

ProjectTitle: San Diego Opportunity Youth Nursing Assistant Apprenticeship
RecipientName: San Diego County Office of Education
ProjectAbstract: The San Diego County Office of Education (SDCOE), in partnership with Procareer Academy (Procareer), proposes to develop a Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) pathway for opportunity youth in the San Diego region. This Apprenticeship Planning Grant (COYA-AP) will address the critical need for skilled healthcare workers, specifically Certified Nursing Assistants (CNAs), while creating a sustainable career pathway for opportunity youth.

ProjectTitle: Grow Our Own: Opportunity Youth Apprenticeship Pipeline for California's Future Educators
ProjectAbstract: We are proposing the development of a comprehensive, stackable teacher apprenticeship pathway for opportunity youth ages 16-24 in rural Central California. Led by the Tulare County Office of Education  (TCOE), in partnership with Hanford Joint Unified High School District and regional educational partners, this effort addresses the dual challenge of workforce barriers facing local youth and the growing teacher shortage across public schools-especially in special education and single subject areas.

ProjectTitle: iFoster PSS and CHW Planning Grant for Foster Youth
ProjectAbstract: The iFoster AmeriCorps Jobs Program is a comprehensive, evidence-based model designed to support system-involved youth through training, wraparound services, and hands-on work experience. This model not only builds job readiness but also ensures youth are positioned for long-term success in professional careers. The COVA planning grant will enable iFoster to expand upon this model, formally developing Registered Apprenticeship Programs (RAPs) for both Peer Support Specialists (PSS) and Community Health Workers (CHW).

RecipientName: Glenn County Office of Educ. - Willows, CA
ProjectAbstract: This proposal seeks to establish a competency-based paraprofessional apprenticeship program tailored for opportunity youth in Glenn County. Spearheaded by the Glenn County Office of Education, the initiative will align with the Education, Child Development, and Family Services CTE pathways and integrate on-the-job training alongside related and supplemental instruction. Comprehensive wraparound services will support participants, and the program will articulate with California State University, Chico's credentialing pathway to create a seamless pipeline into the education workforce.

Hollywood CPR prepares individuals for trade and specialty crafts "behind the scenes" union jobs in the high-paying entertainment industry, with a focus on populations historically excluded from these opportunities.

ProjectTitle: Empowering Futures: Pharmacy Technician Apprenticeships for Opportunity Youth
ProjectAbstract: This Apprenticeship Planning grant seeks to establish a comprehensive Pharmacy Technician Registered Apprenticeship Program for opportunity youth facing barriers to employment, education, and economic mobility. By offering a structured pathway to high-quality, industry-recognized training in pharmacy technology, this apprenticeship will open doors to competitive career opportunities within the growing healthcare sector.

San Diego Theatrical Training Corporation (SDTTC) will develop a new, DAS Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP), which will provide overburdened and opportunity youth in San Diego County, ages 18-24, with comprehensive training, educational services and supportive services for the occupation of Stage Technician.

ProjectTitle: AmityWorks Substance Use Counselor Apprenticeship Project
ProjectAbstract: AmityWorks is proud to launch a Substance Use Counselor Apprenticeship Program in partnership with East Los Angeles College (ELAC) Foundation, Cuesta College, and New Ways to Work, LLC. This innovative 18-month apprenticeship program creates a clear and supported pathway into careers in behavioral health, particularly for individuals with lived experience in reentry and recovery while providing support services and case management to those enrolled in the apprenticeship program.

ProjectTitle: STRIVE Learn & Earn: Culturally Responsive Apprenticeships for Opportunity Youth
ProjectAbstract: Strive Community Health Institute (Strive) seeks funding through the COVA-Al grant to implement and expand its DAS-registered apprenticeship programs in healthcare and human services. The proposed project will serve 100 opportunity youth ages 16-24 across California, placing them in culturally responsive earn-and-learn pathways that lead to careers as Case Workers, Resource Coordinators, and Doula Healthcare Specialists.

ProjectTitle: Elevate & Empower: Advancing Opportunities for Youth through Apprenticeship
RecipientName: Hawkeye Properties and Workforce Innovation, Inc.
ProjectAbstract: Crafting Culinary Careers Through Registered Apprenticeship Programs is designed to place Opportunity Youth in Los Angeles County on a clear and sustainable career path as Line Cooks or Baristas/Latte Artists. With the hospitality industry rapidly expanding to meet the demands of annual tourism and global events like the 2026 World Cup, 2027 Super Bowl, and 2028 Summer Olympics, there is a growing need for a highly skilled workforce-this program helps meet that need.

ProjectTitle: Woodcraft Rangers Apprenticeship Pathways (WRAP). Together Rising Los Angeles - Expanding Access to Early Childhood Careers
ProjectAbstract: Woodcraft Rangers Apprenticeship Pathways (WRAP): Together Rising Los Angeles (TRLA)- Expanding Access to Early Childhood Careers will deepen opportunity youth participation in the TRLA Registered Apprenticeship Program through targeted outreach, culturally grounded mentorship, and wraparound wellness services. The initiative includes Future Rising, a career exposure and readiness pipeline for high school students (ages 16-18), leading to dual enrollment, summer training, and eventual TRLA enrollment.

As a 501 (c)(3) non-profit organization with a proven track record of creating career pathways in the television and film industries for opportunity youth though workforce development programs, Handy Foundation will expand supportive services and improve implementation of its DAS Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) for this population.

ProjectTitle: Crafting Culinary Careers Through Registered Apprenticeship Programs
RecipientName: Hospitality Industry Training and Education Fund, dba Hospitality Training Academy
ProjectAbstract: The Hospitality Training Academy's (HTA) program, "Crafting Culinary Careers Through Registered Apprenticeship Programs," aims to place Opportunity Youth in Los Angeles County on a strong career path as Line Cooks or Baristas/Latte Artists within the thriving local hospitality industry. Through HTA's Registered Apprenticeship Programs, 75 Opportunity Youth will receive comprehensive training, beginning with an intensive eight-week classroom component led by experienced culinary instructors in a professional kitchen and lab setting.

Better Youth's Registered Apprenticeship Program (RAP) is a state and federally approved workforce development apprenticeship program designed to provide foster and system-impacted youth with structured, paid career pathways in the creative economy. Through industry-aligned training tracks in media production, animation, gaming, and project management, apprentices receive up to 2,000 hours of on-the-job training (OJT), 150+ hours of Related Supplemental Instruction (RSI), and individualized wraparound support.

ProjectTitle: Western Riverside County Multiple Species Habitat Conservation Plan/Natural Communities Conservation Plan (G2598082)
RecipientName: Western Riverside County Regional Conservation Authority (RCA)
ProjectAbstract: This funding will result in permanent protection of conservation lands totaling 958.55 acres that will complement the Western Riverside Multiple Species Habitat Conservation Plan/Natural Communities Conservation Plan reserve in western Riverside County, California. The purpose of the land acquisition proposal is to acquire and permanently conserve ecologically significant lands and a regional movement corridor to other conserved lands for federally endangered, federally threatened, and at-risk species.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Statewide grant opportunity for conservation land acquisition to help meet 30x30 goals.

ProjectTitle: Los Robles Ranch Conservation Easement Project (G2598070)
RecipientName: Land Trust for Santa Barbara County
ProjectAbstract: The Los Robles Ranch Conservation Easement Project seeks to conserve three parcels to advance recovery of the Santa Barbara County Distinct Population Segment of the California tiger salamander (Ambystoma californiense; Federally endangered and State threatened). The Project abuts previously conserved lands located within designated Critical Habitat for the Santa Barbara County DPS of the California tiger salamander, and the lands proposed for acquisition comprise a vital piece of a larger wildlife-movement corridor.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Statewide grant opportunity for conservation land acquisition to help meet 30x30 goals.

ProjectTitle: Coachella Valley Multiple Species Habitat Conservation Plan/Natural Communities Conservation Plan (G2598078)
ProjectAbstract: The purpose of the proposed land acquisition is to acquire, permanently protect, and manage highly developable but essential habitat that supports two federally listed covered species and is immediately adjacent to five conservation areas identified in the Coachella Valley Multiple Species Habitat Conservation Plan/Natural Community Conservation Plan. These species include the federally endangered Coachella Valley milk-vetch (Astragalus lentiginosus var. coachellae) and federally threatened Coachella Valley fringe-toed lizard (Uma inornata).
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Statewide grant opportunity for conservation land acquisition to help meet 30x30 goals.

ProjectTitle: Santa Cruz Long-Toed Salamander Conservation and Public Assistance Project (G2598081)
RecipientName: Land Trust of Santa Cruz County (LTSCC)
ProjectAbstract: This project will reduce persistent threats and conflicts between conservation of the Federal and State endangered Santa Cruz long-toed salamander and the federally threatened California red-legged frog resulting from competing land uses on properties associated with the Tucker Pond Habitat Conservation Plan (HCP) and the Seascape Uplands HCP. The conservation goal would be achieved by permanently protecting habitat for these species. The secondary purpose is to assist private landowners with regulatory burdens due to presence of the Santa Cruz long-toed salamander on their property.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Statewide grant opportunity for conservation land acquisition to help meet 30x30 goals.

ProjectTitle: East Contra Costa County HCP/NCCP Land Acquisition (G2598080)
RecipientName: East Contra Costa County Habitat Conservancy
ProjectAbstract: Funding will support the purchase of 866.66? acres of important habitat lands in eastern Contra Costa County for the East Contra Costa County Habitat Conservancy Plan and Natural Community Conservation Plan (HCP/NCCP) Preserve System to benefit six federally-listed or at-risk species. The acquisition will further the conservation goals of the HCP/NCCP, completing a linkage between conserved land in the area and protecting habitat and natural communities, including oak woodland, annual grassland, oak savanna, chaparral, alkali grassland, rock outcrop, creek, pond, and wetland habitats.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Statewide grant opportunity for conservation land acquisition to help meet 30x30 goals.

ProjectTitle: Salinas River Operations Habitat Conservation Plan
ProjectAbstract: The Salinas River Operations Habitat Conservation Plan (HCP) project seeks additional funding to finish development and obtain Endangered Species Act incidental take permits for Monterey County Water Resources Agency covered activities. The HCP will cover federal and state listed terrestrial and aquatic species that may be impacted by the covered activities. Impacts may include direct incidental take of individuals or degradation of habitats. Development of the HCP will include species specific conservation measures intended to offset the impacts and minimize incidental take.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Statewide grant opportunity for conservation land acquisition.

ProjectAbstract: Funding will support continuation of the planning phase of the Sonoma County HCP/NCCP in northern California. The Sonoma County HCP/NCCP is a multi-species and multi-phased joint Habitat Conservation Plan (HCP) and Natural Community Conservation Plan (NCCP) compliant with the Federal Endangered Species Act and the California Natural Community Conservation Planning Act (NCCP Act) of 2002 (as amended) to address and mitigate potential impacts to threatened and endangered species associated with growth and development in the County.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Statewide grant opportunity for conservation land acquisition.

ProjectTitle: Completion of Sweetwater Authority Natural Community Conservation Plan (NCCP)/Habitat Conservation Plan (HCP) and CEQA / NEPA Processes
ProjectAbstract: Sweetwater Authority (SWA) has initiated and is currently preparing an Administrative Draft combined state Natural Community Conservation Plan (NCCP) and federal Habitat Conservation Plan (HCP) to programmatically permit its 70 operations and maintenance  activities and certain new or expanded facilities. Finalization of the SWA NCCP/HCP will streamline regulatory approvals, remove uncertainties that can occur when activities are permitted on a case-by-case basis and provide for the long-term conservation and management of covered species within the Plan Area.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Statewide grant opportunity for conservation land acquisition.

ProjectAbstract: The City of Livermore is located in the eastern San Francisco Bay Area where open space, working lands, and urban development intersect. This area supports habitats for several listed and at-risk plant and wildlife species. To address these unique habitats, the City is developing the Livermore Habitat Conservation Plan, which will streamline compliance with the federal Endangered Species Act for operation, maintenance and development of public facilities while conserving habitat and protecting species such as the California tiger salamander, California red-legged frog, and monarch butterfly.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Statewide grant opportunity for conservation land acquisition.

ProjectTitle: Comprehensive Management Plan and Environmental Documents for the Stephens' Kangaroo Rat Habitat Conservation Plan Amendment/Renewal
ProjectAbstract: The Riverside County Habitat Conservation Agency  seeks funding for the planning, development, and completion of a Comprehensive Management Plan and the development and completion of required environmental CEQA and NEPA  documents to support the amendment/renewal of the Habitat Conservation Plan for Stephens' Kangaroo Rat in Western Riverside County (SKR HCP). The SKR HCP was permitted in 1996 and has had a foundational role in the conservation and improved status of the recently downlisted federally threatened Stephens' kangaroo rat (Dipodomys stephensi) (USFWS 2022).
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Statewide grant opportunity for conservation land acquisition.

ProjectTitle: Humboldt Natural and Working Lands Carbon Stock and Management Study
ProjectAbstract: The development of a Carbon Stock Inventory and Carbon Sequestration Feasibility Study to develop a better understanding of the existing and future carbon sequestration capacity in Humboldt County. This effort will create the initial understanding of carbon sequestration as a resource for the region so that future efforts can be developed and made to use carbon sequestration as an effective strategy to climate resilience.  The studies will also inform the Humboldt Regional Climate Action Plan 2030 update to achieve carbon neutrality by 2045.

ProjectTitle: AFL-CIO - Monterey Bay Central Labor Council

ProjectAbstract: The Monterey Bay Central Labor Council (MBCLC), representing more than 80 affiliated unions and 37,000 members in Monterey and Santa Cruz counties, advances economic and social justice for working families. Through worker organizing, political advocacy, community partnerships, education, and training, MBCLC promotes workplace equity and empowers workers to protect their rights. By uniting labor and community organizations, MBCLC strengthens worker voices and expands opportunities for fair, inclusive, and sustainable economic growth.

Through experienced, trained canvassers, the organization delivers culturally competent messaging and empowers workers to understand and defend their rights. With deep knowledge of rural communities and an expanded staff, FMTK CLC is well-positioned to provide effective, community-based outreach and support.

ProjectTitle: Central Labor Council of San Bernardino and Riverside Counties - Inland Empire Labor Council
RecipientName: Central Labor Council of San Bernardino and Riverside Counties - Inland Empire Labor Council
ProjectAbstract: The Inland Empire Labor Council AFL-CIO represents local unions from every sector of the labor movement in Riverside and San Bernardino Counties. The Labor Council and our affiliated unions work to build worker power through union organizing, political education, economic development and training programs to give workers a voice to improve their lives.

The Los Angeles Black Worker Center (LABWC) advances economic justice by advocating for and supporting Black workers in protecting their workplace rights. Through education, organizing, and community engagement, LABWC addresses systemic racism and barriers to quality employment, fair wages, and safe working conditions. By empowering workers and promoting long-term systemic change, LABWC helps build pathways to economic opportunity, dignity, and workplace equity for Black communities.

Central Valley Empowerment Alliance (CVEA) serves farmworkers in rural communities across Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare, and Kern counties. Through trusted multilingual staff and community leaders, CVEA provides culturally responsive outreach in Spanish, Ilocano, Tagalog, English, and Indigenous languages. Using texting, phone banking, surveys, and community-led research, CVEA identifies local needs and shapes its programs. Its education-focused, community-driven approach empowers residents and improves access to critical services and resources.

SoCal COSH educates, advocates, and mobilizes for safe, healthy workplaces, focusing on underserved, low-income, migrant, and limited-English-proficient workers across Southern California. Through culturally responsive outreach, bilingual staff, and interpretation services, it delivers worker education in participants' preferred languages. ProjectTitle: Population Trend, Habitat Quality, and Resiliency to Environmental Change in a Large Population of Golden Eagle Overlapping the Altamont Pass Wind Resource Area, California
RecipientName: U.S. Geological Survey Forest & Rangeland Ecosystem Science Center
ProjectAbstract: The Project objectives are to: 1. Maintain demographic population monitoring of golden eagles in and around the Altamont Pass Wind Resource Area; 2. Quantify long-term population trend and responses to wind energy production with respect to: a) site-occupancy, reproductive rate and age-class of territorial pairs and b) abundance of territorial pairs and non-territorial subadults (eagles less than four years old); and 3. Leverage long-term demographic surveys to develop spatial layers of habitat quality.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The Project will be conducted within the Golden Eagle Demographic Study Area on approximately 5,170 square kilometers of privately-owned and publicly-owned land located within the Altamont Pass Wind Resource Area (historical and current footprint) and six counties (Contra Costa, Alameda, Santa Clara, Merced, Stanislaus and San Joaquin).
CountiesServed: Alameda; Contra Costa; Merced; San Joaquin; Santa Clara; Stanislaus

ProjectTitle: Conserving Golden Eagles in the Face of Wind Energy Generation
ProjectAbstract: The Project will perform visual-scan surveys to determine whether the golden eagle population has continued to decline since 2019, and measure crippling bias to assess impacts within the Altamont Pass Wind Resource Area. The Project will perform validation tests of turbine micro-siting recommendations; update collision hazard models; analyze APWRA vs. Diablo Range eagle use patterns to measure before and after use of a large wildfire; measure response to human altered environments to predict impacts to eagle populations; and identify communal roosts for strategic acquisition or protection.

ProjectTitle: Demography and Movement of Golden Eagles at Altamont and Tehachapi
ProjectAbstract: The Project will provide key demographic data and modeling for golden eagles at the Altamont Pass Wind Resource Area and Tehachapi Wind Resource Area and expand efforts to link flight behavior of eagles to their risk of colliding with wind turbines. The Project will develop a subsampling strategy of eagle feathers; collect additional feathers at nests; complete DNA analysis of feathers; and complete demographic analysis of eagles. The Project will also link eagle flight behavior to risk of colliding with turbines.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Altamont Pass Wind Resource Area is within Alameda and Contra Costa counties. Tehachapi Wind Resource Area is within Kern County.

Nonprofits throughout the State work independently through their local chapters and/or affiliates to provide disaster training and resources to diverse populations disproportionately impacted by emergencies. This work is intended to increase their communities’ disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and mitigation capabilities.

ProjectTitle: Listos California CERT Support Grant (LC) Program
ProjectAbstract: To provide funding to a fiscal administrator which will in coordination with Cal OES, support new and existing CERT programs to build their capacity to prepare vulnerable and underserved populations including, but not limited to: providing CERT training in languages other than English, providing CERT training to underserved populations and/or populations that are at high risk for disasters, providing accommodations for training participants that have access and functional needs, such as English as a Second Language (ESL) interpretation, and building capacity to respond to disasters.

ProjectTitle: ANNA Bus Rapid Transit and Community Connection Nodes Planning Project
ProjectAbstract: The Anaheim Transportation Network (ATN) will use grant funding to 1) develop a Community Outreach Plan and 2) prepare 20% Engineering Design Plans for the Advancing Neighborhood Networks for All (ANNA) Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) and Community Connection Nodes project. The project is needed to address traffic congestion, growing population and developments, and increases in visitors in the City of Anaheim; and will provide an easily accessible and efficient transit option.

ProjectTitle: Move OC: A Vibrant Path to Active Transportation
ProjectAbstract: A countywide active transportation plan will be developed which focuses on mode share, safety and comfort, bicycle and pedestrian network improvement, and transportation equity. The Plan will include infrastructure, programmatic, policy, and funding recommendations based on goals, metrics, and comprehensive infrastructure and non-infrastructure inventories. A multi-phase public outreach to achieve the vision where residents of all ages, abilities, and income levels can easily choose safe non-motorized transportation as their primary mode for trips within the county.

ProjectTitle: Heart of El Centro Community Connectivity and Revitalization Project
ProjectAbstract: The Heart of El Centro Revitalization and Connection project will create a master plan for the city's Main Street Corridor, covering Downtown El Centro and the Civic Center areas, spanning 120 acres. Specifically, the project aims to revitalize these key urban areas by improving mobility, enhancing public spaces, and identifying mixed-use development zones to reduce reliance on automobiles and accommodate the growing demand for housing, transportation, and workforce development related to the region’s expanding lithium extraction industry.

ProjectTitle: Rural Corridors Study: Improving Transportation Infrastructure on or near Tribal Lands
ProjectAbstract: SANDAG will conduct a corridor study of the eastern segments of SR-76, SR-79, I-8, and SR-94 with a focus on projects that are regional in nature and priorities for the reservations along those corridors: Pala, Pauma, Rincon and La Jolla reservations along SR 76; Santa Ysabel Reservation along SR 79; and La Posta, Manzanita and Campo reservations along SR 94 and I 8. The Study will include an existing conditions report, prioritized transportation solutions, a feasibility assessment, and an action plan for future funding.

ProjectTitle: Campus Drive Complete Streets and Safety Study
ProjectAbstract: The Project is located along Campus Drive, between University Drive and Turtle Rock Drive. It was identified as a hot spot and key corridor for improvements in the City’s Local Roadway Safety Plan (LRSP). The Study will review applicable local/state/federal standards, collect data, analyze the corridor and its intersections for pedestrian and bicycle enhancements, develop design alternatives, and select the preferred alternative.

The City of Oceanside will develop an Active Transportation Plan to improve access, safety, and connectivity to schools, parks, and other community destinations. The AT Plan will build on years of engagement, data collection, and feasibility analysis conducted for the 2008 Bicycle Master Plan, 2020 Oceanside Safe Routes to School Plan, and recent General Plan update. The AT Plan will result in a list of prioritized infrastructure projects and complementary policies and programs that will help create a healthier, safer, and more connected Oceanside.

The City of San Diego will develop a comprehensive, data-driven, and community-led framework for enhancing Balboa Park's mobility options and addressing access needs. The study will build on the City’s Pedestrian Master Plan, Parking Demand Management Study and ongoing Trails Master Plan, Mobility Master Plan, Bike Master Plan, Park Needs Index, and Balboa Park Prioritization Framework; and integrate archival records, travel data, and community input to identify mobility constraints and propose solutions to long-standing accessibility barriers caused by car-centric planning.

ProjectTitle: Gateway of the Americas Freight Optimization Plan
RecipientName: Imperial County Department of Public Works
ProjectAbstract: Project funding will support the development of a freight optimization plant to determine critical capital improvements based on existing and planned land use to maximize commercial freight and passenger vehicle circulation and reduce greenhouse gas emissions and other harmful environmental determinants of health caused by traffic congestion and vehicle idling accessing the Calexico East POE; advancing the statewide priorities outlined in the CFMP 2023, CAPTI, and Climate Adaption Strategy and SCAG's Regional 2024-2050 RTP/SCS.

ProjectTitle: Planning for First and Last Mile Transportation Solutions in Unincorporated San Diego County Villages
ProjectAbstract: The project will create a FM/LM Transportation Services Evaluation and Implementation Plan to determine the feasibility of FM/LM services in unincorporated SD Co and develop an implementation strategy. The Plan will evaluate transportation service needs, service areas, costs, and funding to address gaps in transportation connectivity and access to essential services for residents with limited transit options, high transportation costs, and mobility barriers, while also reducing VMT, lowering GHG emissions, and enhancing equitable and sustainable transportation solutions.

ProjectTitle: San Diego Regional Last-Mile Freight Delivery Plan
ProjectAbstract: The San Diego Regional Last-Mile Freight Delivery Plan will address these issues by developing a proposal for a Regional Last-Mile Freight Delivery Program supported by analysis of potential funding sources, such as a regionwide delivery fee, and a path to implementation that navigates legal obstacles. The Project will advance recommendations and actions identified in SANDAG’s 2021 Regional Plan, CTP 2050, CFMP 2023, CSFAP, CAPTI, San Diego and Imperial Counties Sustainable Freight Implementation Strategy, and SANDAG Concept of Operations for Curb Access Management.

ProjectTitle: Otay Mesa East Transit Planning Study
ProjectAbstract: Through robust, extensive outreach efforts, MTS will engage with the Otay Mesa community to gather input and ensure that local needs are prioritized. A comprehensive transit study will then assess current transit services and identify opportunities for improvements tailored to the area's unique requirements. The resulting recommendations will inform adjustments to the transit network, promoting equitable access and improved mobility for the community.

ProjectTitle: San Diego Regional Freight Resilience Plan
ProjectAbstract: SANDAG, in partnership with The Port of San Diego will produce a San Diego Freight Resilience Plan, and replicable approach for other jurisdictions, that will assess the region’s resiliency capabilities, assets, and challenges pertaining to our multimodal freight network and adjacent critical infrastructure. The Plan will strategize efforts that will enhance our regional capacity to mitigate, prepare for, respond to, and recover from catastrophic natural or manmade disasters.

ProjectTitle: Merced County Travel Demand Model Update
ProjectAbstract: MCAG will collaborate with The Transit Joint Powers Authority for Merced County to enhance its travel demand forecasting model by integrating post-pandemic on-demand data, developing a mode choice module including a transit component, and refining the assessment of performance indicators such as VMT and GHG emissions.

The Calaveras Council of Governments TDM Update will modernize transportation planning tools to analyze traffic patterns, VMT, and multimodal impacts in Calaveras County. The Project will update the TDM with detailed land use data, new trip generation rates, seasonal and weekend scenarios, and recalibration for improved accuracy. Recommended by the 2022 CCOG SB 743 Implementation Plan, it supports regional and state planning efforts, including CCOG’s RTP and the Climate Action Plan for Transportation Infrastructure (CAPTI).

ProjectTitle: Town of Mammoth Lakes Climate Adaptation Plan
ProjectAbstract: The Town of Mammoth Lakes is requesting funding to work with a consultant to prepare a Climate Adaptation Plan. The Climate Adaptation Plan will help the Town address climate vulnerabilities, and plan for adding resilience to our transportation and other infrastructure. This plan will tie into existing work that has already been completed on the General Plan Safety Element, LHMP and Community Wildlife Protection Plan. The Climate Adaptation Plan will also help the Town meet the State’s  greenhouse gas (GHG) and vehicle miles traveled (VMT) reduction targets.
Gather information from Tribal community on existing conditions and improvements to incorporate into a 2.5 year project, resulting in a Sustainable Transportation Plan

ProjectTitle: Downtown Modesto Multimodal Transportation Network and Land Use Compatibility Action Plan
ProjectAbstract: The City of Modesto will lead, the preparation of the Downtown Modesto Multimodal Transportation Network and Land Use Compatibility Action Plan. The Plan will build on the efforts of SJRRC’s Valley Rail Project to seamlessly integrate the future rail network and its operations with the new ACE commuter rail station beginning in 2026.

ProjectTitle: Cesar Chavez Street Corridor Transformation Plan
ProjectAbstract: The City of Coachella proposes the Cesar Chavez Street Corridor Transformation Plan to address critical transportation and land use challenges along the city’s most significant north-south corridor. This project will create a comprehensive transformation plan that prioritizes safety, expands multimodal access, and fosters sustainable land use along the corridor.

ProjectTitle: Inyo County Evacuation Route Resilience Plan
ProjectAbstract: The Inyo County Local Transportation Commission will hire a consultant to prepare an Evacuation Route Resilience Plan to improve safety for rural communities by making critical ingress/egress routes more resilient to present and future climate change impacts. The Plan will identify and catalog evacuation routes for Inyo County communities and develop a Capital Improvement Plan for Climate Adaptation that provides a prioritized list of necessary infrastructure improvements over a five-year implementation period.

The City of Culver City will develop an expanded, more detailed, and more robust Implementation Procedures as a needed revision to the City’s first Complete Streets Guidelines. The Project includes a robust public and stakeholder engagement process, an inventory of available ROW for Complete Streets project construction, an updated Complete Streets implementation process, a revised Reconciliation Process, new Dedication Requirements, and a prioritized project list and 5-year plan for implementation.

ProjectTitle: Coachella Valley Multimodal Corridor Plan (CV MCP)
ProjectAbstract: The Coachella Valley Multimodal Corridor Plan addresses the region’s transportation challenges by enhancing non-motorized mobility options and focusing on equitable travel solutions across three critical freeway corridors within the Transportation Uniform Mitigation Fee (TUMF) zone that hinder local roadway connectivity: Interstate 10 (I-10), the region’s primary east-west route; State Route 62 (SR-62), connecting Desert Hot Springs and northern communities; and State Route 86 (SR-86), linking Indio and Coachella to rural areas in the southern valley.

ProjectTitle: 360 Degree Look at Senate Bill 960 for San Bernardino County: Implementation Plan (Short title: 360° for SB 960)
ProjectAbstract: The 360 Degree Look at Senate Bill (SB) 960 for San Bernardino County: Implementation Plan (360° for SB960) will take a grassroots 360° (from all angles) approach to identifying targets and performance measures for complete street assets in San Bernardino County along the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) state highway system as required by SB 960.

ProjectTitle: Charging Forward: Bell Gardens Zero-Emissions Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Plan
ProjectAbstract: The City of Bell Gardens will develop a Zero-Emissions Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Plan to address the deficiency of citywide charging infrastructure, with a focus on equitable access for under-resourced communities. The plan will analyze existing land use, zoning, and transportation patterns while aligning with the city’s Environmental Justice (EJ) element, forthcoming Climate Action Plan (CAP), and California's greenhouse gas (GHG) reduction goals.

ProjectTitle: Montebello Mobility Hub Connectivity Feasibility Study
ProjectAbstract: The Montebello Mobility Hub Connectivity Feasibility Study is an innovative initiative designed to explore the potential of establishing a Mobility Hub that enhances connectivity, accessibility, and sustainability across the city's primary commercial corridors: Washington Boulevard, Whittier Boulevard, Montebello Boulevard, and Beverly Boulevard.

ProjectTitle: Ventura County Multimodal Transportation Network Climate Vulnerability Assessment & Action Plan
ProjectAbstract: To address climate-related infrastructure challenges facing Ventura County, the Project will produce: (1) Countywide Multimodal Vulnerability Assessment; (2) Outreach Plan; (3) Climate Adaptation Strategy and Funding Plan; (4) Adaptation Assessment and Action Plan; and (5) a Transportation Emergency Preparedness Guide for Individual & Families.

SCRRA, operator of Metrolink regional rail, will work with local cities/counties, riders, stakeholders, priority populations, and connecting transit operators to develop a Signage and Wayfinding Master Plan for clear, accessible, and inclusive signage at 67 Metrolink stations in six counties to increase ridership, and promote equitable, accessible, affordable non-auto mobility options.
CountiesServed: Los Angeles; Orange; Riverside; San Bernardino; San Diego; Ventura

ProjectTitle: Pico Rivera's Urban Renaissance: A Vision for a Multimodal, Climate Adaptive, and Economically Vibrant Future For All - General Plan Element Update (PR-UR)
ProjectAbstract: Pico Rivera's Urban Renaissance: A Vision for a Multimodal, Climate Adaptive, and Economically Vibrant Future For All - General Plan Element Update aims to close critical gaps in mobility, housing, and equity by comprehensively updating the Mobility/Circulation, Land Use, and EJ Elements of the General Plan. The City’s 2012 General Plan Circulation Element is outdated and does not account for the high-quality transit network and rail stations being introduced, including a new Metro E-Line station, a LOSSAN commuter rail station, and enhanced first/last mile connections.

The Arcadia Active Transportation Plan will seek to further regional and local sustainability through an improved active transportation network that will include bike/ped improvements along primary travel corridors with connectivity to major activity centers. The AATP will alleviate the safety and environmental hazards by establishing priority transportation needs to identify feasible options to implement complete streets, TOD, and first-last mile improvements and connections, provide seamless active transportation access and facilitate safe routes to schools safety features.

ProjectTitle: Rose Bowl Area & Brookside Park Multimodal Connectivity
ProjectAbstract: The Rose Bowl, along with the nearby Brookside Park, is a key regional event hub and an important venue for the 2028 Olympics; however, longstanding connectivity issues have made it difficult for residents of the city's disadvantaged communities to access these sites. The Rose Bowl Area & Brookside Park Multimodal Connectivity Project aims to solve these challenges by developing a Multimodal Transportation Plan that emphasizes safe, sustainable active transportation and transit connections to the Rose Bowl, Brookside Park, adjacent schools, and employment centers.

ProjectTitle: Manning Avenue Transformation Technical Study (MATTS) Project
ProjectAbstract: The City of Parlier's  Manning Avenue Transformation Technical Study is a planning effort to identify, prioritize, and implement equitable and sustainable transportation solutions that improve pedestrian safety, multimodal accessibility & connectivity, and overall quality of life for all residents. The project will analyze options such as reducing the corridor to a single lane in each direction, adding a Class 1 multi-use trail, implementing traffic circles at key intersections, and synchronizing traffic signals to enhance public safety, operation efficiency, and active transportation.

ProjectTitle: Evaluating the Feasibility and Impacts of Fare-Free Transit for Tulare County: Advancing Sustainable and Equitable Mobility Solutions
ProjectAbstract: This project seeks to evaluate the feasibility, implementation strategies, and impacts of a fare-free transit system across Tulare County's transit operators. Eliminating transit fares, if feasible, will encourage increased mode shift towards transit and lower the cost burdens of transportation on county residents. The project will assess the financial, operational, and environmental implications of eliminating fares.

ProjectTitle: Regional Climate Adaptation and Resilience Framework for Madera County
ProjectAbstract: MCTC will develop a comprehensive Regional Climate Adaptation and Resilience Framework that takes a regional approach to identifying and addressing the climate vulnerabilities of the county’s transportation system and its communities due to wildfires, flooding, drought, and extreme heat, using the best available climate science. This framework will guide Madera County’s long-term resilience to climate change, promoting safe, sustainable, and accessible transportation infrastructure.

Fresno County Rural Transit Agency (FCRTA) aims to transition to an all-electric vehicle fleet by 2030. FCRTA completed its groundbreaking Fresno County Microgrid & Multimodal Resiliency Hub Feasibility Study in 2024. FCRTA plans to conduct Phase 2 of the Microgrid Study, focusing on creating partnerships with local Fresno County public schools and installing microgrids on school district properties.

ProjectTitle: City of Corcoran Trail Technical Study ?" Transit Station to Park
ProjectAbstract: Through the Trail Technical Study ?" Transit Station to Park Project, the City of Corcoran will develop a plan for a Class 1 multi-use trail along Otis Avenue, providing multimodal connectivity to the city's transit station, Amtrak train station, the dowtown district, Gateway Park, and housing all located along Otis Avenue. This project addresses critical safety and accessibility challenges for pedestrians, cyclists, and disabled travelers in Corcoran's disadvantaged community (SB 535).

RecipientName: San Luis Obispo Council of Governments
ProjectAbstract: This project will rebrand and update the San Luis Obispo Council of Governments' twelve-year-old Park & Ride Lot Study, developing a plan to elevate existing park and ride facilities into a modern mobility hub network. The updated study will incorporate innovative alternative transportation options to facilitate mode shift and reduce VMT. Additionally, a comprehensive operations evaluation of the regional and connecting local transit system will inform recommendations for future service planning, enhancing transportation access between affordable housing and employment centers.

ProjectTitle: Fresno Metropolitan Light Rail Feasibility Study
ProjectAbstract: This project will be a case study for the feasibility of Light Rail Transit in the Fresno Metropolitan Area. The study will evaluate the economic, social, and environmental benefits for the Fresno area.  All options should be objectively assessed, including LRT, Streetcars, and other light rail options.  Ridership modeling will occur to determine feasibility of the LRT system, and the study will evaluate a phased implementation approach if it is demonstrated that a LRT system is viable from a ridership and operational cost perspective.

ProjectTitle: Santa Cruz METRO Bus Stop Master Plan
ProjectAbstract: The Santa Cruz METRO will implement a Bus Stop Master Plan to enhance accessibility, safety, and comfort across its bus network. This initiative will address the necessity for modernized infrastructure to better serve customers, including those with disabilities, and to comply with the ADA.

ProjectTitle: Santa Ynez Valley Active Transportation Regional Connector Planning
RecipientName: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians
ProjectAbstract: The proposed planning work will help to accomplish a variety of planning efforts leading up to completion of 30% design of a selected alternative for what will ultimately become a 10-mile-long multi-use path. The future path will provide the Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians (SYBCI) with long-needed safe access to local schools, grocery stores, medical facilities, employment opportunities, and other vital destinations, while filling critical gaps in the Santa Ynez Valley’s (SYV) active transportation network and adapting the region to expanding bike-tourism.

ProjectTitle: Hwy 1 SLO North Coast Resiliency and Safety Plan
RecipientName: San Luis Obispo Council of Governments
ProjectAbstract: This project will conduct a comprehensive analysis of a 12-mile segment of the Pacific Coast Highway (Highway 1) between San Simeon and Cambria and applicable road segments in each community.  The study aims to develop actionable recommendations for future projects that improve the corridor's functionality, resilience, and overall benefit to surrounding communities.

RecipientName: Santa Barbara County Association of Governments
ProjectAbstract: The State Route 135 Comprehensive Corridor Study will have a wide scope, considering all road users and addressing safety, mobility, congestion, access management, and GHG emissions reduction. A consultant will be hired to prepare the corridor study, managed by SBCAG, with the major deliverable being a written document identifying the needs of the corridor and a list of projects and strategies to inform future regional transportation plan updates.

ProjectTitle: Connecting Capitola Village Active Transportation Plan
ProjectAbstract: The City of Capitola will develop its first Active Transportation Plan (ATP) to create a safe, accessible, and connected active transportation network that meets the needs of all community members, including underserved populations such as seniors, youth, and low-income residents. This project will identify gaps, barriers, and opportunities in Capitola’s bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure and emphasize modern, protected designs to improve safety and equity for all users.

The Nighttime Safety Enhancement Plan will improve the citywide street light system to increase nighttime traffic safety and prevent crashes for all road users. The Plan will assess the existing lighting conditions, propose minimum illumination levels in various development areas with a focus on high pedestrian and bicycle corridors, and establish maintenance programs, processes for handling new street light requests, and short- and long-term capital improvement alternatives.

ProjectTitle: 2026 Active Transportation Plan and Level of Traffic Stress Analysis
ProjectAbstract: The 2026 Monterey County Active Transportation Plan and Level of Traffic Stress Analysis will develop a comprehensive strategy to create walking, biking and non-motorized transportation options for vulnerable and underserved persons throughout the county. This Plan will include a Level of Traffic Stress analysis that will assess the experience of non-automotive road users and produce an interactive map highlighting existing bicycle and pedestrian network gaps to help TAMC and local jurisdictions focus on implementing the highest benefit projects on our transportation network.

ProjectTitle: MST Designing for Transit Guidelines and ADA Analysis Project
ProjectAbstract: The project will develop an updated Designing for Transit Guidelines document that outlines adequate bus stop placement, required dimensions for ADA-compliant bus stops and amenities, and minimum complete street dimensions for accommodating buses and other transit-supportive/priority treatments and an analysis that identifies non-ADA compliant bus stops and cost estimates for ADA upgrades.

ProjectTitle: City of Belmont Transportation Master Plan
ProjectAbstract: The City of Belmont proposes a Transportation Master Plan (TMP) that will guide the city in making multimodal transportation investments while accommodating growth in a way that maintains a high quality of life for Belmont residents, visitors, and commuters. A 5-year and 10-year Short Range Plan and a 20-year Long Range Plan phasing forecasts will be developed and evaluated to provide a tool to help Belmont plan for growth.

ProjectTitle: Transit Connectivity and Bus Stop Design Guidelines
ProjectAbstract: The Transit Connectivity and Bus Stop Design Guidelines will establish standards, policies, and strategies to improve County Connection bus stops. These guidelines aim to enhance multi modal access by improving pedestrian and bike connectivity for first/last mile connections, ensuring consistent and appropriate improvements across various land use contexts, streamlining the design process for quicker implementation, and improving bus speeds and service reliability.

ProjectTitle: Bay Point Enhanced Bicycle and Pedstrian Improvements Study
ProjectAbstract: The Bay Point Enhanced Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvements Study is a Contra Costa County-led effort that will evaluate the implementation of enhanced bicycle and pedestrian facilities, including Class IV bicycle facilities and green infrastructure, in Bay Point, specifically on: 1) McAvoy Road, 2) along Port Chicago Highway to Willow Pass Road, and 3) Willow Pass Road from the the Evora Road-westbound State Route 4 ramps intersection to the border with the City of Pittsburg.

ProjectTitle: Nevada City Active Transportation, Trails, and Complete Streets Master Plan
ProjectAbstract: The City intends to create a Master Plan document that will focus on active transportation improvements, ultimately guiding the creation of a comprehensive and interconnected bicycle and pedestrian system that serves users of all ages and abilities and that can guide development of an active transportation network of safe and walkable streets, bikeways, and connecting trails to prioritize active transportation for residents, visitors, and workers.

ProjectTitle: BART's Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Survey & Modeling
RecipientName: San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit District (BART)
ProjectAbstract: This Project is comprised of three interrelated components to assess the pandemic’s impact on transit ridership and the effects of TOD on communities throughout the region.  TOD Travel Behavior Survey  TOD Scenario Model Update  BART’s Mode Shift Planning Tool Update integrating new TOD travel behavior data, recent station surveys, and the pandemic's effect on ridership to determine future access needs with the future TODs and parking reductions.

ProjectTitle: West Sac Forward Transit Priority Plan
ProjectAbstract: The City of West Sacramento in partnership with SacRT, YoloTD, and Via, with support from SACOG will develop the "West Sac Forward Transit Priority Plan": an innovative sustainable public transit plan that will analyze existing systems targeting efficiency, effectiveness, and seamless integration of public bus, rail, rideshare, and planned rapid transit systems to better serve residents and local workforce through new policies, strategies, and recommended infrastructure improvements.

This grant will update the Placer-Sacramento Gateway Plan, a comprehensive multimodal corridor plan developed in 2020 in partnership with regional and local agencies. The objective of the Gateway Plan Update is to identify and fund projects designed to reduce congestion through performance improvements that balance transportation needs, community impacts, with environmental benefits along the highly traveled 40-mile Gateway Corridor that includes segments of I-80, Bus 80, and SR 65, as well as parallel local roadways, transit, and bikeways.

ProjectTitle: Yuba City Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Plan
ProjectAbstract: The City of Yuba City will develop the Yuba City Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure Plan. The City will to develop an EV infrastructure plan to strategically plan for public EV infrastructure and City-owned fleet upgrades, prioritizing safety, equity, and sustainability while mitigating climate change by reducing greenhouse gas emissions from combustion engines.

SACOG is developing our first toll lanes to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve transit reliability, and manage freeway congestion in our growing region. The CARTA Regional Toll Equity Study (Study) will fill this gap by reviewing toll equity best-practices, analyzing how toll lanes will impact travel for equity-priority communities, and providing a clear and actionable roadmap to deliver an equitable toll lane network in the Sacramento Region.
CountiesServed: El Dorado; Placer; Sacramento; Sutter; Yolo; Yuba

ProjectAbstract: The Wilton Area Roadway Resiliency Project entails the development of a Resilience Improvement Plan to enhance the ability of existing surface transportation assets to withstand flooding and wildfires associated with extreme climate events. Sacramento County Department of Transportation will work closely with Caltrans and multiple stakeholders to analyze climate impacts, understand community needs and concerns, identify and prioritize potential improvements, and prepare 30% design plans and estimates for improvements identified by the plan.

ProjectTitle: City of Davis Active Transportation Plan
ProjectAbstract: The City of Davis proposes to develop a city-wide Active Transportation Plan (Plan) with the goal to increase the active mode share trips by 5% by 2040 with the development of innovative and data-proven successful projects, programs and policies that will reduce vehicle miles traveled and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions (transportation accounts for 74% of GHG emissions in the City of Davis), improve access to transit stops, and enhance safety for all.

The City of South Lake Tahoe will prepare the Stateline Avenue Complete Streets Study to identify current multimodal mobility challenges and develop a set of proposed improvements to enhance safety, vehicle circulation, and active transportation connectivity along Stateline Avenue. The Study will recommend innovative and context-sensitive multimodal improvements, and provide the foundation for future implementation grant funding.

ProjectTitle: Lassen County Electric Vehicle Charging Master Plan
ProjectAbstract: The Lassen County Electric Vehicle Charging Master Plan will outline a path forward to install effective and equitable electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure throughout Lassen County by evaluating the physical and financial feasibility of expanding the charging network in the county and conducting a site analysis for EV charging locations. The Plan will include an evaluation of existing conditions, findings of stakeholder and public outreach, a feasibility and siting analysis, an infrastructure analysis, an economic analysis, and an implementation plan.

ProjectTitle: GoShasta Regional Active Transportation Plan Update (GoShasta Update)
ProjectAbstract: The GoShasta Regional Active Transportation Plan Update (GoShasta Update) will build on the success of the Original GoShasta Plan by prioritizing equitable, multimodal transportation investments that enhance safety, connectivity, and sustainability across the Shasta Region. This update will address critical gaps in active transportation infrastructure, incorporate evolving state and regional priorities, and identify high-impact projects ready for funding and implementation.

ProjectTitle: Yuba County - Climate Action & Adaptation Plan
ProjectAbstract: The County proposes to prepare a Climate Action & Adaptation Plan for adoption by the County’s Board of Supervisors.  The Plan will identify transportation system vulnerabilities and climate-related risks to existing transportation infrastructure users; identify adaptation planning projects that address those vulnerabilities and risks; and set into place climate projects for future programming into local or regional transportation plans, or both.  Climate-related risks will, at a minimum, include Severe Weather ?" Extreme Heat, Flood, and Wildfire.

ProjectTitle: City of Ukiah East Perkins Street Multimodal Transportation Plan
ProjectAbstract: The proposed City of Ukiah East Perkins Street Multimodal Transportation Plan will address deficiencies in pedestrian, bicycle, and transit facilities by studying needs and recommending multimodal and streetscape improvements for East Perkins Street (from Main Street to Oak Manor Drive), a key corridor connecting US 101 to downtown Ukiah.

ProjectTitle: Bizz Johnson Rail Trail Extension Feasibility Study
ProjectAbstract: This project will fund the development of a Feasibility Study to extend the 25.4-mile Bizz Johnson National Recreation Trail another two miles eastward along an abandoned railroad grade to connect with the existing 3.5-mile Skyline Path at the intersection of State Route 36 and Skyline Road.

ProjectTitle: Climate Adaptation Storm Drainage Vulnerability Analysis
ProjectAbstract: This project will conduct a vulnerability analysis of culverts running under County owned and maintained rural roadways for impacts due to climate change. ProjectTitle: Loleta Safe Routes to School and Connectivity to Tribal Lands
ProjectAbstract: HCAOG will partner with Redwood Community Action Agency, the Wiyot Tribe, the Bear River Band of the Rohnerville Rancheria, Humboldt County Public Works, Caltrans, community members of Loleta to develop 30% design plans that focus on multimodal transportation safety improvements from Loleta Elementary School to Loleta’s Main Street, and two Tribally-informed multimodal needs assessments and concept plans focused on enhancing transportation safety between both Bear River Rancheria and the Wiyot Tribe's Table Bluff Reservation, and Loleta Elementary/Main Street.

ProjectTitle: Mendocino County Regional Vehicle Miles Traveled (VMT) Mitigation Program
ProjectAbstract: MCOG will develop a Regional VMT Mitigation Program for the Mendocino County region to help local jurisdictions comply with SB 743 which requires CEQA lead agencies to assess VMT impacts that land use development or transportation projects may cause, and to mitigate these impacts. This project would develop recommendations for a regional VMT mitigation program that would allow developers and project sponsors to offset project VMT impacts through various methods, including the payment of fees, or direct implementation of, projects and programs that would reduce VMT in Mendocino County.

ProjectTitle: Lake County Tribal Transportation Needs and Engineered Feasibility Study
ProjectAbstract: The project will explore the needs, priorities, and feasibility of improving identified deficiencies within tribal road systems and transportation networks, both within and adjacent to native lands in the Lake County region. The goals of the project would be to identify and prioritize tribal transportation projects.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection

ProjectAbstract: We will measure prescribed and cultural fire effects on oaks and other culturally important species. We will calibrate a dynamic vegetation model using multi-site observations for oak woodland structure, and for management and wildfire effects. We will run the calibrated model statewide with alternative management and climate scenarios to inform management planning for climate resilience.

We will develop a scalable next-generation vegetation treatment approach at CAL FIRE through burn planning at demonstration state forests, IC training and virtual prescribed fire training modules.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: A Cost Benefit Framework for Improving the Effectiveness of California’s Fuel Treatment Programs
ProjectAbstract: RFF proposes a generalized economic modeling framework to evaluate costs and benefits of state wildfire hazard mitigation strategies that extends the C+NVC model to address fuel treatment planning, incorporating consequences for damages, suppression costs, and choices over managed fire. This research will provide key insights to decision-makers to evaluate and plan fuel treatment projects.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection

ProjectAbstract: Wildfire activity and severity is on the rise in coast redwood forests. Although redwoods are adapted to survive severe fire, it can have negative effects on habitat, timber quality and human communities. To support better fuels management in the redwood range, we propose to fill two key knowledge gaps: 1) postfire fuels dynamics and 2) fuel load estimations specific to redwood forests.
CountiesServed: Alameda; Del Norte; Humboldt; Mendocino; Napa; San Mateo; Santa Cruz; Sonoma

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection

ProjectAbstract: This project aims to advance Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) fire risk modeling by enhancing the Fire Dynamics Simulator's modeling capabilities and integrating it with geospatial technologies. The framework will enable 3D physics-based and high-resolution parametric simulations of WUI fires, accounting for the complex interactions of terrain, community layout, vegetation, wind, and ember exposure.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Carbon Retention and Resilience in Southern Coast Redwood Forests: The Role of Management, Wood Products, and Wildfire
ProjectAbstract: This project evaluates selective harvest effects on carbon, structure, and fire resilience in southern coast redwood forests. Using Soquel Demonstration State Forest’s harvest history, we integrate field inventory, terrestrial LiDAR, and modeling to assess carbon dynamics, resilience, and harvested wood product storage. Findings will inform climate-adaptive management and restoration practices.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection

The Water Erosion Prediction Project model will be used to simulate and quantify post-wildfire reservoir sedimentation as a function of restoration treatment type, terrain, reservoir proximity, and wildfire hazard.

RecipientName: University of Southern California - ONE Archives at the USC Libraries
ProjectAbstract: We will digitize for online public access archival materials on LGBTQ+ communities of color, transgender people, and people with disabilities in California. By increasing accessibility for materials documenting LGBTQ+ and transgender communities of color and organizations for LGBTQ+ people with disabilities, we will meet the needs of our diverse research communities and help bring these underrepresented stories to the surface.

ProjectTitle: Russian River LGBTQ+ Community Respone to HIV/AIDS
ProjectAbstract: The Russian River Historical Society will document, preserve, and make accessible materials related to the unique response to the AIDS epidemic by the Russian River LGBTQ+ and allied communities in the 1980s. Through oral histories, digitization of West County Health Centers records, and public engagement, we'll preserve this crucial chapter of California LGBTQ+ history showing how rural communities unified against discrimination. We plan to involve younger generation LGBTQI+ to help produce and host public engagement events.

ProjectTitle: Northern California’s Two-Spirit LGBTQ+ History Archive
ProjectAbstract: Queer Humboldt will partner with local organizations, including tribal governments, to document Northern California’s Two-Spirit (2S) and LGBTQ+ history. Young 2S/LGBTQ+ adults will interview 2S/LGBTQ+ elders, highlighting Indigenous and rural voices. Promoted through community channels, this resource will foster intergenerational connections and celebrate and document the Queer history of the California Redwood Coast.

The Rank and File: LGBTQ+ Digital Oral History Project, led by Palm Springs Cultural Center (PSCC), seeks to recover and reveal the cultural histories of the LGBTQ+ Silent Generation and Baby Boomer Generation, whose lives were profoundly impacted by the most dramatic shift in attitudes towards homosexuality in modern history. The project involves recording oral history interviews with LGBTQ+ seniors, producing an ongoing film series, and showcasing the series at Cinema Diverse: The Palm Springs LGBTQ+ Film Festival and online.

ProjectTitle: Intersectional Archives: BIPOC and Transgender Foundations of San Diego’s LGBTQ+ History
ProjectAbstract: This project will digitize and preserve the histories of underrepresented LGBTQ+ communities in San Diego—particularly BIPOC groups, transgender activists, and grassroots organizations. By making these collections accessible online and integrating them into educational curriculums, we aim to honor these voices and provide a richer, more inclusive understanding of LGBTQ+ history for public and educational benefit.

RecipientName: The June L. Mazer Lesbian Archives
ProjectAbstract: This grant will enable the Mazer Lesbian Archives to make available to researchers and the public 11,376 digitized images of the most heavily used materials in our archives by creating metadata which allows us to post them on the UCLA Digital Library. Included are flyers from 1970's collectives, a walking packet to oppose Prop 6, and other one of a kind material.

ProjectTitle: Enhancing Access to LGBTQ Posters and Other Digitized Material at the GLBT Historical Society
ProjectAbstract: We will process our collection of 1,500 posters; purchase equipment for poster digitization; build 10 new digital collections; continue building out our Digital Asset Management System; and host 2 public events. The projects will make our collections more accessible, help us prepare for an upcoming move to our new facility, and ensure remote, public access to our LGBTQ archival material.

ProjectTitle: Gay Games Mobile Interactive Impact Display
ProjectAbstract: Our mission is to create an interactive, multilingual digital display that celebrates and preserves the vibrant histories of LGBTQIA+ artists and allies, local historians, and the global inclusive sports community, while engaging the broader State of California public. We will achieve this by curating and showcasing a dynamic archive of historical video and image assets, accessible in multiple languages, through an intuitive and inclusive platform.  We aim to amplify marginalized voices, foster cultural understanding, and inspire meaningful connections across generations and communities.

ProjectTitle: CRIISC Out in the I.E. Exhibition Project
RecipientName: Civil Rights Institute of Inland Southern California
ProjectAbstract: The Civil Rights Institute of Inland Southern California plans to launch an exhibition project, Out in the I.E., that tells the story of LGBTQ+ communities in Inland Southern California by collecting archival materials, conducting oral histories, collaborating with like minded organizations to make their materials accessible, and using these materials to launch a free public exhibition.
