AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Pathways to Progress: Reducing Youth Recidivism via Mental Health and Wraparound Support
ProjectAbstract: Justice-involved youth in Yolo County face layered and interrelated chalenges that significantly hinder their ability to succeed in school, reintegrate into their communities, and transition into adulthood. These young people often struggle with untreated mental health conditions, disconnection from school, lack of access to job and career opportunities, and the absence of a consistent support system.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Target Population: Parents and caregivers of youth ages 12?20 who are justice-involved or at risk of justice-involvement in Yolo County.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Tuolumne County Probation ? Prop 47 Reentry & Treatment Program
ProjectAbstract: Tuolumne County's Proposition 47 initiative wi l expand diversion and treatment options for individuals with substance use and mental health disorders, particularly those with treatment mandated felonies under Proposition 36.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The target population for this grant includes adults eligible under Proposition 36 who are individuals with multiple prior drug convictions who are now facing treatment-mandated felony charges under Health and Safety Code ?11395.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: CUE's Prop 47 program wil serve up to 150 justice-involved individuals in Valejo over three years, with a focus on Black and Brown men ages 18?35, LGBTQ+ youth, and young parents.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Black, Latinx, and Filipino youth and adults ages 16 to 35 who reside in Valejo, have experienced arrest, incarceration, or probation/diversion, and present with co-occurring behavioral health and substance use disorder (SUD) needs.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The City of Santa Rosa, in partnership with a local nonprofit social service provider (to be determined), proposes the inResponse Health Navigation Program to expand supportive services for individuals with histories of justice involvement, mental health cha lenges, and substance use disorders.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: To address critical gaps in healthcare access, mental health services, and supportive resources for individuals with mental health and/or substance use disorders, who are underserved and/or experiencing homelessness in Santa Rosa.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: San Francisco Department of Public Health
ProjectAbstract: The SFDPH STARR Program provides a critical component towards breaking the cycle of homelessness and addiction in San Francisco by providing additional residential treatment and residential step down beds for criminal justice involved adults with co-occurring substance use disorder and mental health issues. The overall goal is to reduce incarceration and recidivism by bolstering city-wide initiatives focused on jail diversion, recovery, and community re-entry.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Defendants in criminal cases who struggle with mental health and/or substance use issues & experience homelessness will be diverted from jail to receive community-based support, including supplemental housing-related services, job skills training, case management, & civil legal services

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The County of San Luis Obispo's Preventing Re-Offense Project (SLO PROP) is a comprehensive community mental health and substance use disorder program addressing Proposition 36's focus on rising crime, drug addiction, and homelessness; the elevated rate of overdose deaths in the county; and recidivism rates.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The target population to be addressed by the SLO PROP Proposition 47 Grant are primarily those individuals meeting the Prop 36 (11395) criteria and other clients who have been arrested, charged with, or convicted of a criminal offense and who have a history of mental health and SUD issues.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: City of Redlands Path from Reentry and Houseless to Self Sustainability
ProjectAbstract: The City of Redlands seeks funding through California's Proposition 47 grant program to expand its community-based services for individuals experiencing homelessness who are also impacted by low-level criminal offenses. This initiative builds upon existing municipal and county efforts, aiming to create a robust continuum of care that breaks the cycle of homelessness, justice system involvement, and poverty.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: City of Redlands Proposition 47 Grant Application Summary Supporting Homeless Individuals with Low-Level Offenses through Shelter,Workforce Development, and Permanent Housing.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Pathways to Healing and Recovery is a comprehensive reentry program aimed at fostering a thriving Los Angeles by supporting individuals affected by incarceration who also face mental health and substance use challenges.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Pathways will serve justice-involved adults for up to 18 months, offering support for stabilization, treatment, and reintegration. Services will be provided in three regions of Los Angeles: San Fernando Valley, Central and South Los Angeles.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: Pala Band of Mission Indians - Pala Housing Resource Center
ProjectAbstract: Native Youth Rising will strengthen and expand support systems to address critical service gaps in mental health, substance use treatment, housing, culturally based community services, life skills development, workforce  readiness, civil legal advocacy, and intensive case management.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: This project focuses on tribal youth ages 12?26 who are enrolled members or descendants of the Pala Band of Mission Indians, or other Native youth residing on/near the Pala Reservation in northeast San Diego County.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The LBUSD School-Based Youth Diversion Program interrupts the school to prison pipeline by offering early intervention for students cited or arrested for nonviolent offenses on school campuses. Focused on restorative justice, the program diverts youth from formal justice involvement through a culturally competent, trauma-informed model.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Long Beach Unified School District (LBUSD) is committed to implementing alternatives to punitive school discipline in order to mitigate practices that fuel the school-to-prison pipeline, especially for students navigating multiple layers of vulnerability.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Care Management and Workforce Services for Justice Involved Individuals of LA County
RecipientName: Los Angeles County Justice, Care and Opportunities Department
ProjectAbstract: The Los Angeles County Justice, Care and Opportunities Department (JCOD) will continue to provide and expand reentry-focused intensive care management, and wrap-around services as well as sector-based employment services to improve behavioral health and employment outcomes and reduce recidivism among justice-involved individuals with mild to moderate substance use and mental health disorders.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The target population for LA County's Proposition 47 (Prop 47) grant funding is adults (age 18 and older) who have been arrested, charged with, and/or convicted of a non-violent, non-sexual, and non-serious criminal offense and who have mild to moderate MH and/or substance use disorders (SUD).

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Reentry Intervention Support and Engagement (RISE) System
ProjectAbstract: The Reentry, Intervention, Support, and Engagement (RISE) system pilot is a behavioral health intervention system and program model led by El Dorado County Probation to reduce recidivism, improve access to care, and support reentry for adults with mental health and substance use disorders. RISE integrates court, custody, and community-based services to create a seamless, individualized care pathway across pretrial, diversion, and felony supervision caseloads.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The Reentry, Intervention, Support, and Engagement (RISE) pilot system addresses critical service gaps for individuals with mental health and substance use disorders (SUD) who fall outside County Behavioral Health's specialty mental health programs.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: Kern County Behavioral Health and Recovery Services
ProjectAbstract: Kern Behavioral Health & Recovery Services (KernBHRS) provides high quality behavioral health care to Medi-Cal members in Kern County. The Kern New Beginnings (KNB) program will treat eligible individuals, under newly passed Proposition 36, by providing a substance use disorder (SUD) and/or mental health (MH) treatment alternative to felonies for certain drug related crimes. KNB will provide brief evaluations, treatment referrals, case management, and housing resources.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The purpose of the Kern New Beginnings Program (KNB) is to expand Substance Use Disorder (SUD) and Mental Health (MH) treatment to justice-involved individuals as an alternative to a felony conviction for certain drug-related crimes.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The City of Berkeley is applying for $8 million in Proposition 47 Cohort 5 funding to launch the Berkeley CareBridge Program-a post-arrest diversion and reentry initiative that will provide transitional housing and wraparound services to unhoused individuals with mental health and/or substance use disorders (MH/SUD) who are arrested for low-level offenses in Berkeley. The program is designed to address systemic gaps between arrest, behavioral health care, and housing access-offering a treatment-based alternative to recidivism.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The City of Berkeley (COB) faces an urgent and growing crisis at the intersection of homelessness, mental health (MH), substance use disorder (SUD), and criminal justice involvement.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: B2W-Pathways is a regionally coordinated reentry program serving justice involved individuals with behavioral health needs returning to California's Central Valley. A collaboration between Back 2 Work (BCOE), North Star Wellness Center, and Workbay, the initiative blends workforce, behavioral health, and technology solutions to deliver wraparound care. It offers trauma-informed housing, outpatient treatment, legal support, and employment navigation
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The B2W-Pathways initiative focuses specifically on justice-involved individuals returning to Central Valley communities, particularly those reentering from state prisons or under Fresno County Probation supervision.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: El Dorado County Office of Education
ProjectAbstract: This Counties Against Recidivism project launches with the El Dorado County Office of Education, generating high-impact data to serve as a catalyst for scaling the model across California's County Offices of Education. High-dosage tutoring-an evidence-based strategy widely used in public K-12 schools-remains largely untapped for justice impacted students. This project will demonstrate HDT's potential to reduce recidivism, complemented by wraparound services such as mentoring, high school diploma & CTE certificate support, & job placement programming.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Gaps exist in educational programming that targets the reduction of recidivism in disproportionately diverse and vulnerable student populations, particularly through the usage of highdosage tutoring?an innovative, evidence-based diversion program utilized nationwide by public K12 schools.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: PROJECT?RESTORE is a Prop?47-funded diversion initiative led by the Tehama County Department of Education in partnership with communitybased organizations to reduce recidivism.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: ROJECT RESTORE serves justice-involved adolescents and young adults (ages?12?30) with mental health and substance use needs.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: County of Santa Barbara Department of Behavioral Welness
ProjectAbstract: The Justice & Healing Colaborative (JHC) aims to identify and divert individuals with behavioral health needs as soon as possible after arrest. Through earlier screening and expanded treatment, we aim to reduce racial disparities in our jail population.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The goal is to reduce the harm of pre-trial incarceration for those welsuited to be released from jail and diverted from the criminal legal system.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: REDIRECT: Restorative Engagement and Diversion through Incarceration Reduction, Care and Treatment
ProjectAbstract: The Restorative Engagement and Diversion through Incarceration Reduction, Care and Treatment (REDIRECT) Project flips the script on justice-involvement by treating trauma, not just behavior.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Focused on youth and adults ages 15?35 with Proposition 47-eligible offenses, REDIRECT recognizes substance use and criminal behavior as symptoms of deeper issues: unaddressed trauma, instability, and systemic neglect.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Public Summary of Proposition 47 Cohort 5 Proposal The Sacramento Employment and Training Agency (SETA), in colaboration with Emerge Career as the primary service provider, seeks Proposition 47 Cohort 5 funding to implement a comprehensive, community - based reentry program in Sacramento County.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: SETA, in partnership with Emerge Career, proposes to serve justice involved adults residing in Sacramento County who (1) have been arrested or convicted of a non-violent offense and (2) have a documented or self subscribed history of mental i lness and/or substance use disorder (SUD).

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: SB Cares: Community Alternatives, Recovery, and Empowerment Services
ProjectAbstract: The City of San Bernardino seeks Proposition 47 funding to expand its PEACE Team. The expanded PEACE Team will serve adults arrested, charged, or convicted of criminal offenses and those with a history of substance use or mental health disorders; many also experience homelessness or chronic instability
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The target population-adults who have been arrested or charged with low-level offenses and who have a history of mental health or substance use disorders-mirrors the core demographic that Prop 47 funding seeks to support.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Pasadena HOME (Helping Offenders with Meaningful Engagement) Diversion Program
RecipientName: Pasadena City Attorney / City Prosecutor's Office
ProjectAbstract: The Pasadena City Attorney / City Prosecutor's Office HOME Diversion program (Helping Offenders with Meaningful Engagement) will connect justice-involved unhoused adults with a history of mental health or substance use disorders to housing and treatment.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The intended target population for this Prop 47 initiative is adults experiencing homelessness within the City of Pasadena who have been cited or arrested for misdemeanor offenses, including those covered by Prop 47.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Pasadena Outreach Response Team (PORT) Expansion Project
ProjectAbstract: The Pasadena Outreach Response Team - Expansion (PORT-E) is a  multidisciplinary, field-based program that diverts justice-involved, unhoused individuals with behavioral health needs away from incarceration and into care. Led by the City of Pasadena Public Health Department, PORT-E provides proactive outreach, intensive case management, housing navigation, health screenings, and behavioral health referrals to unhoused individuals.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The PORT-E program is designed to serve a measurable, high-need subset of the local unhoused population: individuals experiencing homelessness in Pasadena who have a history of criminal justice involvement & who also face serious mental health, substance use, and/or co-occurring medical conditions.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The City of Hayward proposes to expand its successful Hayward Navigation Center (HNCP47), a diversion and reentry program for adults experiencing homelessness with histories of mental illness, substance use disorders, and justice involvement. Located within the under development 4.13-acre Regis Village, the 40-bed downtown HNCP47 facility will provide non-congregate housing and wraparound services, including behavioral health treatment, case management, and housing navigation.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The Hayward Navigation Center (HNC47) will serve adults who are homeless, have a history of mental health/substance use disorders (SUD) and have been arrested, charged with, or convicted of a crime.

ProjectTitle: Campesino de California Outreach Grant - Radio Media Program Year 2025-26
ProjectAbstract: The La Cooperativa partnership will develop and deliver a statewide radio media outreach program to farmworkers and their families through 24 live, semi-monthly 30-minute public affairs “La Voz del Campo” radio talk shows. The shows will be done in Spanish, then rebroadcast during the network’s Mixteco and Triqui programming. The radio broadcasts will highlight the full range of Employment Development Department (EDD) and partner services and provide Subject Matter Experts on current topics of interest and benefit to California's farmworker communities.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Amador, Butte, Colusa, Fresno, Glenn, Imperial, Kern, Kings, Lake, Lassen, Madera Merced, Modoc, Monterey, Napa, Riverside, Sacramento, San Benito, San Bernardino, San Diego, San Joaquin, San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara, Santa Clara, Santa Cruz, Sierra, Siskiyou, Solano, Sonoma, Stanislaus, Sutter, Tehama, Tulare, Ventura, Yuba, and Yolo counties.

ProjectAbstract: The research proposes to evaluate how post-fire restocking affects forest recovery and wildfire hazard, comparing areas with different management intensities, planting patterns, and fire histories on forestlands in CAL FIRE's Northern Forest District.

RecipientName: Fernande?o Tataviam Band of Mission Indians
ProjectAbstract: FTBMI San Fernando is a 4-story, 27 unit new construction senior project, with one manager unit, 24 one-bedroom units, and 2 two-bedroom units serving households with incomes ranging from 30-50% of the AMI. The project is located on Fee Land and will have be restricted to seniors who are Tribal Members.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Project is located on Fee Land and will have a preference for Tribal members that are seniors.

AgencyDept: Department of Housing and Community Development
ProjectAbstract: Two Feathers Wellness Village is an Eight (8) unit New Construction Special Needs project with Six (6) one-bedroom, One (1) two-bedroom, One (1) three-bedroom serving households with incomes at 15 percent of Area Median Income (AMI) to primarily house individuals and families experiencing homelessness or at-risk of homelessness, and no manager's unit. Units will have a washer/dryer, dishwasher, disposal, refrigerator, range, microwave, storage area, ceiling fans, air conditioning, blinds and patio. Amenities include a Community Room, Picnic Area, Playground, Gated Entry, and Security Cameras.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Project is located on Fee Land inside of Indian Country and will serve the Tribal members.

AgencyDept: Department of Housing and Community Development
ProjectAbstract: Tribal Winds - Phase 5 is an Eighteen (18) new construction single family dwelling project with Ten (10) two-bedrooms, and Eight (8) three-bedrooms serving households with incomes at 20 percent of Area Median Income (AMI) for Special Needs Population that are experiencing homelessness in Covelo, Mendocino County, within the Trust Lands of the Round Valley Indian Tribe.  Each home will have a washer/ dryer, dishwasher, disposal, refrigerator, range, microwave, ceiling fans, air conditioning, fireplace, patio, and fenced rear yard. Amenities include High Speed Internet and Playground.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Project is located in Tribal Trust Lands and will serve members of the Tribe.

AgencyDept: Department of Housing and Community Development
ProjectAbstract: Maidu Mountain Lion Housing Development is a 12 single family, new construction project that will consist of 6 two-bedroom units and 6 three-bedroom units serving households at 30% of the AMI. The project is located on Fee land outside of Indian Country and the Tribe intends to place the land into Tribal Trust in the near future. The project will serve their Tribal members.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Project is located on Fee Land outside of Indian Country and the Tribe intends to place the land into Trust in the near future.

AgencyDept: Department of Housing and Community Development
ProjectAbstract: Kamath Glen Yurok Homes is a twenty-four (24) unit new construction SNP/SH/LF project located within Indian Country. Units will consist of 12 single family homes (3 bedroom, 2 bathrooms) and 12 one-bedroom attached dwelling units. The twenty-four (24) unit development includes one manager's unit. The project will occupy populations with extremely low income 30-80 percent of Area Median Income (AMI), and an average AMI of 50%, per tax credit requirements. The project is located on Fee land Within Indian Country and will serve members of the Tribe.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The project is located on Fee land Within Indian Country and will serve members of the Tribe.

AgencyDept: Department of Housing and Community Development
ProjectAbstract: The CICC's Old Res Housing Complex is a new construction project which will provide 21 permanent, rental supportive housing units. It is comprised of two eight-plex buildings with 16 two-bedroom units and 5 three-bedroom villas, serving individuals with incomes at 40 percent of the Area Median Income (AMI). All units, except the manager unit, will be subsidized by Tribal General fund. The overall building will be two-story with a communal green area between the two buildings. The 5 villas will be single story units and will serve members of the Tribe.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The project is located within boundaries the Tribal Trust land and will serve members of the tribe.

AgencyDept: Department of Housing and Community Development
RecipientName: Dry Creek Rancheria Band of Pomo Indians
ProjectAbstract: Bi'du Khaale is a 25 unit new construction senior project with seventeen (17) two-bedroom, and seven (7) three-bedroom serving households with incomes ranging from 30 to 60 percent of Area Median Income (AMI), and one (1) two-bedroom manager's unit. Each unit will have a washer/dryer, dishwasher, refrigerator, electric range, ceiling fan, central air, window blinds, composite/title flooring, grab bars in primary bathroom, patio, attached one car garage with 34 parking spaces. and a community center.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Project is located on Fee Land outside of Indian Country and will serve Tribal members that are seniors.

AgencyDept: Department of Housing and Community Development
RecipientName: Big Sandy Rancheria of Western Mono Indians

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Medeiros Dairy Inc Mechanical Separator Project
ProjectAbstract: Medeiros Dairy Inc. will improve their current manure management practices by construction an AgPro mechanical separator to reduce solids from entering the waste stream conveyed to the storage ponds, with the added benefits of reducing greenhouse gases and improving facility aesthetics.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Mancebo Holstein Dairy Solid Separation Project
ProjectAbstract: The project includes installing a new mechanical solid-liquid separator to treat all liquid manure produced daily at the dairy. The treated water will be used for irrigation with lower environmental risks. By effectively separating the solids, the dairy can prevent the long-term storage of volatile solids and nutrients in lagoons where anaerobic conditions generate methane and ammonia emissions. The project will significantly increase the volume of solids separated from the liquid stream before entering the lagoon. The separated solids will be composted and spread on the fields.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: SCREWworm: Surveillance, Control, Research, and Education Working group for IPM of a critical invasive threat to California
ProjectAbstract: Working closely with CDFA’s Animal Health Branch, this project will establish the necessary framework for rapid response to screwworm. New world screwworm would be a significantly damaging pest of animal industries in California if it were to re-establish here. The project aims to form a working group and a surveillance network, develop IPM guidelines for both prevention and control of infestations, and initiate an educational training program to empower veterinarians and animal producers to better recognize, address, and report screwworm infestations in animals.

ProjectTitle: Tulloch Reservoir - Aquatic Invasive Species Prevention Initiatives
ProjectAbstract: Activities funded by this grant project will ultimately support the reactivation of Tulloch Reservoir's primary public decontamination station, which is currently non-operational. Reactivating this site is a priority as it will enhance decontamination access for high-traffic users, increase geographic coverage of AIS prevention protocols, and support broader regional containment efforts in light of recent Golden Mussel detections.

ProjectTitle: Santa Clara County Parks Invasive Mussel Response (IMR) Project
RecipientName: County of Santa Clara (Parks and Recreation)
ProjectAbstract: Invasive mussels pose a serious threat to both the infrastructure and the ecological integrity of freshwater systems. This grant funds the purchase and deployment of two mobile trailer-mounted hot-water decontamination units using recycled water, plus one additional pump for maintenance resilience during unit breakdowns. The objective of this grant is to safeguard water supply infrastructure, protect local aquatic ecosystems, and maintain public recreational boating opportunities at Santa Clara County's reservoirs.

ProjectTitle: Trinity and Lewiston Lake Aquatic Invasive Prevention
ProjectAbstract: This grant project aims to protect Trinity and Lewiston Lakes, as well as downstream waterbodies, from the threat of aquatic invasive species with the acquisition of decontamination equipment and training resources.

ProjectTitle: Nevada Irrigation District - Invasive Mussel Response
ProjectAbstract: This grant funds the procurement of a mobile decontamination unit in addition to removable bollard materials for two reservoirs managed by the Nevada Irrigation District: Scotts Flat and Rollins Reservoir. This is aimed at preventing the introduction of invasive mussels.

ProjectTitle: Rancho Seco Lake- Invasive Mussel Prevention
ProjectAbstract: This grant aims to prevent the spread of invasive Golden Mussels at SMUD's Rancho Seco Lake location. Besides its importance to SMUD power generation, the Rancho Seco Lake location is part of the larger 400-acre Rancho Seco Recreational Park open to the public for camping, fishing, hiking and water activities, receiving approximately 100,000 visitors per year. Project funds will be spent on allowable equipment purchases and facility enhancements. This grant will benefit recreational boaters by maintaining an open lake with available capacity.

ProjectTitle: Ruth Lake Boat Decontamination Facility for Invasive Mussel Prevention
ProjectAbstract: The Grantee plans to invest in a Clean Wake decontamination dip tank at Ruth Lake to enhance aquatic invasive species prevention efforts. This grant would support efforts to move forward with this purchase and implementation. Recreational boaters with watercrafts with a ballast tank would have the option to be able to launch their watercraft into the lake following a decontamination process without undergoing a mandatory 30-day quarantine.

ProjectTitle: Invasive Mussel Prevention to Preserve Boating Access at Nacimiento and San Antonio Reservoirs
ProjectAbstract: The objective of this grant is to prevent the introduction of golden mussels, quagga mussels, and zebra mussels, into the Nacimiento Reservoir located in San Luis Obispo County and the San Antonio Reservoir in Monterey County. In addition, grant funded activities will benefit recreational boaters by ensuring continued public access to the Nacimiento and San Antonio Reservoirs and preventing damage to boating equipment, docks, and launch ramps that could occur if a vessel or related infrastructure is impacted by invasive mussels.

ProjectTitle: Invasive Mussel Response - Modesto and Woodward Reservoirs
ProjectAbstract: County of Stanislaus Parks and Recreation staff will implement this grant project at both the Woodward Reservoir and the Modesto Reservoir. The grant funds will be used to support invasive mussel prevention activities such as vessel inspections and decontaminations as well as staff trainings. By participating in the Grantee's inspection and decontamination processes, recreational boaters help prevent the spread of invasive mussels and reduce the risk of reservoir closures due to infestations.

ProjectTitle: Mobile Mussel Prevention at Lake McClure and Lake McSwain: Deploying a Self-Service Clean-Drain-Dry Station
ProjectAbstract: Grant funding will be used to acquire one Clean-Drain-Dry-Dispose (CD3) Wayside Solar Trailer System to be deployed at the busiest reservoir access points based on seasonal launch data and logistical access to support continued safe and sustainable boating at Lake McClure and Lake McSwain, and to help avoid costly access restrictions due to mussel infestations.

ProjectTitle: Invasive Mussel Response Program for Folsom Reservoir
RecipientName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectAbstract: This grant project will be implemented by the California Department of Parks and Recreation and will fund the purchase of seals/cables supplies critical to supporting invasive mussel prevention activities at Folsom Reservoir which is currently facing a high introduction risk due to its year-round boat traffic. The supplies will ensure safe and efficient boat launches while protecting long-term recreational use.

ProjectTitle: Department of Water Resources Watercraft Decontamination Unit
ProjectAbstract: The grant funds awarded for this project will be used to purchase equipment and field supplies to support the watercraft inspection and decontamination program to aid in the prevention of golden, quagga, and zebra mussels from entering DWR's Oroville Field Division reservoirs. This will benefit recreational boaters by protecting the fisheries and recreational opportunities at these reservoirs.

ProjectTitle: Lake Casitas Recreation Area Decontamination Unit
ProjectAbstract: This project involves the procurement of one trailer mounted hot water pressure washer/decontamination unit which will be solely dedicated for use at the Lake Casitas Recreation Area (LCRA). Procuring a unit dedicated to the LCRA for the purpose of decontamination is necessary to enhance the efficiency of the existing process and help prevent the introduction of invasive mussels in Lake Casitas.

ProjectTitle: Elk Creek Fish Passage and Sediment Reduction Project, Crossing 1
ProjectAbstract: The project will restore fish passage and migration access to spawning and rearing coho salmon by replacing an existing undersized culvert with an 8-foot-diameter culvert with a natural channel bottom. The culvert upgrade is one part of a larger project that will restore fish passage at six barriers in the headwaters of Elk Creek. Riparian plants will be installed in areas impacted by construction and currently lacking riparian cover.

ProjectTitle: Arroyo Seco River Fish Passage Project - Sycamore Flats
ProjectAbstract: This project will implement (permit and construct) a project designed through a CDFW WGP Plan/Design contract Q2396022. Construction will remove an existing concrete vehicle ford which spans the Arroyo Seco River (barrier) and replace it consistent with approved plans on private property (Sycamore Flats). The completed project will eliminate a priority migration barrier and improve conditions for federally threatened South Central Coast steelhead trout on the Arroyo Seco River in Monterey Co.

ProjectTitle: Lower SLO Creek Floodplain Preserve Steelhead Habitat Enhancement Project
RecipientName: The Land Conservancy of San Luis Obispo County
ProjectAbstract: The goal of the Project is to provide design and permitting for habitat restoration opportunities benefiting steelhead on the Land Conservancy's Lower SLO Creek Floodplain Preserve Properties. The design will include large wood augmentation, expansion of floodplain connectivity through creation of off-channel habitat, and diversification of hydraulic and geomorphic complexity throughout the floodplain.

ProjectTitle: Green Valley Creek Off-Channel Habitat Enhancement Implementation at Sweetwater Nursery
ProjectAbstract: The project will connect an existing floodplain pond to Green Valley Creek via an excavated connector channel to allow free access to off-channel habitat for juvenile salmonids at flows above an estimated winter base flow. This will Improve complex instream rearing habitat adjacent to the connector channel through: excavation of a pool/alcove at inlet and inset floodplain with swales/alcoves downstream and Installation of engineered log jams to drive pool development and provide woody cover.

ProjectTitle: Upper SF Eel River Instream Habitat Improvement Project
ProjectAbstract: The project will increase salmonid survival by improving available habitat for spawning and rearing. This will be accomplished by implementing engineered design plans for a large wood project along 3.5 mi of the upper South Fork Eel River. Forty-one LW structures will be constructed using 145 logs, 21 logs with rootwads, and 202 boulders. Structures will deepen pools, increase shelter and shelter complexity, capture spawning gravels, improve off-channel habitat, increase floodplain and side channel inundation, and provide velocity refugia to Coho, Chinook, and steelhead.

ProjectTitle: Hydrology to Habitat: Critical Steelhead Restoration Assessments in San Luis Obispo Creek Watershed
ProjectAbstract: The purpose of this project is to collect the data and conduct the landowner outreach required to identify and advance transformative steelhead habitat restoration projects on SLO Creek and its major tributaries including fish passage improvements, steelhead rearing habitat enhancement, estuary restoration and streamflow enhancement. Data will include barrier assessments, engineering barrier analysis, ecologically critical streamflow monitoring, water quality and steelhead mark and recapture.

The Annual Salmonid Restoration conference offers an unparalleled opportunity for stakeholders with a vested interest in the recovery of California's native salmonid populations to engage in technical education. The 4-day conference highlights regional and topical issues that affect salmonids and their diverse habitats through field tours, technical workshops, panel discussions, and a plenary session on the state of salmonid recovery in California. Field tours include all-day visits to regional, dynamic, state-of-the-art restoration sites.

ProjectTitle: Cachagua Creek Fish Passage Alternative Plan/Design Project - Quevedo
ProjectAbstract: The project will provide a Plan/Design to remediate an existing migration barrier in this important tributary to the Carmel River. The focus is a concrete ford which provides access to a private residence (Quevedo). The ford is a partial migration barrier for all life stages of SCCC steelhead. The removal and replacement with a free span bridge will improve migration conditions in this important reach of Cachagua Creek.

ProjectTitle: Bridge Creek - CCC Large Wood Coho Habitat Enhancement Project
ProjectAbstract: The project goal is to improve the quality, complexity, and frequency of pools, provide flow refugia for salmonids, and sort spawning gravels in Bridge Creek by installing properly sized large wood (LWD) features throughout a 0.86 mile stream reach. The project will result in 46 LWD features, comprised of 151 pieces of properly sized LWD. This will bring the key piece count within the project reach from a "Poor" rating to a "Very Good" rating for frequency of wood within the stream as outlined in the NOAA Fisheries Final Recovery Plan for Central California Coast Coho Salmon ESU.

ProjectTitle: Chamberlain Creek Instream Habitat Enhancement Project
ProjectAbstract: The project will improve Coho and steelhead trout habitat in the 2.56-mi Chamberlain Creek project reach by installing large wood structures to increase stream complexity, pool frequency, pool depth, and provide high-flow refugia, cover and protection from predation, and over-summer and over-winter rearing habitat. The project will procure material and install 114 non-engineered LW unique structures, install erosion control treatments and rehabilitate site post-construction in 1.37 acres of riparian area, and document pre-implementation and post-implementation conditions at all structures.

ProjectTitle: Upper Long Bar Salmonid Rearing Habitat Restoration Project
ProjectAbstract: This Project aims to restore 8 acres on the lower Yuba River by introducing complexity to the main channel's edge through grading seasonal and perennial habitat features (alcoves, floodrunner, large wood, edge enhancements, and roughness features) designed to meet the biological needs of special status species including fall-/spring-run Chinook salmon and Central Valley steelhead during the rearing period. Planning, permitting, and design work are complete, making this a shovel-ready project.

ProjectTitle: Bouverie Dam Removal for Fish Passage
ProjectAbstract: This project restores access to .68 mi high-quality rearing habitat for federally endangered steelhead trout by removing Bouverie Dam, the final human-made barrier to fish passage in Stuart Creek, a tributary to Sonoma Creek in the San Pablo Bay watershed. Located on Audubon Canyon Ranch's Bouverie Preserve, the decommissioned 45-ft concrete diversion dam is a complete barrier to juvenile salmonids and a substantial impediment to adult passage. The project will remove the dam and construct a stream simulation channel.

ProjectTitle: Upper Klamath River Design and Planning Project - Beaver Creek
ProjectAbstract: This project will develop a 100% level fisheries restoration design on seven miles of Beaver Creek. The project area has approximately 50 acres of low lying floodplain that is disconnected due to channel constraint. The design would improve conditions for spawning and rearing fish by proposing: 1) the removal of berms, 2) the creation of side channels and off-channel features, 3) grading floodplain material at strategic locations to widen the channel, and 4) adding instream structures.

ProjectTitle: Lower SF Cottaneva Instream Habitat Improvement Project
ProjectAbstract: This project will add 38 structures along 1.2 mi of South Fork Cottaneva Creek, Rockport Creek, and an unnamed tributary to Rockport Creek. Redwood seedlings and native plants will be planted in the riparian zone. The goal is to increase salmonid reproductive success and juvenile survival by improving ecological complexity.

ProjectTitle: Yr. 33 Watershed Stewards Program in partnership with the California Conservation Corps and AmeriCorps
RecipientName: California Conservation Corps Watershed Stewards Program in partnership with AmeriCorps
ProjectAbstract: The California Conservation Corps Watershed Stewards Program in partnership with AmeriCorps (WSP) will engage 44 WSP Corpsmembers throughout CA to monitor and enhance anadromous watersheds through fisheries/habitat surveys, riparian restoration, community education/engagement, and by providing participants with insight into the environmental science field. WSPs habitat improvement strategy is multifaceted and has produced a greater understanding of watershed needs and solutions for over 30 yrs.

ProjectTitle: 2025 Mainstem Buckeye Creek Instream Enhancement Project
ProjectAbstract: This goal of this project is to restore salmonid habitat by placing 55 key pieces of large woody debris at 21 structure sites in 4,340 feet of Buckeye Creek to increase stream complexity, high flow refugia, pool frequency and rearing habit for salmonids.

ProjectTitle: Blue Lake Rancheria Good Fire Healing Coalition
ProjectAbstract: Blue Lake Rancheria’s (BLR) ‘Good Fire Healing Coalition’ looks to build a regional team of Indigenous women cultural burners to be housed at BLR. The project will enact fire management regimes on BLR’s recently acquired fee title lands, Leavey Ranch. Fire management regimes, including prescribed and cultural burns, will be implemented for the restoration of pyro dependent ecosystems and cultural resources, supporting BLR’s food sovereignty and Traditional Ecological Knowledge resurgence.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Bringing Good Fire Back: Mooretown Tribal Cultural Landscape
RecipientName: Mooretown Rancheria of Maidu Indians of California
ProjectAbstract: The purpose of this project is to support Mooretown Rancheria in healing a large swath of their ancestral lands after the catastrophic North Complex Fire (2020) by restoring a forest ecosystem that is vital to plants, animals, and people. This project focuses on an early phase in a large-scale project. The proposed project is part of a larger vision of incorporating indigenous land management techniques across a larger landscape to promote culture, restore habitat, and increase resilience.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectAbstract: The Deer Flat Camp project includes removal of uncharacteristically dense brush, oak woodland restoration, thinning overstocked conifer stands, grass seeding, and roadside fuels treatments on the Round Valley Indian Tribes' 90-acre Deer Flat property. The Tribes’ objective is to rehabilitate the property so it can be used as a summer camp for Tribal youth, a training area for prescribed/cultural fire, and a place for the stewardship of ancestral fishing, hunting, and gathering areas. The project will also provide workforce development opportunities for RVIT’s Forestry and Youth crews.

ProjectAbstract: Rural Initiative Grants will be funded using JUUL settlement funds allocated to the California Department of Education by the California Department of Justice. Funding will support existing youth education and outreach, as well as the development of new educational campaigns in tobacco prevention for California student communities. Funding will help to counter trends by developing up to two Rural Initiative Centers to increase student access to Tobacco-Use Prevention Education (TUPE) services in underserved rural areas.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectAbstract: The Top Line Dairy Digester project will construct a new covered lagoon dairy digester facility for the purpose of capturing manure methane emissions to create carbon-negative transportation fuel while increasing the environmental sustainability of the host dairy, Top Line Dairy. The Top Line Dairy Digester project will capture the biogas from the digested manure, transport it via private pipeline to the Lakeside Pipeline conditioning facility and then inject the product biomethane directly into the utility pipeline. The project is being developed by Maas Energy Works LLC.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Reduce health harms suffered disproportionately by priority populations due to air pollutants. Create quality jobs and increase family income. Increase job readiness and career opportunities.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectAbstract: Correia Dairy is part of the developing Gustine dairy biogas to fuel cluster in Merced County, CA. The project is committed to building a Tier 1 double-lined, manure-only, covered lagoon digester with integrated gas storage and pre-treatment. An on-dairy biogas conditioning system will remove hydrogen sulfide and moisture and then meter and move the clean biogas into a gathering line connecting to a centralized biogas upgrading and interconnection facility. The project's biomethane will be delivered as R-CNG to fleets and CNG fueling stations in California.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Identified community needs that this project will address include improving air quality, increasing energy production, providing local internships, and creating local jobs.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectAbstract: Black Diamond Dairy will install a Tier 1 designed manure only covered lagoon digester with integrated gas storage and pre-treatment. An on-dairy biogas conditioning system will remove hydrogen sulfide and meter and move the clean biogas directly into 4 co-located, ultraclean, high efficiency Mainspring linear generators interconnected to PG&E. CalBio will generate LCFS credits by directly matching generation and supplying the renewable energy credits to in-state electric vehicle re-charging load.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Identified community needs that this project will address include improving air quality, increasing energy production, providing local internships, and creating local jobs.

Biomethane, meeting PG&E Rules 21 and 29, will be injected into the co-located point of receipt. The project's biomethane will be delivered as R-CNG to fleets and CNG fueling stations in California. California Bioenergy is the project developer.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Cost-effective, Bespoke Adaptive Tutoring using Open Source Tools and GenAI
ProjectAbstract: UC Berkeley partners with San José State and Mission College will expand the open-source OATutor platform from UC Berkeley to provide low-cost, mastery-based STEM tutoring. Using generative AI, the system personalizes instruction to teachers and students, enhancing learning and accessibility. All tools and materials will be freely shared under open licenses.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: GenAI Preparedness for Teaching & Learning at SF State
ProjectAbstract: This project will advance institution-wide readiness and governance around Generative AI through faculty development, intra- and inter-departmental collaboration, and policy design. The grant will support the critical, ethical, and equitable development and adoption of cutting-edge GenAI processes, policies, and curricular tools and materials to support student academic success and workforce preparation.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: GenAI as Coding Tutor to Support First Year Engineering Students
ProjectAbstract: This  project integrates an AI coding tutor into an introductory MATLAB course for first-year and transfer aerospace engineering students. By providing real-time, personalized feedback, the tutor supports students with limited coding experience, improves problem-solving and confidence, and reduces equity gaps.  The use of an AI coding tutor aims to reduce equity gaps by providing equal access to high-quality programming resources for all students, regardless of background or prior experience with coding.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Empowering Future Educators with AI-Enhanced Pedagogy
ProjectAbstract: This project will integrate AI tools into the Elementary Teacher Education associate’s degree program to transform curriculum, pedagogy, and student learning. Embedding AI across courses will prepare future educators to use these technologies ethically and inclusively. By providing faculty with professional development in AI, the project will transition from faculty-led innovation to college-approved policies and procedures, ensuring the sustainable use of AI across the institution.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: AI-Enhanced Curriculum: Transforming Calculus and Statistics Education
ProjectAbstract: This project will transform Calculus 1 instruction by integrating AI tools like MathGPT.ai and ChatGPT to enhance engagement and conceptual understanding. Faculty will collaborate through a Community of Practice to design AI-driven, inquiry-based modules and workshops. A pilot AI-enhanced course will assess impacts on problem-solving, skill mastery, and student attitudes toward AI in learning.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: The Japanese American Incarceration Testimony Interactive Q&A Project
ProjectAbstract: This project uses AI to transform video archives of Japanese Americans incarcerated during WWII into an interactive educational tool. Using NLP, students and educators can ask questions and receive AI-generated responses from survivors’ stories. (NLP) will enable users to ask questions and receive AI-driven responses directly from the archive. It will  be integrated into History, Journalism, and Computer Science courses. By offering free access, the project ensures that students from diverse backgrounds can connect with this vital part of Central California’s history.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: SCAPE: Student-centered Collaborative AI Platform for Personalized Engineering Learning Experience
ProjectAbstract: This project will develop SCAPE?"an open-source, student-centered AI platform for personalized engineering learning. Emphasizing transparency, equity, and educator control, SCAPE integrates human insight to support critical thinking and reduce bias.  SCAPE guides students through problem-solving processes with detailed, step-by-step explanations to foster critical thinking and independence.  Piloted across multiple engineering disciplines, the project will also launch a Faculty Ambassadors program and create an AI collaboration handbook to promote inclusive AI education.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Customizable AI Integration in Higher Education: Marketing Example
ProjectAbstract: Cal Poly Pomona partners with San Francisco State University to develop a tiered, adaptable framework for integrating AI into business education. This project proposes a customizable, adaptable, and tiered framework for AI integration, desgined to provide comprehensive, curriculum-embedded AI training with hands-on, applied opportunities to leverage AI in for marketing. The project will provide comprehensive AI education resources, including courseware, teaching materials, course and program designs, and implementation strategies.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Saddleback College AI for Language Acquisition
ProjectAbstract: This project integrates AI into language instruction to enhance learning for diverse students across ESL, English, Reading, Sign Language, and International Languages. It will analyze student AI use, develop best practices for ethical and effective integration, and pilot classroom applications. Through workshops and interdisciplinary collaboration, the project will impact numerous students and faculty while producing OER resources.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Natural Language Processing Tool to Analyze Lower-division Chemistry Course Evaluations
ProjectAbstract: CSUMB partners with UCLA to use Natural Language Processing (NLP) to analyze student evaluations of teaching in lower-division chemistry courses. The NLP model aims to: (1) identify areas for curricular improvement, (2) compare data quality across diverse student populations, and (3) uncovercorrelations between student sentiments and outcomes.  By providing data-driven insights to support tailored teaching strategies, it will enhance inclusive instruction and student success.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectAbstract: This project aims to develop an AI literacy framework for courses involving quantitative experimentation.  This project seeks to advance AI literacy across diverse educational contexts and to providean instructional opportunity to establish an equitable understanding about the application of AI, regardless of the level of an individual’s prior exposure. A pilot engineering course will integrate AI use in research, data analysis, and technical writing while addressing ethical implications. Materials and assessments will be shared as OER.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: E-GAISE: Ethical Generative AI in Undergraduate Computer Science Education
ProjectAbstract: This project will develop GenAI-focused curricular materials to prepare students for an AI-driven workforce. Emphasizing AI literacy and ethics, the project will adapt lessons from the university’s Graduate Certificate in Ethical AI to undergraduate courses. This data-driven and iterative process, conducted in partnership with students, aims to emphasize AI literacy and ethical AI practices both in the classroom and beyond.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Acquiring math prerequisites efficiently and scalably with AI
ProjectAbstract: UCSD partners with San Diego City College to expand an AI platform to improve student progress in preparatory mathematics, where backgrounds vary widely. Building on a successful pilot, the project will enhance individualized learning through adaptive models and computer vision for real-time feedback. It aims to create scalable methods applicable to other foundational courses.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Addressing Generative AI Literacy Gaps in Gateway Writing and Mathematics Courses
ProjectAbstract: Cal Poly Maritime partners with UC Santa Cruz and UC Davis to examine how AI-integrated assignments in gateway writing and math courses affect students’ critical thinking, writing, and quantitative reasoning. Through surveys and longitudinal research, the study explores AI’s impact on learning, ethics, and pedagogy to promote equitable, AI-literate education and improve student preparedness and retention. The goal is to promote AI-literate educational equity in gateway courses, helping students to feel more successful and prepared in their college career.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Improving student engagement and outcomes equitably with course-specific open-sourced AI-tutors
ProjectAbstract: UCSD, partnering with Cal State San Marcos, Palomar College, San Diego City College, and San Diego State University, will leverage SmartLearning Hub to develop AI tutors for eight courses in AI Literacy, Biology, and Computer Programming, plus a faculty workshop. These customizable, open-source tutors will deliver interactive, personalized learning experiences. The project will engage instructors across California higher education and rigorously assess the tutors’ effectiveness in enhancing learning and mitigating disparities in different contexts.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Peer & AI Review + Reflection (PAIRR) in Writing Instruction
ProjectAbstract: UC Davis partners with CSU Bakersfield, Glendale Community College, College Of Marin, Sacramento State, Cal Poly Maritime, Los Angeles Mission College, American River College to use generative AI to strengthen writing skills, AI literacy, and metacognition. Building on a 2023?"24 pilot, it integrates peer and AI feedback with critical reflection and revision. This intervention enhances metacognition and the human relationships that motivate students to learn.
CountiesServed: Kern; Los Angeles; Marin; Sacramento; Solano; Yolo

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Across-the-curriculum AI-based personalized assistants to support student success in engineering
ProjectAbstract: UC Riverside partners with Norco College and Cal Poly Pomona to develop adaptive software to to 1) improve mastery of domain knowledge among engineering students, 2) improve student outcomes for all groups, and 3) reduce equity gaps. The adaptive software will take the form of a personalized assistant that coordinates content knowledge expected of students throughout their college careers, including for transfer students. The software will deliver content in relation to individual student’s’ actual learning behavior, thus providing them with personalized learning and review tasks.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Equitable AI Alliance: Empowering Students through Equitable AI Education
ProjectAbstract: San Diego State University partners with UC San Diego and the San Diego Community College District to promote equitable access to AI education through three activities: AI needs assessment, AI literacy education, and AI access. By developing micro-credentials and shared AI tools, the Alliance will bridge the digital divide, enhance career readiness, and model scalable, inclusive AI education across institutions.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Enhancing Academic Writing and Digital Literacy with an AI Coach
ProjectAbstract: UC Irvine partners with Cal State Fullerton and the North Orange County Community College District to advance PapyrusAI, a tool that guides students in planning and revising academic writing through AI-assisted prompts.  This project will refine the platform, develop faculty resources, and expand use across first-year and disciplinary writing. The project aims to engage 25% of writing instructors at participating institutions and sustain access across California institutions.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Animate Math Concepts in Engineering Education using Large Language Models
ProjectAbstract: This project  uses generative AI to create Python-based animations that visualize complex engineering and physics concepts. By transforming abstract theories into dynamic visualizations, students gain deeper, more intuitive understanding.  In addition, the project aims to fine-tune large language models withteaching materials and establish an online platform for student Q&A and feedback collection.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Creating a Framework for Valued Learning Outcomes in 2030
ProjectAbstract: This project reimagines assessment design in the age of generative AI. Rather than restricting AI use, the team will apply backward design and adapt AAC&U VALUE rubrics in critical thinking and information literacy to reflect skills needed in an AI-infused world. The project aims to pilot revised outcomes and share open educational resources for equitable learning. Research findings and developed materials will be published within the higher education community or made available as open educational resources (OER).

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: SpartanAI: Elevating Course Design with Faculty and Student-Centric AI Agent
ProjectAbstract: This project develops SpartanAI, a scalable machine learning tool that provides secure, customizable course content analysis and AI-driven feedback based on student insights and instructional design principles. This project supports faculty by offering equitable, timely course design guidance and improving teaching quality through data-informed feedback. It partners with QualityMatters, a leading nonprofit in course quality assurance, to guide SpartanAI's development.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: ELEVATE: Enhancing Learning Experiences Via AI TEchniques
ProjectAbstract: This project will integrate AI tutors across disciplines to enhance learning and advance educational equity. By refactoring courses to include AI-driven support, the project will generate lasting impact for students and faculty. Combining computational thinking and prompt engineering, this project aims to model scalable, equitable AI integration. This initiative promises to advance pedagogical practiceand educational equity, potentially reshaping how institutions nationwide utilize AI to foster student success.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Developing and Testing the "Build Your Career Pathway" AI Chatbot at CSU Dominguez Hills and East Los Angeles College
ProjectAbstract: This project partners with East Los Angeles College to develop an AI chatbot to support student career development. Using regional education and workforce data, the chatbot will provide personalized, multilingual, and culturally relevant guidance. Integrated into curricula and tested in classrooms, it will help students build resumes, explore careers, and improve job readiness.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: SMC & GCC SOAR (Strategies for Optimal AI Resilience)
ProjectAbstract: This project partners Santa Monica College with Glendale Community College to equip faculty to integrate AI into teaching while aligning with diversity, equity, and inclusion principles. Through a virtual academy, dicipline-embedded AI coaches, and a faculty Community of Practice, the project aims to create research-driven, scalable and shareable models for effective AI adoption across community colleges..

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Titan Research Immersion: Empowering Diversity in Chip Design
ProjectAbstract: This project introduces students to AI-assisted chip design through an 8-week immersive experience and a year-long research program. Using open-access tools, first and second year undergraduate students will gain hands-on experience in generative AI for semiconductors. The project will also create an OER to integrate AI-driven chip design into engineering courses.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Student Innovators Teaching Old Projects New Tricks (AI-PBL)
ProjectAbstract: This project partners Sac State with UC Davis and Folsom Lake College to pilot AI-enhanced project-based learning (PBL) in engineering education. By integrating AI tools, students will actively explore and solve real-world problems, fostering critical thinking and equity through personalized support. This collaborative effort ensures rigorous evaluation and continuous improvement of the pilot.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Empowering Rural Education: Generative AI and Student-Centered Learning at College of the Siskiyous
ProjectAbstract: This project develops a scalable model for AI literacy in a rural-remote setting that helps both academic and CTE faculty integrate AI into classrooms. Following a needs assessment survey, instructors will complete AI training and design AI-enhanced modules for classroom use. After classroom testing and student feedback, a guide will be published describing best practices for integration of AI into education in rural-serving contexts. The guide and all modules with be broadly shared as open educational resources (OER).

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: AI-Assisted Assessment to Award Credit for Prior Learning (A4CPL)
ProjectAbstract: This project partners LACCD with UC San Diego to develop and test an AI-driven assessment tool to support equitable Credit for Prior Learning (CPL) for Fire Protection. The tool will evaluate prior knowledge, adapt to diverse learner backgrounds, and generate individualized feedback.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Collaborative AI Integration in STEM Education
ProjectAbstract: This project develops and validates collaborative mathematical tasks integrating generative AI (genAI) to foster teamwork, critical thinking, and equitable learning in STEM. It will explore how AI-integrated tasks support diverse students, improve prompt design and student-AI interaction, and produce classroom guidelines for effective genAI use.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: Revolutionizing STEM Education: Integrating AI and Virtual Reality to Enhance Learning and Engagement
ProjectAbstract: This project partners with Sierra College to integrate AI and Virtual Reality (VR) to enhance Physics and Biology instruction. Through immersive VR simulations and an AI-driven assistant, students will explore key concepts and receive adaptive, real-time feedback. The project aims to improve learning outcomes, engagement, and accessibility in STEM education.

AgencyDept: Governor’s Office of Land Use and Climate Innovation
ProjectTitle: AI-Assistance in Lower Division Chemistry Laboratory Course Curriculum
ProjectAbstract: This project integrates the AI-assisted platform Stemble into UC Irvine’s lower-division chemistry labs to enhance student learning. The project has two objectives: (1) to evaluate how real-time AI feedback during lab sessions supports learning and (2) to compare the quality of student resubmissions after receiving AI + TA versus TA-only feedback. It also explores the ethical impact of AI on TA to student interactions and develops guidance for broader implementation.

ProjectTitle: UCLA/Westwood Zero Emission Transit Service Expansion: Deploying Wireless Charging at Scale
ProjectAbstract: Fully electrifies UCLA bus fleets, adds eight ZEBs, and installs static and dynamic wireless charging in partnership with CALSTART and Electreon.

ProjectTitle: Bringing Easy Ticketing Solutions to the Coachella Valley
ProjectAbstract: Implements an open-loop payment system on all SunLine vehicles to improve rider access and reduce operational costs.

ProjectTitle: Cross Valley Express: Kings ? Tulare County Regional Bus and Capital Infrastructure Plan
ProjectAbstract: Creates a regional bus network linking Visalia, Hanford, and Lindsay with eight ZEBs, 40-mile express service, and BRT on SR-63 with dedicated lanes.
Builds two new service and inspection tracks, doubling capacity and enabling two new round trips on the IEOC and San Bernardino lines.

ProjectTitle: Santa Barbara County Charging Forward Project ? Advancing Clean Mobility for the Central Coast
RecipientName: Santa Barbara County Association of Governments (SBCAG)
ProjectAbstract: Procures 23 ZEBs, adds fast chargers, launches BRT on SR-135 with contactless fares, and builds new operations facilities with solar and battery storage.

ProjectTitle: Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit District (SMART) Rail and Pathway Corridor Project
ProjectAbstract: Extends SMART rail to Healdsburg with new track, stations, freight spurs, PTC, and a parallel bike/ped path built to Great Redwood Trail standards.
Installs a CBTC system using Wi-Fi and cellular for real-time control, improving reliability, reducing delays, and supporting major housing growth along transit corridors.

ProjectTitle: Bridging Rail Initiatives, Technology, and Education (BRITE)
RecipientName: San Joaquin Regional Rail Commission and San Joaquin Joint Powers Authority (SJJRC and SJJPA)
ProjectAbstract: Advances grade separation, crossovers, the Madera HSR station, and a workforce training program to expand passenger rail and support future HSR operations.

ProjectTitle: Enhancing Ridership Through System Improvements, Public Engagement, and Workforce Development

ProjectTitle: Deployment of a Steam-Generating Heat Pump for Deep Industrial Decarbonization and Improvement to Grid Operations
ProjectAbstract: With Skyven Technologies, Inc. for a $5,000,000.00 federal cost share grant to deploy a Skyven Arcturus open-cycle mechanical vapor recompression steam-generating heat pump at a CA-based industrial facility and adopting staff’s determination that this action is exempt from CEQA.

ProjectTitle: Demonstrating Hybrid Glass Furnace Technology to Support the Decarbonization of the United States Glass Industry
ProjectAbstract: With Gallo Glass Company for a $5,000,000 federal cost share grant to deploy a new electric-driven glass melting equipment as part of an overall shift of one of Gallo Glass’ natural gas operated glass furnaces to a hybrid solution.

ProjectTitle: Community Alliance for Direct Air Capture
RecipientName: The Regents of the University of California, Berkeley
ProjectAbstract: With UC Berkeley, Berkeley Law for a $300,000 federal cost share grant to conduct a detailed feasibility study of a community-centered Direct Air Capture (DAC) Hub situated in the southern part of California’s San Joaquin Valley. CALDAC will pioneer an innovative model for community partnership and co-production from feasibility phase to hub design, construction, ownership, and operation.

RecipientName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectAbstract: The Conservancy provided a $1,500,000 grant to the California Department of Parks and Recreation to conduct planning and studies, and preparing designs, environmental review, and permit applications for increasing lower-cost accommodations at Silver Strand State Beach in San Diego County.

The Conservancy granted $865,000 to the County of Santa Cruz to prepare technical and feasibility documents, plans, environmental review documents, and permit applications to construct low cost cabins and associated amenities within Greyhound Rock County Park in Santa Cruz County.
