ProjectTitle: Clear Lake Hitch Habitat Improvement Planning and Design in Cole Creek
ProjectAbstract: The Cole Creek Restoration Project aims to restore 1.55 miles of spawning habitat for the Clear Lake Hitch (CLH), a state-listed species under consideration for Federal Endangered Species Act protection. Funding will be used for planning, engineering, and design to improve flows, reduce sediment barriers, and address flooding. Its goal is to create a community-supported restoration plan to enhance CLH fish passage, spawning, juvenile migration, and long-term ecological resilience.

ProjectTitle: BIPOC Coastal Research * Study Abroad Program
ProjectAbstract: This project will fund a research program to 15 college students pursuing environmental careers. Experiential learning opportunities occur over 32 weeks of student immersion among southern California coastal watersheds and habitats. Will also provide funding to acquire two Hybrid SUV vehicles to transport youth.

ProjectTitle: Northern California Tribal Youth Outdoor Education Program Transportation
ProjectAbstract: This project will fund a youth program that will teach Indigenous traditional knowledge through camps, dam removal, restoration tours, rafting trips and Traditional Ecological Knowledge events, and will serve 200 youth. Will also provide funding to acquire a clean vehicle to transport youth.

ProjectTitle: Salted Roots Rising Leader Youth and Environmental Stewardship Programs
ProjectAbstract: This project will support the Rising Leaders Youth and Environmental Stewardship program and serve approximately 300 youth in Alameda County. Program will connect participants to the ocean and environmental stewardship through the world of surfing and will provide ocean education, leadership development and cultural surfing experiences. Will also provide funding to acquire a clean vehicle to transport youth.

This project will fund the Explore Outdoors After School Program to provide underserved youth from Valencia Park Elementary and Porter Elementary Schools with outdoor and cultural experiences. Program will serve approximately 200 youth over two years.

ProjectTitle: Youth Leadership & Exploration of Natural and Cultural Resources by Bicycle
RecipientName: Santa Barbara Bicycle Coalition (dba MOVE Santa Barbara County)
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide bicycle education and 12-18 bicycling trips to natural and cultural resources and will serve 24 youth, ages of 14-26. Locations include beaches, dunes, parks, museums, and government buildings.

This project will provide educational and recreational experiences in National Forests and State Parks, and will serve approximately 100 youth in Stanislaus County. Activities will include biking, hiking, kayaking, camping, and learning about the cultural significance of the indigenous tribes that stewarded the area.

ProjectTitle: Natural and Cultural Access Program for Central Valley Incarcerated Youth
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide weekly field trips to natural and cultural resources for up to 100 youth who have been, or who are at risk for being, impacted by incarceration. Program also includes two longer excursions per year. Will also provide funding to acquire a vehicle to transport youth.

ProjectTitle: Outdoor Leadership Expeditions for Girls and Gender Expansive Youth
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide six outdoor summer expeditions in backpacking, kayaking, rock-climbing in the California wilderness, and will serve youth ages 11-17. Participants receive up to 300 hours of environmental programming for leadership skills development. Sites may include Half Moon Bay, Point Reyes National Seashore, Sonoma Coast, and Sierra National Forest.

ProjectTitle: In-School Programs - Young Lives Transformed Through Science
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide scientific, hands-on coastal field trips as well as living lab field trips, and will serve over 6,000 youth. Students will gain practical knowledge and appreciation for their environment and heritage, fostering a sense of stewardship as they recognize how actions in the urban watershed affect the coastal ecology.

This project will provide approximately 30 trips to provide access to natural and cultural resources, with a focus on educational and outdoor activities. The project will serve approximately 1,220 youth during the 15-month program.

ProjectTitle: City Surf Project’s Alumni Program: Growing Young Leaders Through Surfing
ProjectAbstract: This project will fund an apprenticeship program for City Surf Project (CSP) youth alumni. During the one-year program, the alumni youth will work in outdoor recreation in natural areas as surf coaches. They will work on team building and independence building retreats, health and wellness activities, and support case management. The project will provide equitable access to the ocean, enabling youth to build physical and mental wellbeing, community, and connection to nature. Project will serve 17 transitional aged youths with previous CSP experience.

ProjectTitle: Fostering Environmental Awareness Through High School Education and Research (FEATHER)
ProjectAbstract: This project will implement a 12-month, in-school program to provide 15 trips to natural resources, where youth will participate in hands-on science and learn about research, leadership, and college-readiness while connecting with natural ecosystems.  Project will serve 500 high school students from underserved Central Coast communities.

This project will provide approximately 90 field trips to experience natural and cultural resources and will serve approximately 300 youth. Will also provide funding to acquire four 12-passenger clean energy vans to transport youth to field trip locations.

ProjectTitle: Revisioning Education through Student Led Outdoor Leadership Training
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 20 outdoor, overnight field trips to natural resources over a two year period, and will serve approximately 500 youth. These trips will include hiking, camping and nature exploration actives. Trips may include a 3-day backpacking trip to Hetch Hetchy, a 2-night snow skills trip to Lake Tahoe, and a 3-day camping trip to Sequoia. Project will also provide funding to acquire two clean energy 8-passenger vehicles to help transport the youth on these trips.

ProjectTitle: Increasing Access to the Outdoors for Rural Central Valley Youth
ProjectAbstract: This project will fund a two year community leadership program that offers integrated leadership, literacy and outdoor programming to each student. The program will include classroom time and outdoor program time which will include overnight camping, backpacking or cabins stays. Project will serve youth ages 14-18 from two neighboring, rural, underserved communities in the Central Valley: Dos Palos and Firebaugh.

ProjectTitle: Youth & Young Adult Forestry and Fire Training Program
RecipientName: The Urban Association of Forestry and Fire Professionals, Inc. DBA the Forestry and Fire Recruitment Program
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 35 young adults ages 18-26 with 256-384 hours of paid training and leadership programming over an 8-12 week programming cycle. Up to 50% of this time will be spent out in the field performing wildfire prevention projects and earning certifications.

ProjectTitle: STAR Youth Camping, Field Trips and other Nature and Cultural Activities
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide approximately 12 day trips to natural and/or cultural resources, as well as weekend camping trips a State Park, and will serve 20 -25 youth ages 9-14. The program also includes academic tutoring, life skills classes focused on drug abuse and gang intervention, bullying prevention, self-esteem enhancement, peer pressure management, and educational enrichment activities. The program allocates 40% of the time to tutoring and academic activities and 60% to program activities including community service and outdoor experiences accessing natural and/or cultural resources.

RecipientName: Central Coast Salmon Enhancement DBA Creek Lands Conservation
ProjectAbstract: This project will implement an immersive, 2-day outdoor environmental/climate literacy program. The program will be bi-lingual (English/Spanish) and free of charge for approximately 384 youth, ages 10 to 18. There are four 2-day sessions held every season from Fall 2025 to Winter 2027. Will also provide funding to acquire a clean vehicle to transport participants.

RecipientName: Social Advocates for Youth, San Diego, Inc.
ProjectAbstract: This project will expand existing programs that will connect 60-80 youth with natural and cultural resources. The project will fund 8-12 excursions during the 15-month program to cultural and natural resources, to Chollas Creek, Chicano Park, Mission Regional Park, Barona Cultural Center and Museum, and the Sycuan Band of Kumeyaay Nation Pow-Wow. The program will allow youth to participate in the Youth-Led Participatory Action Research framework and will include youth-led systematic research, planning and evaluation, community organizing, and youth advisory boards.

ProjectTitle: Akuutet Learning Nursery Outdoor Youth Leadership Program
ProjectAbstract: This project will fund three, 12-week nature based program sessions (120 hours - 75% in the field) and up to 5 days of camping for high school aged youth to learn about native plant cultivation and uses, interpretation of outdoor experiences, and the role of fire in an ecosystem.
This project will provide three, 12-day summer camping sessions in the Sequoia National Forest and will provide 250 boys and young men from Southern California camp experience.

RecipientName: Boys & Girls Clubs of San Francisco
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide enriching overnight summer camp experiences in the majestic redwood forests of Mendocino County at Camp Mendocino and will serve over 2,000 youth from San Franciso  communities. Each session will integrate outdoor adventures with structured support group activities tailored to foster leadership and personal growth.

This project will provide day and overnight field trips focusing on outdoor educational, experiential, and cultural activities for approximately 315 K-12 students at the Anawakalmekak International University Preparatory of North America charter school in South Los Angeles. Program incorporates leadership development for 24 youth, including internships for four youth interns ages 18-26. Will also provide funding to acquire two clean vans to transport youth.

ProjectTitle: Edventure Youth: Advancing Environmental Access, Leadership and Conservation
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide outdoor excursions for approximately 500 youth in the Central Valley. Excursions will focus on leadership development, conservation practices, increased ecological awareness and cultural heritage. Students will also be exposed to career and educational pathways in agriculture, environmental science, outdoor education, youth recreation, social work and cultural studies.

This project will provide 48 field trips to the Upper Newport Bay Ecological Reserve and will serve 1,412 youth from Orange County. Field trips will combine classroom learning and outdoor activities. Project also includes paid internships to lead youth field trips.

ProjectTitle: Modern Youth Internship Academies - Mentoring and Leadership Components
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide approximately 11 field trips to natural and cultural resources in Humbolt and Del Norte Counties and will serve  approximately 771 youth. Twenty youth interns will receive mentoring to plan, organize, and lead field trips and present one youth-led conference.

ProjectTitle: San Bernardino Healthy in Nature Equity (SHiNE) Program
ProjectAbstract: This project will fund a 12-month field trip program for 500 youth ages 13-20 from the San Bernardino Unified School District. Program will include 25 events to locations such as Garden Workshops at Garden of Health, Overnight Trips to Joshua Tree, Snow Activity in Big Bear, Kayaking in San Diego, Surfing in San Clemente, and 17 Day trips to area parks and natural resource areas.

ProjectTitle: Family Harvest Farm - Natural Resource Workforce & Leadership Development for Foster Youth
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide field trips to approximately 70 youth and provide apprenticeships to approximately seven transition-age foster youth at the organic Family Harvest Farm (FHF) in Pittsburg. Program includes outdoor education workshops, field trips, cooking classes, outdoor recreation, healthy eating, farming techniques, and youth leadership development.

ProjectTitle: Community Fellows: Youth Leaders in Coastal Conservation
RecipientName: University of California at San Diego > Division of Extended Studies
ProjectAbstract: This project will fund a 12-week, college level ocean literacy course for San Diego youth. The online course will be paired with in-person experiences to various natural sites in the San Diego area. Youth can also apply for two intensive summer programs, Conservation Leadership Naturalists and Conservation Leadership Divers, which offers dive certification, as well as a trip to Santa Catalina Island. Youth will also participate in paid fellowships.

This project will fund a week-long, overnight summer camp program at Happy Trails' 135-acre site, located between the Sierra Pelona Mountains and the San Gabriel Mountains near Antelope Valley. This project will serve approximately 1,000 Los Angeles County foster youth. Camp activities include swimming, archery, horseback riding, canoeing, hiking, stargazing. Junior leaders are trained to support camp counselors and receive valuable job skills and early career experience.

ProjectTitle: Reconnecting Southeastern San Diego Youth to Nature
ProjectAbstract: This project will fund two Green Team cohorts of 14 high school students in Southeastern San Diego. Students will create and install a half-acre Kumeyaay ethnobotanical garden complete with native plants, walking trails, signage, artwork, a learning/teaching station, and a traditional Kumeyaayewaa thatched shelter in the 4-acre EarthLab Climate Action Park, an outdoor classroom managed and maintained by Groundwork. Youth will participate in day-trips to cultural and natural resources and overnight camping. Provide funding to acquire 8-passenger clean vehicle to transport youth participants.

ProjectTitle: AADAP SAFE Youth: Substance Awareness, Fitness, and Education Program
RecipientName: Asian American Drug Abuse Program, Inc. (AADAP)
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide outdoor experiences to approximately 200 youth in Los Angeles County, including overnight and day trips to local, state, and national park areas. Will also provide funding to acquire an electric van to transport youth and deliver program supplies and educational materials for community outreach and activities.

ProjectTitle: Youth Belong LA: A Social and Cultural Hub Enhancing Belonging and Wellness for LA Youth
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide weekly classroom engagements and field trips to natural and cultural sites and will serve approximately 90 youth (ages 12-18). Will also provide funding to acquire an 8-passenger vehicle to transport youth.

ProjectTitle: Bridging Culture and Place Orange County (OC)
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide workshops and field trips for youth where they will learn about marine life, conservation efforts, develop workforce development skills and access career pathways. Project will serve approximately 180 transitional-aged youth in Orange County to provide access to natural, significant historical and indigenous resources in Southern California.

ProjectTitle: Crissy Field Center High School Youth Leadership Program
ProjectAbstract: This project will connect high school students to outdoor excursions and learning in state and national parks. The program offers comprehensive training and hands-on work within their communities to empower young people to identify social and environmental issues they care about and develop actionable plans.

RecipientName: San Joaquin River Parkway & Conservation Trust
ProjectAbstract: This project will expand an existing program which connects 40 participants from the Madera and Fresno Unified High Schools to the San Joaquin Parkway through field trips, training in leadership and outdoor skills. Will also provide funding to acquire electric vehicles and a charging station to transport youth.

ProjectTitle: Los Angeles-Mono Lake Youth Outdoor Experiences Program, Phase II Mono Basin Outdoor Education Center Improvements
ProjectAbstract: This project will increase capacity for the Los Angeles-Mono Lake Outdoor Experiences Program, by funding the installation of an outdoor kitchen, dining area shade, ADA improvements, two outdoor bathhouses, 2-3 covered group sleeping platforms, a rainwater/gray water system, and educational landscaping featuring healthy food, indigenous plants and 100’ of improved fencing. The program annually provides approximately 250 youth from the Los Angeles area with 5-day outdoor educational and recreational programs at Mono Lake.

ProjectTitle: Lion's Pride Youth Outdoor Access Program
RecipientName: East Bay Asian Local Development Corporation (EBALDC)
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide youth, ages 5-26, field trips to greater Bay Area and California cultural and natural resources. Youth will experience the outdoors and learn about natural and cultural history, including local indigenous histories and practices. Youth will develop leadership skills through helping design seasonal programming and field trip experiences.

RecipientName: San Joaquin County Office of Education
ProjectAbstract: Project serving 2400 4th grade students with trips to Durham Ferry Outdoor Education Center where they will experience hiking trails, ponds, meadows, and a working farm. High School and college age youth will be hired to provide leadership for the 4th graders.

This project will provide an internship program to approximately 200 youth, age 14 to 21, in nature-based paid work experience such as habitat restoration. For 50 of the youth, it will also include two outdoor field trips and an overnight camping trip to destinations in or around San Francisco, such as Muir Woods, Alcatraz Island, Angel Island, or TomKat Ranch.

ProjectTitle: Creating Access to Eco-Opportunities and Green Careers for Youth
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide a 14-week environmental education and youth climate leader program to approximately 60 at-risk youth ages 16-24 from Compton and Canoga Park. Program includes in-class and outdoor learning, guest speaker talks, field trips to regional natural and cultural resources, and localized Environmental Service Learning Projects.

ProjectTitle: Expanding the Santa Lucia Watershed Education Program to Underresourced Communities.
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide experiential watershed-based field trips for 20 classes of elementary, middle, and high students (3rd-12th grade) in Monterey and the surrounding counties. The project will provide teachers, materials and transportation for 600 students to participate in educational activities in the Carmel River Watershed and old-growth Redwood ecosystem in Potrero Canyon.

This project will provide leadership development opportunities, healthy life skills mentorship, and wilderness immersion through six hiking day trips and two overnight camping trips. Project will serve approximately 150 Latinx youth from the Heritage Valley communities of Santa Paula, Ojai, Filmore, and Pir.

ProjectTitle: Camp for All: A Free Summer Camp Outdoor Educational Wilderness Experience for Underserved Youth in Los Angeles
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide day camp and hikes with enriching STEAM activities to 960 youth from the Los Angeles area.

This project will expand the South LA Youth Explorers program by providing four overnight nature retreats and 18 field trips to museums, historical sites, beaches, parks, community gardens and other sites of interest, and will serve approximately 100-150 youth between the ages of 7-26. Will also provide funding to acquire a clean vehicle to transport youth.

ProjectTitle: Empowering Youth Through Nature: The Black Neighborhood
ProjectAbstract: This project will serve approximately 1,050 youth through overnight camping trips, mental health hikes, day camps and leadership development program. Will also provide funding to acquire a clean vehicle to transport youth.

This project provide approximately 130 guided fly fishing trips, four fly fishing clinics, and six outdoor educational experiences for youth living in the Northern California Central Valley.	 Will serve 465 youth participants and teach them about fly fishing and their local outdoor environment.

This project will provide 20-25 field trips, including overnight backpacking trips and day hikes in the Ventana and Silver Peak Wilderness areas. The program also includes a pre and post trip classroom session and will serve 200-250 youth.

ProjectTitle: Grip Discovery Camp - Cultivating community, connecting with nature, and pedaling into the future
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 160 youth a full week of summer camp that focuses on using bicycles on daily field trips on bike trails to local natural and cultural resources. 16 youth will be given scholarships for a three-month after school program where they will plan a reunion and ways to keep youth safe and engaged on bikes.

ProjectTitle: From Streets to Peaks: Northern California Outdoor Excursions for Urban Homeless Youth
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide outdoor excursions throughout Northern California, aiming to promote healthy lifestyle choices through activities like hiking, kayaking, mountain biking, and beach trips and will serve approximately 80 urban homeless youth ages 18-24.

ProjectTitle: Accessible Environmental Education for Title-I Schools with Project AWE
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide approximately 200 STEM-based field trips at a historic, non-working dairy for 2nd to 5th grade students in the Sacramento area. Students will engage in hands-on activities involving topics such as hydroponic gardening, beekeeping, composting and vermiculture and water conservation in partnership with the Sacramento Area Sewer District.

This project will provide approximately 10 excursions to natural resources includes camping trips to lakes, waterfalls, beaches, hiking, kayaking, and environmental education, and will serve approximately 315 youth. Will also provide funding to acquire a clean vehicle passenger-van to transport youth participants

This project will provide 40 single-day surf camps, serving 25 youth at each camp for a total of 1,000 youth ranging in age from 5-20. The program will also include mindfulness practice and emotional health exercises, substance abuse prevention lectures, and water safety education, as well as a beach cleanup day to mitigate coastal pollution, foster social responsibility and understanding of environmental issues. The project will include 3 paid interns. Will also provide funding to acquire a clean energy vehicle to provide transportation for the youth.

ProjectTitle: Two Feathers Youth Community Access Program
RecipientName: Two Feathers Native American Family Services
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide a minimum of 50 natural and cultural experiences to American Indian youth over the course of one year and will serve 40 youth. Experiences include outdoor activities, cultural programs, cultural activities in outdoor spaces, and two large scale cultural exchange programs. Will also provide funding to acquire four clean vehicles to transport youth.

This project will implement a ten-week, annual field trip series to McKenzie Preserve in the City of Fresno, with additional field trips to Mariposa Creek Parkway and Stookey Preserve in Mariposa County. This project will serve approximately 950 youth from Fresno and Mariposa counties and is a partnership with the Southern Sierra Miwuk Nation and the Ethos Youth Center . Programming will include STEAM curriculum, environmental stewardship and cultural resource education.

This project will provide environmental programing and outdoor experiences to natural resources that include trips to lakes, creeks, parks, green spaces, and outdoor gardening and will serve approximately 75 youth, aged 16-26.

ProjectTitle: Empowering Youth: Restorative Outdoor Education, Green Jobs, and Recreational Adventures
ProjectAbstract: This project will fund one paid summer crew and one paid school year crew from the Hayward/San Lorenzo areas to engage in conservation and outdoor recreational activities and will serve approximately 20 youth ages 14-26. Will also provide funding to acquire a clean truck for transporting youth crews and supplies to project sites. Participants will engage in formal conservation skill training and regular outdoor recreation activities.

ProjectTitle: Summer Search: Access to Environmental Education, Leadership-Building and Outdoor Experiences for Bay Area Youth
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide outdoor experiential learning for approximately 32 Bay Area high school students ages 15-16. Youth-lead programming will range from 14-21 days with students participating in activities such as sea kayaking, camping, backpacking and white water rafting, in the Bay Area, Central Valley and Sierra Mountains.

This project will take approximately 225 youth, ages 5-19 from Santa Ana on field trips and camps to places including the Santa Ana Zoo and Orange County Museum of Arts, provide classroom training in safety, basic outdoor skills and trip planning. Project also includes purchase of a clean vehicle to transport youth.

This project will provide a year-long paid internship in which Sacramento high school students gain skills and experience in sustainable agriculture, workplace readiness, and individualized self-development. The internship consists of multiple pieces: weekly work hours in their extensive school gardens, field trips to local ag lands and natural resource sites, visits from industry guest speakers, consistent leadership development opportunities, and weekly workforce development learning.

This project will provide 8-12 immersive nature excursions, including overnight nature trips to national, state, and regional parks and natural areas in California and 18 monthly nature hikes in local natural areas. Will serve 165 to 220  youth ages 10 to 26. Additionally, 15-20 youth ages 17-26 will participate in a 14-month Outdoor Equity Youth Leadership Internship.

This project will provide youth-guided bicycle rides, public transportation adventures to the coast and cultural resources, and field trips to natural and cultural areas. The project includes approximately 54 activities over a 12-month period with natural or cultural resources that will reach approximately 1,400 youth in the communities of El Monte and South El Monte.

RecipientName: Sacramento Native American Health Center, Inc.
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 100 youth access to natural and cultural resources, including overnight multi-day trips to Kumeyaay lands, Chaw’se Indian Grinding Rock, the foothills of Amador county on Miwok/Me-wuk and Nisenan lands, and Yosemite National Park on Miwok/Me-wuk and Paiute lands. Program will also include working in a community garden and assisting with developing social marketing material for the program.

This project will provide backpacking opportunities, monthly hikes and intergenerational field trips in the East Bay area as well as statewide, to young men of color (18-24) from the East Oakland area to engage them in natural and cultural resources and to develop leadership through youth-led project design and selection.

This project will serve approximately 600 youth ages 6-18 and 5-8 youth interns ages 17-26. Youth interns will learn the environmental education pathway and lead the student participants in watershed education activities and field trips to urban and regional parks around Richmond. Project includes development aspect of creating a culture and ecology mural at Booker T. Anderson Community Center.

ProjectTitle: CAPK Youth Centers Nature and Culture Program
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide approximately 30 field trips to national and state parks, cultural monuments and historical sites, in addition to other structured activities and educational components that enhance participants' understanding of local ecosystems and cultural heritage. Will serve up to 240 youth and focus on fostering environmental stewardship, cultural awareness, and leadership skills. Will also provide funding to acquire  a clean vehicle to transport youth.

ProjectTitle: Teapot City Sprouts: Expeditions & Outdoor After-school Care
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide funding for a year-long Environmental Education & Art program, including after school field trips for 102 elementary school students. Program will also include 12 paid internships to high school participants at a local botanical herb garden in Los Angeles, as well as trips to locations such as Huntington Gardens, Stoneview Nature Center, Natural History Museum Garden, LA Arboretum, Malibu Lagoon & Coldwater Canyon Park.

ProjectTitle: /n’e k’ut xo-yash na-lhee/ “Our Youth Together On the Land” (Wailaki)
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 9 outings to culturally significant natural areas throughout Wailaki ancestral territory in rural Northern California and will serve up to 125 Native youth from tribal communities in Northern Mendocino and Humboldt Counties. Youth participants will gain the lived experience of connecting with places and nature and education on history, landscape, animals and plants, and ancestral language. Will also provide funding to acquire one clean vehicle for transporting youth.

ProjectTitle: Junior Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary Stewards (JSS) Program
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 10 field trips to natural and cultural resources in Monterey Bay through afterschool programming and will serve approximately 50 youth in middle school. Students will participate in weekly trips where they will develop skills in data collection, journaling, art projects, and species identification.

This project will expand the existing Santa Ana River Watershed Exploration Program and provide approximately 60 field trips, supplemented with a 1 hour in-class lesson related to the field trip, and will serve approximately 2,000 youth from the Fontana and Santa Ana Unified School Districts.

This project will provide support for youth affected by trauma by providing field trips in Monterey County, as well as interacting with rescued animals and spending time on a working ranch. Will serve approximately 250 youth in Greenfield, King City, Salinas, and Soledad in Monterey County.

ProjectTitle: Experiential + Environmental Learning with Escondido Union School District
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 62 environmental education lessons and 109 nature-based experiences and will serve approximately 5,200 students, grades 3-5, from approximately 12 elementary schools within Escondido Union School District.

ProjectTitle: LA River Fellows: STEM Youth Eco-workforce Development
RecipientName: Friends of the Los Angeles River
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 35 experiences in nature and a year-long program in eco-STEM career pathways, and will serve approximately 30 student, grades 9-11, from disadvantaged communities along the Los Angeles River.

This project will provide funding to develop and deliver 18 months of new programing for 50 school age youth from Fruitvale, San Antonio and East Oakland neighborhoods in Alameda County. Program will provide 15 field trip day excursions, and overnight trip activities to natural and cultural sites across the Bay Area and surrounding regions.

This project will provide hands-on watershed learning through restoration techniques, scientific monitoring methods, and natural resource stewardship practices and will serve approximately 300 youth, ages 5 to 26. The program will also include rafting trips on the Klamath River, an overnight summer camp that incorporates a backpacking trip into the high country, field trips to conduct Fall Chinook salmon surveys on nearby creeks in the fall, and data collection trips in the spring to visit and observe migrant fish traps.

ProjectTitle: Youth Nature Access Program at Descanso Gardens
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide approximately 100 school group tours to Descanso Gardens for approximately 6,000 youth including transportation costs.

ProjectTitle: Out & About: Exploring California's Heritage & Nature
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide approximately 250 LGBTQIA+ youth, aged 18-24, access to monthly activities such as workshops, immersive excursions, and field trips to parks and culturally significant locations in Los Angeles. The program will provide a safe, empowering space for youth to learn skill-building opportunities, environmental stewardship, and cultural awareness.

This project will provide funding to hire youth, ages 18-25, as Eco-Apprentices who will build and manage an edible food garden under the Eco-Adventures program (recruiting K-12) . Cooking lessons to learn how to prepare harvested foods will also be a part of programming as well as field trips to other urban gardens.

RecipientName: Booker T. Washington Community Service Center
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide approximately 180 youth (2nd -12th grade) with 144 experiences to natural and cultural destinations including overnight excursions, daytime excursions and field trips over an 18-month period. A clean air vehicle will be purchased to provide transportation to all excursions.

ProjectTitle: ICOE - Heritage and Horizons: Natural and Cultural Resources for Migrant Youth / ICOE - Herencia y Horizontes: Recursos Naturales y Culturales para Jovenes Migrantes
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide migrant students in the Imperial Valley opportunities to learn about and visit natural and cultural resources in California. The program will provide classroom instruction and excursions to approximately fifty K-12 students. Additionally, approximately 20 students will participate in the  Student Ambassadors Environmental Leadership Project.

ProjectTitle: Camp Fresno for All: A Nature Experience for Underserved Youth
RecipientName: City of Fresno > Dept. of Parks, After School, Recreation, and Community Services (PARCS)
ProjectAbstract: This project will expand access to the existing Camp Fresno for All summer program by providing approximately 10 overnight trips and 8 day-camp trips to approximately 250 youth (ages 7-17).

ProjectTitle: Empowering Historically Marginalized Youth Through Equitable Access to Local Natural Resources
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide funding for staff support for ongoing outdoor access and gardening program. Program includes organic farming, communal meals, nature trips, food access projects, land stewardship projects, and educational workshops for 75 youth annually, as well as annual Harvest Festival. The program includes paid stipends, free transportation, and school credit at no cost to the youth participants.

ProjectTitle: Outside the Neighborhood: Equitable Community Access for WHCHC Youth
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide four field trips to natural and cultural resources in southern California with older youth serving as leaders and mentors on trips.

ProjectTitle: Aim High’s Summer Magic “Get Outdoors” Initiative
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide funding to implement a summer academic and enrichment program, including recreation, a backpacking trip, and a professional development retreat for aspiring teachers. Will serve approximately 2,111 youth.

This project will provide classroom and outdoor adventures over the span of 15 months to 150 youths to support the Corpsmember Outdoor Leadership and Adventure (COLA) program. Will develop 10 COLA Committee leaders to engage youth Corpsmembers in outdoor access through ecology awareness and adventure trips. Will also provide funding to acquire passenger van to transport youth.

This project will expand the Canyon Connections Initiative program by funding 18 youth-led initiatives to design, monitor, and construct Monarch Waystation habitat restoration sites, enhance existing trailhead gardens, and create interpretive resources for the communities of San Diego. Project will serve approximately 72 high school aged youth and provide environmental workforce opportunities.

RecipientName: Jewish Big Brothers Big Sisters of Los Angeles and the Foundation for Camp Bob Waldorf
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 850 youth, ages 7 to 17, from  under-resourced areas of Los Angeles County with 9 camping trips and 3 backpacking experiences at Camp Bob Waldorf, located on 112 acres in the foothills of the Verdugo Mountains in Glendale.

ProjectTitle: Wellness Through Nature Programming in Partnership With Migrant Farmworker Families in South Monterey County
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 66 nature experiences throughout the Monterey region, including field trips to local and state parks and beaches, kayaking, and whale watching and will serve approximately 876 youth. Will also provide funding to acquire one clean vehicle to transport youth.

ProjectTitle: Eco-Healing for Joy, Resilience and Liberation in Richmond, CA
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide at least 15 field trips, multiple workshops, and paid internships over 15 months and will serve 150 young people. Field trips will be to community farms, Bay Area outdoor recreation activities, and local environmental activism opportunities.

This project will provide 80 high school intern youths hands-on leadership and 10 environmental education opportunities and provide over 2,000 3rd-5th grade youths with 59 outdoor access opportunities over two years. The high school interns will learn about the natural and cultural history of the region and apply the knowledge to lesson plans and field trips for the elementary aged students. Interns will also have opportunities to engage in restoration and community service events on nature preserves.

ProjectTitle: ís si?'wa thús ís k?"í?'ká?'ci "may you live well in the Indian way"
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide tribal youth from 150 northern Tribal regions access to natural/cultural resources in partnership with Pit River Tribe, Winnemem Wintu Tribe, Modoc Tribe, and the Mountain Maidu Tribe. Tribal youth will be resourced, stewarded and connected with cultural sacred sites through a series of cultural camps and spiritual gatherings hosted by cultural bearers, spiritual leaders and Indigenous Rights organizers.

RecipientName: Girls Athletic Leadership Schools Los Angeles
ProjectAbstract: This project will connect 40-50 youth from the Girls Athletic Leadership School Los Angeles (GALS LA) to natural resources and nature-based activities through a 5-day camp at Pyles Camp in Sequioa National Forest.

This project will provide funding for the Sustainable Youth Internships afterschool program, which serves approximately 320 public high school students in Contra Costa and Alameda counties. Students will work as paid environmental interns to participate in workshops and outdoor trips which are divided into six ecosystem modules: forests, coastal forests, beaches, wetlands, estuaries and oceans.

ProjectTitle: South LA Rides for Hikes and Tides
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 18 nature excursions to coastal beaches, hiking trails, camping trips, and WLCAC's urban agriculture training center MudTown Farms in South Los Angeles. Project will serve approximately 250 youth ages 8-26, 40 of which are paid youth interns. Will also provide funding to acquire two clean vehicles to transport youth.

This project will provide 740 Indigenous youth with education on Traditional Knowledge, Group Peer Support, as well as 12 direct experiences with natural and cultural resources including field trips and overnight camping excursions. These activities aim to reconnect youth with their heritage, foster social-emotional learning, and reduce recidivism and substance about through immersive experiences with natural and cultural resources. Will also provide funding to acquire two clean vehicles to transport youth.

This project will provide 150 youth in Glenn County with 23 enriching, multifaceted, outdoor activities and excursions. Specific activities will include community gardening, educational sessions on sustainability, fishing clinics, hiking, kayaking, paddleboarding, canoeing, and hands-on experiences in nature. Participants will gain an understanding of healthy living, environmental stewardship, and the importance of sustainable practices.

ProjectTitle: A Place Called California: Access, Exposure, & Exploration for South Central LA Youth
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide 40 field trips (curated excursions) that integrate experiential learning into a comprehensive roster of afterschool and summer programming as well as broaden opportunities for youth leadership. Project will serve 300 youth in South Central Los Angeles.

ProjectTitle: Youth Leadership Pathway: Nurturing Healthy, Engaged, and Empowered Environmental Leaders and Advocates
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide approximately 600 youth the opportunity to go on 60 camping trips to local, regional, and national parks to reduce limited access to nature, and improve physical and mental health.

ProjectTitle: Providing Equitable Access to Natural and Cultural Resources in the Inland Empire.
RecipientName: Southern California Mountains Foundation > Urban Conservation Corps of the Inland Empire

Program will include leadership and community outreach component for all participants including 4 paid interns.

This project will fund a leadership program and provide 36 youth in the San Diego area with approximately 95 outdoor experiences and trips to local, state, and national parks. Project includes the acquisition of 2 hybrid vans that will be used to transport the youth participants. Program also includes 5 youth stipend paid internship opportunities.

ProjectTitle: Vallejo Youth Cultural And Natural Resources Access (Vallejo Youth CAN)

ProjectTitle: Youth Health, Urban Agriculture & Leadership Development Program
ProjectAbstract: This project will implement a program for 120 middle to high school age students to learn about urban agriculture and environmental stewardship, and includes a 20-week internship. Activities will include working in the urban garden and learning about gardening practices, soil health, irrigation, planting, pest control, harvesting, garden enterprise, and ongoing garden maintenance. Program also includes experiences in applied nutrition, cooking, and community engagement.

ProjectTitle: Trailblazers to a Green Tomorrow Initiative
ProjectAbstract: This project will provide programming though a combination of day camps, retreats, and ongoing weekly youth groups for 120 high school-age youth from communities in Shasta and Siskiyou counties. Will also provide funding to acquire two clean vehicles to transport youth.

This project will support the Juntos program and provide nine field trips to natural resources around the Salton Sea and will serve 10 paid youth leaders and 70 youth participants, ages 18 to 22 from communities around the Eastern Coachella Valley. ProjectAbstract: SBSS will provide California nutrition information and technical assistance to eligible older adults in the Mid-City, Echo Park, and Hollywood neighborhoods of Los Angeles as part of the SBSS education program. SBSS will offer information about nutrition, California agriculture, and food safety with regard to disaster preparedness and recovery. SBSS will work with members to ensure that all who are qualified for SFMNP will receive the benefits and incentives from partner organizations so that they may purchase produce and other California goods at local farmers markets.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Introducing eWIC and eEMNP to Bay Area Farmers Markets
ProjectAbstract: This project supports the implementation of eWIC and eFMNP at certified farmers' markets in the San Francisco Bay Area. PCFMA will provide technical support to encourage and support farmers to complete the steps required to accept eWIC and eFMNP payments for purchases. To encourage participation and purchases by eWIC and eFMNP participants, the project matches the value of their benefits up to preset limits of $15 per eWIC card eFMNP card per month, during the grant period.
CountiesServed: Alameda; Contra Costa; San Francisco; San Mateo; Santa Clara; Solano

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: North Coast Growers’ Association Nutrition Incentive expansion to WIC, FMNP, SFMNP and E-WIC Support Program
ProjectAbstract: The North Coast Growers Association (NCGA) has a well-established program dedicated to increasing the consumption of fresh and locally grown fruits and vegetables for the mutual benefit of positive health impacts for low-income and food insecure community members as well as our local small-scale farmers. NCGA is a 501 c 3 nonprofit organization with a mission of to support Humboldt County's farmers and artisan producers in building a robust and resilient local food system.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Farmers’ Market Nutrition Program (FMNP) Plus: Supporting Vulnerable Angelenos, Small-to-Mid Sized Farmers, and the California Economy
RecipientName: Sustainable Economic Enterprises of Los Angeles dba Food Access Los Angeles (SEE-LA;FALA)
ProjectAbstract: To distribute matching nutrition incentives to shoppers using WIC CVB, WIC FMNP, and Senior FMNP benefits to purchase California-grown fruits and vegetables at 11 authorized Certified Farmers’ Markets in Los Angeles County. The program will increase the spending power of shoppers using nutrition assistance benefit programs in historically underserved neighborhoods, increase access to nutrient dense produce, and incentivize the purchase of California grown fruits and vegetables.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Growing Impact of the Senior Farmers' Market Nutrition Program in Marin and San Francisco Counties
ProjectAbstract: The project focus on senior SFMNP incentive recipients for Marin and San Francisco County participants. The FMNP program offers a limited number of coupons that are often redeemed in a single visit to the Farmers Market. The incentive program, "FMNP Bonus Bucks", is structured to expand access to California grown fruits and vegetables for low-income FMNP recipients from April 2025 - December 2025.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectAbstract: The Center for Healthy Communities (CHC) will coordinate with WIC and the Senior Farmers’ Market Nutrition Program (FMNP) to implement the Extra Bucks program at four rural north-state farmers’ markets in Butte County.  The program will use scrip as incentives matching WIC FMNP and Senior FMNP dollar-for-dollar one-time per shopper based on the check/voucher amount. Additionally, the program will provide technical assistance to our farmers' market partners and senior shoppers to help with this transition of Senior FMNP benefits being distributed electronically on Farmers’ Market Cards.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: "Multilingual Technical Assistance for Farmers and Shoppers to Facilitate the Transition to Electronic WIC FMNP and SFMNP"
ProjectAbstract: Our goals for this project are to assist in the smooth transition from paper WIC/SFMNP vouchers to electronic benefits through technical assistance, training, and increased wi-fi access, while maintaining a supportive and respectful experience for shoppers using the new system. As a result of this project, we anticipate an increase in the number of WIC-authorized certified producers at AIM farmers markets and better understanding by shoppers of how to utilize WIC and Senior Farmers Market Program benefits.

AgencyDept: Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery
ProjectAbstract: Sutter County Resource Conservation District is seeking funding for cleanup of illegal refuse on 8 sites in the county. Most farmers expect illegal dumping occurs at night and on the weekends. Piles are often dumped on main dirt roads but can also be found between tree lines and tree rows. The proposed sites are close enough to town but rural enough where there is a lack of people present makes this type of land an ideal target. Areas with the easiest access are more prone to getting dumped upon. Grant funds will also be used to install necessary gates to deter future illegal dumping.

AgencyDept: Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery
ProjectAbstract: The Yuba Resource Conservation District plans to remove waste from one privately-owned site in Yuba and one in Butte with the permission from Butte County RCD. The waste was illegally dumped onto parcels, and it impedes property owners’ ability to successfully operate their orchards. Property owners conduct cleanups but can no longer keep up with the increase of dumping. Illegally dumped waste includes, but is not limited to, common trash, appliances, furniture, tires, and vehicles. Yuba RCD is also seeking funding for prevention measures.

AgencyDept: Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery
ProjectAbstract: CalRecycle has edited the following summary to reflect the approved grant project: Tulare County is seeking funding to remove waste from three agricultural sites affected by illegal dumping, all owned by private landowners. Grant funds will also be used to implement preventive measures aimed at deterring future illegal dumping.

ProjectTitle: CalSIP Stream Gage Reactivation - Corning Sub-basin Groundwater Sustainability Agency
ProjectAbstract: The primary purpose of this program is to improve stream gage infrastructure and data availability as part of the California Stream Gage Improvement Program (CalSIP). Through the CalSIP program, DWR is actively improving California’s stream gage network by funding public agencies to upgrade existing gages, reactivate historical gages, or install new gages on natural waterways across the state. The Corning Sub-basin Groundwater Sustainability Agency is working on 1 reactivated stream gage.

The arrival of golden mussels exacerbates the need for CDFW to enhance and augment its invasive mussel monitoring, prevention, and containment activities. The funding will CDFW’s Invasive Mussel Program capacity to meet the acute current challenge posed by the introduction of the golden mussel while continuing to meet the objectives of the statewide quagga zebra mussel strategy.

This project will support the implementation of efforts to 1) prevent the overland spread of golden mussel from waters where they have been detected, and 2) prevent the introduction of invasive mussels to waters of California where invasive mussels have not been detected.

ProjectTitle: Copco Valley Public Access and Recreational Boating Facility for a Renewed Klamath River
ProjectAbstract: This project is focused on the Copco Valley facility, which will serve as a critical safe exit point for less experienced boaters prior to the rapids in Wards Canyon, and an entrance point for those seeking a more difficult run. By providing a well-designed public access and boating facility in a strategic location, the site will facilitate safe access to the river and its shores for boating, fishing, and other uses.
