AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Transformative Reentry provides a seamless Warm Handoff for 48-72 parolees over 3 years, ensuring immediate stability upon release. Peer specialists transport individuals from releasing institutions to VTC, where case managers place them in housing and initiate reentry services tailored to their needs. Participants receive clothing, food, behavioral health care, employment support, & vital social service connections. Through case management, system navigation, and housing assistance, we equip individuals with tools for self-sufficiency, fostering lasting reintegration & long-term stability.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Serves paroled veterans at high risk of homelessness, unemployment, mental health crises, and lack of access to VA benefits or social services.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: New Connections: Assisting justice-impacted San Diegans reintegrate into their community
ProjectAbstract: Over 3 years, Vista Community Clinic will provide reentry services to 150 State prison parolees residing in north San Diego County. Most will be referred by Escondido Parole Officers upon release from Donovan Correctional Facility. Staff will also conduct outreach at VCC clinics, social service agencies, & colleges. Led by an experienced, multidisciplinary team trained in trauma-informed care, the New Connections program features 6 months of intensive case management, six months of aftercare, warm handoffs to services, life skills workshops, housing navigation and rental assistance.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Focus on North San Diego County.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: WestCare California's Bridges to Success program in Fresno offers a continuum of care combining Rental Assistance and Warm Handoff services to support formerly incarcerated individuals. The program provides immediate housing support and connects participants to employment, behavioral health services, and other critical resources. Case managers offer intensive, wraparound support, helping participants achieve stability through housing, life skills, and cognitive interventions. The program applies the Housing First model, ensuring participants access permanent housing quickly.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Provides comprehensive reentry services to formerly incarcerated people in Fresno.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: United Way California Capital Region Reentry Project
ProjectAbstract: United Way California Capital Region (UWCCR) seeks to provide a comprehensive Continuum of Care model supporting justice-involved individuals across Sacramento and Placer Counties areas. The program integrates Warm Handoff/Reentry Services-including case management, system navigation, and supportive services-with UWCCR's already established Rental Assistance programs. By offering rent subsidies, deposits, and landlord incentives, the initiative ensures stable housing while fostering self-sufficiency, reducing recidivism, and promoting long-term housing stability.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Special attention will be given to high-need populations, including individuals with co-occurring disorders, those experiencing homelessness, and people facing employment discrimination due to criminal records.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Cal State University San Bernardino RESET
ProjectAbstract: The Cal State San Bernardino Reentry Initiative's (CSRI) RESET (Resource Navigation, Essential Housing Support, Skills Development & Employment, Engagement & Community Integration, Targeted Case Mngmt) Program will support previous state prisoners transition to independent living. Provides housing navigation, rental assistance, & wraparound services. CSRI, with serving over 14,000 in 14 yrs, integrates housing support with case mngmt, employment svcs, & behavioral health svcs. This will promote self-sufficiency, enhance community reintegration, foster safer communities & long-term stability.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Addresses the need for housing stability for individuals returning to the Inland Empire (IE) from incarceration in state prison through individualized housing navigation services, rental assistance, and substance use disorder support.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Pathways Home: Rental Assistance and Reentry Services for Sustainable Reintegration
RecipientName: Turn 2 U Inc.: Doing Business As: The Last Mile
ProjectAbstract: The Last Mile (TLM) will provide rental assistance & reentry services to 50 recently released adults, primarily in LA County, ensuring housing stability & long-term employment. Each participant will receive one year of services, including up to a year of rental subsidies, case management, employment support, & system navigation for supportive services. A savings model helps participants transition to permanent housing. Peer mentors with lived experience provide guidance, while TLM's Employment Partnerships Team connects participants to fair-chance employers.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Peer-to-peer model that connects alumni to a network of fair-chance employers and supportive services.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Tri Counties Community Action Partnership's Warm Hand-Off/Reentry Project aims to provide comprehensive reentry support services to justice-involved individuals in Glenn and Colusa counties. This program will address critical barriers to successful reintegration, including housing instability, unemployment, behavioral health needs, and transportation challenges. By offering person-centered case management, warm-handoff referrals, and enhanced care coordination, the program seeks to reduce recidivism and improve long-term outcomes for individuals recently released from incarceration.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Target population includes individuals recently released from state prison, particularly those who are at risk of homelessness or housing instability.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: True North Housing Aliance Reentry Services Program
ProjectAbstract: True North Housing Alliance's (TNHA) addresses critical gaps in reentry services for individuals released from state prisons in Butte County. Through pre-release planning, housing navigation, & sustained post-housing support, TNHA aims to reduce recidivism & homelessness. Existing rental assistance funds & leveraging of relationships with key partners will streamline housing navigation processes. TNHA will enhance partnerships with local law enforcement, social service providers, & housing providers to reduce stigma & create pathways to stability for a minimum of 150 individuals.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Uniquely positioned to address critical gaps in services, as one of the few countywide providers;  rental assistance and warm handoff services will expand regionwide-covering Butte, Tehama, Colusa, and Shasta Counties.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Access Project 2.0 is a strength-based program for Transgender, Gender-expansive & Intersex (TGI) adults in LA County who have formerly been incarcerated in a CA state prison. The project is an extension of TLC's Access Project implemented between 2022-2025 which itself was an adaptation of the first intervention to improve post-incarceration service engagement among transwomen. Access Project 2.0 will provide intensive peer case management & housing navigation services, based on Housing First principles, to at least 160 clients, linking them to gender-affirming services & continuum of care.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Program for Transgender, Gender-expansive and Intersex adults in Los Angeles County who have formerly been incarcerated in a CA state prison.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: TFCF Wellness Is Stabilized Housing(WISH) serves formerly incarcerated women returning to San Bernardino Co. Through a 4-phase approach combining housing assistance (rental assistance, shelter vouchers, move-in deposits, & stipends) & warm handoff svcs (individualized case mngmt addressing employment, education, legal barriers, & system navigation), WISH will serve 204 women over 3 yrs, with 90% recently released or on state parole. Using evidence-based practices in a Housing First/Continuum of Care model, WISH builds on 23 yrs of reducing recidivism & homelessness promoting self-sufficiency.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Serves formerly incarcerated women returning to San Bernardino County from CA state prison, addressing the needs of underserved, unhoused populations, including women survivors of domestic violence, formerly incarcerated individuals, and homeless women with children.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The Gemma Project is a reentry program specializing in meeting the needs of justice-involved women. Our evidence-based program begins in-custody building a foundation of support that continues into the community upon release. We assist women to identify behavior patterns, personal strengths & needs, & help them build skills to better access & utilize resources. We complete risk & needs assessments & co-develop individualized Reentry Plans. Upon release we provide system navigation & coordination to maintain stability & self-sufficiency. We currently serve the coastal region of California.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Provides services to all women in CIW and CCWF who will be released to the coastal counties, with Contra Costa being the primary focus.
CountiesServed: Alameda; Contra Costa; San Francisco; Santa Cruz

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: The Happier Life Project's Community Reentry Initiative
ProjectAbstract: The Happier Life Project's (THLP) Community Reentry Initiative aims to reduce recidivism & support successful reentry for individuals released from state prison by: (1) providing 12 supportive housing beds and providing rental assistance to 756 people, (2) helping 300 returning residents achieve sustainable employment and successfully complete probation/parole, and (3) strengthening engagement with essential services upon release by increasing participation in THLP's in-reach program within state correctional facilities by 20 percent annually.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Delivers coordinated care to Latino, Native American, & BIPOC individuals in Riverside & San Bernardino counties who are recently released and/or on state parole.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: The Roman Catholic Archbishop of Los Angeles, A Corporation Sole
ProjectAbstract: With 23 years of experience in reentry services, Partnership for Reentry Program (PREP) proposes to provide comprehensive Warm Handoff/Reentry Services and Rental Assistance to support individuals transitioning from incarceration with our Beacon of Hope Project. Our Continuum of Care Model integrates immediate stabilization, case management, peer mentorship, and financial assistance to ensure successful reintegration. We will provide emergency housing, rental subsidies, transportation, and essential home setup support.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The target population will focus on citizens returning home after prison in Los Angeles County, particularly those on state parole or at high risk of reoffending due to unstable housing.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Tarzana will provide Warm Handoff/Reentry Services and Rental Assistance to adults formerly incarcerated in state prison with priority to those on parole. TTC will provide intensive case management, patient navigation, and housing navigation services, including comprehensive screenings and assessments with emphasis on linking participants to housing, employment, mental health, SUD treatment, medical care, legal and other supportive services and providing rental assistance in the form of emergency and transitional housing, application fees, move-in costs, housing set-up supplies, etc.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Target population is primarily low-income, racial/ethnic minorities who have been released from state prison with an emphasis on individuals with behavioral health needs.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: TDD Supportive Living Inc. seeks funding through the Adult Reentry Grant (ARG) Cohort 4 to provide transitional housing, rental assistance, and comprehensive reentry support for justice-involved individuals in South Los Angeles. Using a Housing First model, the program offers case management, employment readiness assistance, life skils training, mental health support, and harm reduction support. By integrating evidence-based reentry strategies, TDD aims to reduce homelessness, lower recidivism, and promote long-term stability for 60 participants annualy.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Provides of reentry, housing, and supportive services for justice-involved individuals in South Los Angeles.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Social and Environmental Entrepreneurs (SEE), as the fiscal sponsor for Community Veteran Justice Project (CVJP) proposes a Project that will provide participant intake and assessment, case management, housing navigation and stabilization services, public benefits advocacy, life skills education, and system navigation supports to help justice-involved Military and Veterans successfully reintegrate in Los Angeles County. The project will prioritize Military/Veterans who have been recently released from state prison and/or on parole.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Prioritizes Military/Veterans in Los Angeles County who have been recently released from state prison and/or on parole, regardless of their discharge status.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: St. John's Community Health South LA Reentry Assistance Program: Warm Handoff/Reentry Services and Rental Assistance
ProjectAbstract: To address the need for culturally competent reentry services in Service Planning Area 6 of LA County, SJCH proposes services that coordinate warm handoff/reentry services and rental assistance using a continuum of care model, moving individuals from incarceration or housing insecurity to permanent housing. SJCH's Program will ensure seamless support for formerly incarcerated individuals across multiple domains, including barrier removal, case management, linkage to medical and behavioral health services, legal assistance, employment services, housing, and basic needs.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Target population is adults 18 and over in Service Planning Area 6 in Los Angeles County, primarily Latinx and Black, including those experiencing homelessness/at risk of homelessness, who were formerly incarcerated in state prison with a priority for those recently released and/or on state parole.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Pathways to Success: Empowering Justice-Impacted Students Through Higher Education and Comprehensive Reentry Support
RecipientName: Project Rebound at California State University, East Bay
ProjectAbstract: Project Rebound at CSU, East Bay empowers formerly incarcerated individuals by providing a pathway to higher education with financial assistance & wraparound services. This addresses systemic barriers, including financial hardship, academic gaps, & housing instability to ensure success. By providing justice-involved individuals with tuition-free education, high-paying campus jobs, & free housing, coupled with personalized academic advising, life skills development, peer mentorship, & reentry support, this project promotes long-term stability, economic mobility, & reduced recidivism.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Recruits formerly incarcerated individuals to California State University, East Bay (CSUEB) Project Rebound.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Igniting hope for a fresh start, the Bridge to Stability Project (B2S) provides dynamic warm handoff reentry services and vital rental assistance for those newly released or on parole. Leveraging 13 years of experience, we supercharge wraparound services: system navigation, case management, housing support, behavioral health, employment, and transportation. B2S unites service providers to propel successful reintegration and tackle housing stability, rewriting futures.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: San Luis Obispo faces a severe housing crisis that significantly impacts returning citizens; focus is on individuals returning from state prison with the average age range 35-44.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Restoring Citizens Housing Assistance and Reentry Services
ProjectAbstract: Restoring Citizens will provide rental assistance & warm handoff services to 180 adult male ex-offenders who have returned to San Diego County from the State prison system, the majority will be of Hispanic origin. The program will use Housing First & engage participants in activities to sustain stable permanent housing. Restoring Citizens will partner with the National Aliance on Mental Illness San Diego to provide direct housing assistance & housing navigation & services will be developed to provide clients with the broadest choice of services to support employment & self-sufficiency.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Provides rental assistance and warm handoff services to adult male ex-offenders who have returned to San Diego County from the State prison system, with the majority of Hispanic origin.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Peer Voices United will expand its peer-led, field-based reentry services for re-entering individuals & implement a program to offer a continuum of care. The primary service area will be LA, with other field offices in Orange County. The project will provide Warm Handoff/Reentry Svcs, including case mgmnt, housing navigation & employment readiness, & Rental Assistance to address housing instability. By leveraging the lived experience of PVU's staff & peer mentorship, PVU will remove barriers to successful reentry, promoting long-term stability, employment & reduced recidivism.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Primarily serves formerly incarcerated individuals, particularly those who are low-income, BIPOC, and justice-involved, who experience disproportionately high levels of housing insecurity, employment discrimination, and limited access to behavioral health services.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Project HEART New Start Warm Hand-off Reentry and Housing Program
ProjectAbstract: Project H.E.A.R.T will provide a team of Case Managers & Peer Mentors to meet with those immediately released from or pending release from prison. The team will provide in-reach services, case management, housing assistance, peer mentorship, and a warm hand-off to substance use disorder and/or other service providers. Using a three-pronged approach, the program provides: 1 Pre-release CBT, case mngt, & release coordination 2 PM's & CM's will meet the releasee at the gate to carry out the release plan 3 Post Release-intensive case management, housing assistance, connection with PM, & CBT.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The sole non-profit community provider offering formal reentry services in Nevada County.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: NAMI SD Imperial County Adult Reentry Program
RecipientName: National Alliance on Mental Illness San Diego and Imperial Counties
ProjectAbstract: NAMI San Diego proposes an Adult Reentry Program to provide direct housing assistance, warm handoff, and comprehensive wraparound support to 120 individuals exiting the California state prison system in Imperial County. The program will serve individuals returning to both urban and rural areas in Imperial County, with a majority identifying as Hispanic. The program will align with the Housing First model and will provide comprehensive case management and housing assistance to all participants.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The program will serve individuals returning to both urban and rural areas in Imperial County, with a majority identifying as Hispanic.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: San Bernardino Reentry & Rental Assistance Resource Center (SB RRARC)
ProjectAbstract: San Bernardino Reentry & Rental Assistance Resource Center (SB RRARC)) aims to support individuals reentering society post-incarceration (CDCR). The program wil provide comprehensive services including case management, transitional housing, mental health care, substance abuse treatment, education, vocational training, and job placement. the program wi l use a continuum of care model, ensuring a smooth transition for individuals reentering society.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Due to the geographical spread and limited availability of necessary services, such as housing, transportation, legal assistance, and job training programs, hamper reentry success, ensures that these services are readily available and accessible.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Pathway to Kinship: Empowerment and Success Program
ProjectAbstract: Pathway to Kinship's Empowerment and Success program is a three part program designed to equip formerly incarcerated participants (with a priority on participants between 18-28 years old) with the ski ls for safe, supportive reentry. The program, piloted in 2024, offers a wraparound 12 week workforce development training program, including a preapprenticeship placement program. The program is offered in cohorts of up to 25 participants who are paired with a case manager for individualized support to support employment, housing, and safe reentry.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Targets justice-involved participants at moments of transition in care (reentry, job loss, foster care), between the ages of 18-28 at high risk of recidivism.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Mariposa's "Keys for Transformation" will provide reentry svcs & rental assistance within a continuum of care model & housing-first approach for individuals leaving state facilities. Our program is designed to meet the client with an individualized care plan provided by a support team of peers, counselors & case mgrs to build self-sufficiency. The program will provide wraparound, comprehensive svcs including barrier removal, mental health & substance use disorder treatment, workforce readiness, referrals to community supports, transitional housing & navigation to permanent housing.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: As one of the only outpatient programs to offer gender-specific programs, provides focused support to women who have differing needs than men post-release.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: MLIFE delivers an integrated Continuum of Care combining Warm Handoff/Reentry Services with Rental Assistance for 180 individuals transitioning from state prison to San Francisco, prioritizing Black & Latino Californians disproportionately impacted by incarceration. Our 3-phase model provides immediate housing stability, case management, workforce development & behavioral health support. The program addresses critical reentry challenges through evidence-based practices & community partnerships ensuring sustained positive outcomes in housing stability, employment & reduced recidivism.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Delivers an integrated Continuum of Care combining Warm Handoff/Reentry Services with Rental Assistance for 180 individuals transitioning from state prison to San Francisco, prioritizing Black and Latino Californians disproportionately impacted by incarceration.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Reentry Warm Handoff and Rental Assistance in Riverside and San Bernardino Counties
ProjectAbstract: The project will provide Warm Handoff and Rental Assistance to adults formerly incarcerated in state prisons & living in Riverside and San Bernardino Counties. The goal is to promote financial security & reduce recidivism via reentry support, housing, employment, & healthcare. RA will assist 35 people with temporary housing and 50 people with permanent housing via navigation, temporary and move-in costs, eviction prevention, landlord incentives, rent, & deposits. WHO will assist 275 people with peer-led case management, 50 with housing navigation, 175 with health coverage, 45 with employment.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Prioritizes people who are unhoused or who immediate intervention such as a health crisis. Over 70% of the region is Black, Indigenous, and People of Color.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Stabilize to Thrive Warm Hand Off and Rental Assistance Reentry Project
ProjectAbstract: Land Together (LT) will provide comprehensive, wraparound reentry services to people being released from 9 CA state prisons. LT will reach a total of 1,260 people, providing: Pre-release in-reach reentry preparation services & case management; Gate pickups, providing transportation, food, and essentials; Personalized system navigation services that include housing, employment/vocational opportunities, linkages to services, social services & public benefits, & behavioral health care; Weekly peer reentry circles; 1:1 case management & mentorship for up to 12 mo; & Rental assistance for 45.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Reentry staff have developed a rich network of both local and statewide service providers, transitional housing providers, and CBOs in every region to meet the reentry needs of participants regardless of where in the state they plan to return.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Workforce training, job placement, and ongoing comprehensive support for those impacted by incarceration.
ProjectAbstract: ManifestWorks is an immersive workforce development and job placement organization; we offer real-world work training, placement and lifelong support to those impacted by incarceration, foster care and homelessness. Our vision is one of transformation: With ties in TV and film, industry partners join us to teach our Production Assistant training program, our team provides wraparound services including housing, guiding participants through re-entry, and ongoing career and clinical services ensure a quadrupling in wages, decreased reliance on welfare, a virtual elimination of recidivism.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Turns real-world experience into learning opportunities for those impacted by incarceration, foster care and homelessness with an 11-week job-training in film, television, and commercial production.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: Healthy Community Forum for the Greater Sacramento Region dba Community HealthWorks
ProjectAbstract: Community HealthWorks' Reentry program proposes to serve up to 450 individuals returning to the community from state prison. Through a trauma-informed community health worker model, Community HealthWorks will address Social Determinants of Health through direct services, care coordination of healthcare services, housing support services, rental assistance and linkages to community resources that mitigate any barriers to care and establish sustainable independence.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Target population includes adults of all ethnicities and backgrounds in Sacramento County who are returning to the community after state incarceration, particularly those at risk of homelessness.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Homeboy Industries Reentry Warm Handoff Services and Housing First Program
ProjectAbstract: Homeboy Industries (HBI) has been serving communities throughout Los Angeles for more than three decades, responding to the needs of formerly incarcerated men and women. HBI's experienced staff provide a multitude of services and approaches to increase the chances of success for the re-entry population. This program at HBI will enhance the provision of "in-house" Warm handoff services to improve housing conditions, employment and financial stability. Through its housing team and additional navigation, life skills and workforce development support, this project focuses on continuing to build.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Former gang members are embraced by a community of kinship as they receive comprehensive wrap around services and a continuum of care.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Reentry with Dignity: Housing & Economic Stability Program
ProjectAbstract: The Reentry with Dignity: Housing & Economic Stability Program will provide trauma-informed, culturally responsive services to 150 formerly incarcerated individuals in Los Angeles communities. The program offers rental assistance, wraparound case management, warm hand-off referrals, and strategic interventions including tattoo removal and workforce development to eliminate barriers to successful reentry. By ensuring stable housing, job readiness, and economic independence, the program will reduce recidivism and promote long-term stability.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Extensive experience serving Latino, Black, and immigrant communities disproportionately impacted by incarceration, ensuring services are culturally relevant and responsive.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Gods Pantry - Providing Hope & Healing Through Warm Handoff, Reentry, and Housing Services
ProjectAbstract: God's Pantry helps formerly incarcerated individuals adjust to life outside the justice system and find purpose. This grant will support warm handoff reentry and housing services for formerly incarcerated individuals in Pomona and the San Gabriel Valley. Using a continuum of care model, we will provide case management, legal aid, mental health support, workforce development, and tattoo removal services alongside housing support, serving at least 200 clients per year. God's Pantry is dedicated to providing hope and healing, empowering returning citizens with the tools and resources necessary.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: This grant will support warm handoff reentry and housing services for formerly incarcerated individuals in Pomona and the San Gabriel Valley.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: NOW WHO-RA (New Opportunity Work Warm Hand Off- Rental Assistance) Program
ProjectAbstract: Goodwill of Silicon Valley (GWSV), an existing partner in BSCC's ARG program, proposes the NOW WHO-RA Program to serve Santa Clara County residents released from state prison who need help coordinating services, including housing and employment, to support their successful reentry into the community. Our direct service team consisting of a Project Director, Case Manager, and Housing Specialist will deliver integrated services using evidence based and informed practices and a client-centered continuum of care. GWSV will track and report on both quantitative and qualitative data.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The need for employment and housing services is particularly acute as the target population is reintegrating into an area with one of the highest costs of living in the U.S.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: ARG WHO/Reentry and Rental Assistance Program
RecipientName: Foothill House of Hospitality dba Hospitality House
ProjectAbstract: Foothill House of Hospitality DBA Hospitality House (HH) will continue providing warm handoff (WHO)/Reentry and rental assistance (RA) services for individuals transitioning from state prison. HH will provide comprehensive case management services to a total of 75 participants through the WHO/Reentry program and 50 participants through the RA program over the duration of the grant. The program addresses gaps in housing, employment, and support services using the housing first approach, ensuring successful reentry, long-term stability, and reduced recidivism.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The only organization offering immediate shelter, case management, housing navigation, and employment support to individuals being released in Nevada County.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Friends Outside Warm Hand-Off Reentry Program
ProjectAbstract: Friends Outside engages individuals who are currently reentering from state prison or have a history of incarceration at a CDCR institution. To promote a successful reentry into the community & reduce the likelihood of future justice system involvement, our program provides comprehensive case mngmt, service navigation, & rental assistance to the individual & their families. Our evidence-based programming & wrap-around case mngnt reduces criminogenic risk & need, increases pro-social skill development & behaviors amongst individuals & strengthens the family's ability to support their reentry.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The San Joaquin Valley has the highest rates of violent crime in the state; Creates second chances for reentering individuals,  identifying the three primary needs of the reentry process as: permanent housing, employment pathways, and pro-social skill development and support.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Finish First Academy Adult Re-Entry Program
ProjectAbstract: Finish First Academy (FFA) will provide pre- and post-release re-entry services for adults who have been incarcerated and are returning to Los Angeles County, with a focus on Watts and the surrounding communities. The program will provide assessments, trauma-informed case management, access to transitional housing (through a 10-bed program operated by FFA), life skills education, employment search and placement services, public benefits advocacy, housing navigation and placement services, housing stabilization services.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Prioritizes individuals being released to state parole who will reside in Watts or the surrounding South Los Angeles communities; specific expertise providing services to gang-involved individuals, young adults (18-26), individuals who are homeless, and survivors of domestic violence.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Returning Home Wel: Integrated Reentry Support Services
ProjectAbstract: Epidaurus DBA Amity Foundation provides case management, systems navigation, service coordination, benefits enrollment, and housing supports for the reentry population in Los Angeles County. Leveraging expert knowledge of community systems and collaborative alliances with reentry-focused CBOs and Parole offices, Amity will recruit, assess, and connect 800 formerly incarcerated individuals into an appropriate system of care or benefit, and provide monthly rental assistance and housing advocacy to 200 individuals who will demonstrate stable, sustained housing after the subsidy period.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Serves parolees in Los Angeles County, 18+, disproportionately people of color, including Long Term Offenders, LGBTQI+, individuals with disabilities, or younger adults including firefighting inmates at CDCR Fire Camps.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Fortifying Life After Incarceration with Warm Hand Off and Rental Assistance
ProjectAbstract: Expanding its reach-in, care coordination, and supportive housing for 180 or more parolees, Family Assistance Program operates transitional houses and support in San Bernardino County, with capacity for 30 parolees. Staff coordinates extensive individual service plans, assessments and screenings, housing navigation and landlord advocacy, financial assistance for moving costs, initial rent and utilities. Individuals achieve economic empowerment and long-term self-sufficiency through personalized, meaningful, client-centered goals and established life ski ls coaching.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: San Bernardino is the largest county and characterized as rural and socially disorganized, with diverse racial, ethnic, economic and geographic make up, high unemployment and poverty rates.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: Contra Costa Interfaith Transitional Housing dba Hope Solutions
ProjectAbstract: Hope Solutions will synthesize our existing BSCC Warm Hand Off and Rental Assistance programs into one holistic Adult Reentry Support Program that utilizes reentry stabilization support, housing navigation, rental assistance, case management, and employment services to ensure client self-sufficiency and public safety. We will expand clients' housing options, deepen our employment and other support services, and lengthen the amount of time each client spends in our program to improve client reintegration.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Improves permanent housing outcomes for those released from California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation under AB 109 and state parolees.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Warm Handoff and Housing Assistance Program
ProjectAbstract: Defy Ventures will provide comprehensive inside-outside reentry programming to support successful reentry for people releasing from California state prisons. With extensive pre-release in-reach programming coordinated via warm-handoff with post-release case management, system navigation, reentry coaching, well-being programs, and housing support, Defy Ventures will support people returning home from incarceration to find success and stability in reentry.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Supports individuals releasing from California state prisons and returning home to Los Angeles County, as well as other counties across the state.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: This proposal outlines the Elevate Pioneer program, which wil be operated by CityServe Network (CSN) and serve populations 18 and over who have been formerly incarcerated in state prison, prioritizing those recently released and/or on state parole. This program wil provide warm handoff, reentry services, and rental assistance services to al participants over a 3-month long period over the 3-year Adult Reentry Grant (ARG) grant period. By the end of the grant period, CSN's administrative team anticipates lower recidivism rates in the Bakersfield community.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Prioritizes rapid rehousing to homeless individuals.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: CAPK Adult Reentry Grant Warm Handoff and Reentry Services with Rental Assistance
ProjectAbstract: Community Action Partnership of Kern (CAPK) will expand its ARG services to address housing instability, employment barriers, and recidivism among justice-involved individuals in Kern County. CAPK will provide case management, rental assistance, job readiness training, and behavioral health referrals, prioritizing high-barrier populations, including those under Penal Code 290. With experienced staff, existing infrastructure, and strong partnerships, CAPK is prepared to implement services immediately, ensuring a continuum of care that promotes longterm stability and reduces recidivism.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Provides case management, rental assistance, job readiness training, and behavioral health referrals, prioritizing high-barrier populations, including those under Penal Code 290.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Removing Barriers to Housing Security: Coordinated Legal and Social Work Services
RecipientName: Community Legal Services in East Palo Alto
ProjectAbstract: CLSEPA's Removing Barriers to Housing Security: Coordinated Legal and Social Work Services project will give people with prison records a roadmap to guide them towards a brighter future for themselves and their families. We will provide our target population with a map and timeline of what their record clearance journey will look like, identify what convictions will create obstacles for their career goals, provide record cleaning services within our geographic service area, and provide social work services, housing financial assistance, and other non-legal warm handoff support for success.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Serves people who have faced systemic barriers to justice and inclusion, including formerly incarcerated community members, those who are low-income, Black, Indigenous, and people of color (BIPOC), LGBTQ, immigrants, low-wage workers, and those with limited English proficiency.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Warm Handoff to Jobs and Housing (WHJH)
ProjectAbstract: The proposed program will address barriers to employment, housing, and wraparound services that former state prisoners in the San Fernando Valley and greater Los Angeles area face. We will enroll at least 200 members of the target population to receive peer-led employment services, cognitive behavioral interventions, housing navigation/rental assistance. We will prepare, place, and retain participants in jobs and provide paths to permanent housing, facilitating successful reentry through a continuum of care model that incorporates the core components of Housing First.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Focus on San Fernando Valley and Los Angeles.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Pathways II Stability Re-Entry Support Program
ProjectAbstract: The Pathways II Stability Re-Entry Support Program by Chances 4 Change, Inc. provides justice-involved individuals in South LA with housing, employment, & behavioral health services. Using a Housing First & Trauma-Informed Care approach, it offers rental assistance, job preparation, case management, & legal aid support to reduce recidivism & promote stability. The program will serve up to 300 participants over 3 years, tracking housing retention, employment success, & behavioral health improvements.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Serving justice-involved individuals in South Los Angeles.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The BAIHP is an Urban Indian organization offering a range of services to both native & non-native individuals. The BAIHP supports individuals transitioning from incarceration by providing stable housing through transitional housing costs, rent subsidies, vouchers, housing setup, & essential necessities. The program will offer case management, mental health care, therapy, counseling, and food security. These services address trauma, stress, & addiction, ensuring long-term stability. The program's approach helps individuals rebuild their lives, avoid reoffending, & achieve stable futures.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Supports formerly incarcerated Native and non-Native individuals.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Statewide Financial Case Management and Housing Stability Program for Justice-Involved Individuals in California.
ProjectAbstract: BIGA IMPACT seeks funding for the Statewide Financial Case Management and Housing Stability Program, reducing recidivism and increasing financial/housing security for justice-involved individuals in California. The program provides financial literacy, credit repair, rental assistance, and eviction prevention, expanding to a minimum of 10 underserved counties. Outcomes will include 80% completing financial training, 70% securing stable housing, and reduced recidivism. Sustainable through partnerships and diversified funding, the program empowers individuals to rebuild their lives.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Rural counties with high poverty rates-such as Imperial, Tulare, Madera, and Siskiyou.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: Catholic Charities of Santa Clara County
ProjectAbstract: Catholic Charities of Santa Clara County, located in San Jose, proposes its Bridge to Reentry Program to expand stabilizing services for those reentering the community from CA state prisons. CCSCC plans to build on the infrastructure it developed operating its Warm Handoff reentry program in Cohort 2 to serve 60 new clients annually and add a rental assistance component. We will leverage our relationships with community and system partners to reach and prioritize individuals released to state parole. The program will help participants attain self-sufficiency, reduce crisis, increase housing.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Serving low-income adults with state prison histories, may currently be on parole or Post-Release Community Supervision, and face critical needs for affordable housing, service navigation, basic necessities, and supportive services.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The Torres Martinez Desert Cahuilla Indians propose creating a trauma informed Tiny Home Village to provide safe, transitional housing for Indigenous individuals who are homeless or at high risk for MMIP. This culturally rooted project addresses urgent safety, shelter, and support needs by offering stable housing, wraparound services, and community connection. The village will serve as a protective intervention space that fosters healing and reduces vulnerability to violence, trafficking, and disappearance.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Sacred and Seen: A Tribal Response to MMIP and Intelectual and Developmental Disabilities- A cultura ly grounded prevention and intervention initiative addressing the heightened risk of victimization for Native individuals with inte lectual and developmental disabilities.
RecipientName: Iipay Nation of Santa Ysabel (Collaborative w/Mesa Grande Band of Mission Indians & Yurok Tribe)
ProjectAbstract: Our project will provide targeted prevention, outreach, & trauma-informed prevention & interventions specifically designed for Natives with intellectual & developmental disabilities (IDD). This population is at significantly higher risk of victimization, exploitation, & disappearance due to multiple compounding vulnerabilities-communication challenges, dependency on caregivers, limited access to appropriate services, & systemic neglect.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Pathways to Protection: A Tribal MMIP Initiative
RecipientName: Scotts Valey Band of Pomo Indians (Collaborative w/Big Valley Rancheria and Middletown Rancheria)
ProjectAbstract: In partnership with Big Valey Rancheria (BV) and Middletown Rancheria, is advancing a comprehensive MMIP initiative rooted in prevention, awareness, education, and response. This initiative addresses identified risks within our Tribal communities and is tailored to the realities of SVBPI citizens. This MMIP initiative is an intentional investment in healing, safety, and resiliency. It builds on SVBPI's long-standing commitment to address addiction, promoting wellness, and preventing tragedy through culturally tailored services.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: RVIT MMIP Awareness and Response Program
ProjectAbstract: RVIT MMIP will implement this program to carry out important and crucial MMIP Awareness, Prevention, and Response Tasks in the Tribal Community of Round Valey in Northern California.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: Mechoopda Indian Tribe of Chico Rancheria
ProjectAbstract: A project that has youth at the forefront with the establishment of GONAs and other events to help the youth understand the risks of trafficking, drugs, and how vulnerable communities are taken advantage. Along with the youth programming, MIT plans on creating a well-rounded program that supports the whole community with reunification services, addiction counseling, community healing, prevention, and more services to support our Tribal community members and surrounding communities protect our vulnerable individuals.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Provide awareness for the Missing and Murdered Indigenous People (MMIP) and human trafficking crisis affecting our community. With grant funding the Redding Rancheria wil promote community engagement opportunities, cultural sensitivity training, government to government collaboration, public outreach, and provide supplies for awareness and prevention. Hosting gatherings, we can collaborate MMIP awareness efforts with local organizations. Enlisting an expert speaker to educate our community. Awareness walks every year with the community will also communicate information.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Yurok To' Kee Skuy' Soo Ney-wo-chek'
ProjectAbstract: The Yurok Tribe's project aims to build tribe-centered systems to prevent and account for the deaths and disappearances of Indigenous people. By enhancing internal infrastructure, increasing response capabilities, supporting families, and educating youth, the project will address the MMIP crisis in Northern California. Key activities include hiring a full-time MMIP Victim Advocate, conducting search and rescue training, acquiring search and rescue supplies and technology, and providing educational outreach. The project will serve 15-20 new MMIP cases and assist in 20-30 cold cases annually.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Two Feathers MMIP Youth Empowerment Project
ProjectAbstract: The Two Feathers MMIP Youth Empowerment Project will work to reduce MMIP issues in our community through strengthening partnerships among organizations serving American Indian youth and culturally, youth-driven and prevention-based programming that supports not only healing, but leadership development among local AI youth. Two Feathers (TF), a Tribally chartered non-profit that is an entity of Big Lagoon Rancheria, will subaward the funds from this grant to implement the project, with a focus on strengthening prevention activities, training, and youth leadership around the MMIP crisis.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: "Honoring Our Roots: Healing Through Culture and Connection"
RecipientName: Enterprise Rancheria of Maidu Indians of California
ProjectAbstract: A  community-based MMIP prevention/healing initiative centered on cultural revitalization, intergenerational engagement, and outreach activities. Rooted in our traditional values, this project will strengthen community resilience and reduce vulnerability to violence, human trafficking, and disconnection by enhancing cultural pride and belonging. This will include hosting seasonal Gatherings, GONA gatherings, cultural dances, where youth, families, and Elders gather to share teachings, language, crafts, songs, and traditional knowledge.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: La Jolla Band of Luiseno Indians
ProjectAbstract: Support our efforts to bring awareness, prevention, education and colaborations to the La Jolla Indian Reservation and surrounding tribal communities. LJBLI wi l implement a program that brings awareness by providing culturaly based prevention strategies, strengthening responses to MMIP and human trafficking, and improving cooperation and communication on jurisdictional issues between state, local, federal and tribal law enforcement. The Tribal Police Department wil assist and a professional evaluator wil perform level one evaluation.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Pala MMIP Expanded Awareness and Prevention Program
ProjectAbstract: Expand on our current MMIP Cohort 2 award with new innovative activities. Pala recognizes that tribes within our region may not apply due to lack of capacity necessary to administer a MMIP program and is willing to bridge the gap in providing services. Pala proposes to developing a dedicated MMIP website. The website will have details and alerts for new missing cases and cases that have not been solved, purchase a drone and incorporate a youth component. Pala proposes to contract with a private investigator and provide training for volunteer search and rescue.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The is an expansion of Pinoleville Pomo Nation's MMIP Project. It is aimed at filing identified gaps in services including outreach and services to incarcerated youth and their families, and outreach and increased awareness around MMIP issues including California's Feather Alert and assistance to families of missing indigenous people. The project will expand outreach to local schools, provide training to Tribal and community members on missing person response, provide information and tools to combat human trafficking, and enhance culturally appropriate services to participants.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: tain?m? watsik?t t?nobi pinasu kimat, tain?m? ohobe n?wid? (our missing people come home again, our people walk strong)
RecipientName: Big Sandy Rancheria of Western Mono Indians of California
ProjectAbstract: Goals: strengthen prevention, promote healing, raise awareness, & improve response Outcomes 1) Raise awareness of MMIP to 10,000 people through community events, outreach materials, and social media 2) Provide services for victims & family members 3) Provide domestic violence counseling & case management for 200 Native Americans 4) Provide services to 30 at-risk Native Americans 5) Create talking circles that include Tribal Elders to support community healing & model cultural-intellectual responses to crises 6) Improve MMIP response efforts by expanding partnerships with law enforcement

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
RecipientName: Coyote Valey Band of Pomo Indians
ProjectAbstract: The Tribe is requesting BSCC MMIP (2025) funding for the Coyote Valey MMIP Program. The Program wil be a community-driven initiative designed to prevent and support cases of MMIP. It wil provide advocacy, case management, and victim services to survivors and affected families. It wil raise awareness through outreach and wil seek to bring local Tribes and services providers together to enhance colaboration on MMIP issues. The mission wil be to protect vulnerable individuals and improve justice for MMIP cases.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: Greenville Rancheria will take a preventive and proactive approach to ensure well-being in our communities along the Northern California I-5 corridor and rural remote CA by: Prevention, Awareness, Education, and events of tribal communities we serve. Develop, produce digital mapping, and story maps with collaboration of experts, to locate new areas where our MMIP persons were last seen or were found. Assist families immediate needs of private investigator funds, counseling, liaison between law enforcement, court processor, and seeking culturally sensitive and familiar outreach.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Gun Violence Reduction Program (GVRP) Expansion Project
ProjectAbstract: The Ventura County Sheriff's Office (VCSO) will implement the GVRP Expansion Project: 1) enabling the Ventura County Superior Court and Ventura County District Attorney's Office to notify VCSO of newly prohibited individuals prior to submission of these individuals to the Armed Prohibited Persons System (APPS) ; 2) installing an additional firearm storage cage and doubling capacity for storage of relinquished firearms; and 3) training law enforcement personnel/community members on topics related to ERPOs.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: City of Westminster Firearm Relinquishment Implementation
ProjectAbstract: The City of Westminster is requesting funding to implement a comprehensive firearm relinquishment program that updates our data systems, officer training, and protocols to ensure guns are safely seized and stored. Grant funding will allow the City to comprehensively update our data analysis and tracking systems and seizure protocols and training to safely identify and seize firearms from prohibited persons in our community.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Identifying and Addressing Early Warning Signs: A Community-Based Behavior Threat Assessment and Outreach Program for Gun Violence Prevention
ProjectAbstract: The first phase will be aimed at community outreach.  The second phase will be the actual removal of firearms from prohibited persons via ERPOs. This will be accomplished by working directly with law enforcement agencies and other stakeholders to create a Behavioral Threat Assessment Response Team. The final phase will be a data collection and analysis component that will guide future gun violence responses within SCC. The data, in turn, will dictate where continued education, enforcement, and funding emphasis should be placed.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: The City of Vallejo's Integrated Health and Resource Team (IHART)
ProjectAbstract: The City of Vallejo Police Department seeks funds to expand IHART, a mobile crisis co-response unit addressing critical service gaps in Vallejo, California. The project will increase crisis response service delivery, referrals to local services, reduce reliance on police for non-violent mental health/SUD-related calls, address and reduce gun violence, and improve crisis outcomes. Expansion addresses urgent demand, high risk of escalation and violence posed by police presence during crises, and VPD's limited staffing capacity to handle both violent and non-violent calls effectively.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The Santa Barbara Sheriff's Office is seeking funding for two Special Duty Deputies to be a part of a Crisis Intervention Team (CIT), Co-Responder model, where they are paired with clinicians from the Department of Behavioral Wellness. The two-person CIT will respond to behavioral health and mental health crisis through 911. They will divert persons from the criminal justice system when appropriate, educating persons on gun violence protection including Gun Violence Restraining Orders, and preventing violence utilizing Behavioral Threat Assessment and Management principles and practices.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Project SAFEGUARD (Schools and Families Engaged for Gun Use Awareness and Risk Detection)
ProjectAbstract: To reduce gun violence, San Mateo Police Department seeks funding for Project SAFEGUARD (Schools and Families Engaged for Gun Use Awareness and Risk Detection), where a full-time Community Service Officer (CSO) will serve as Threat of Gun Violence Expert. This CSO will investigate threats of gun violence at schools, lead crisis interventions, and connect at risk youth to services as well as coordinate public outreach to raise awareness about Extreme Risk Protection Orders.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Will Serve City of San Mateo

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The City of San Diego is proposing to establish a crisis intervention program, expand community education and outreach, develop a public media campaign, and obtain threat assessment and crisis intervention training for personnel to decrease gun violence and improve firearm relinquishment efforts. Furthermore, this proposal will seek to improve safe storage of firearms through the expansion of the San Diego Police Department's nearly full firearm evidence locker, installation of police vehicle gun storage lockers, and the purchase of gun locks for citizens seized and non seized firearms.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Will serve City of San Diego

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Enhancing Crisis Response and Firearm Relinquishment Procedures
ProjectAbstract: Project Summary The proposed project aims to improve crisis response and intervention services to reduce gun violence and enhance public safety in San Rafael. By maintaining the Specialized Assistance for Everyone (SAFE) Team's capacity, improving coordination with law enforcement and mental health professionals, and refining firearm relinquishment procedures, this initiative will significantly reduce uses of force incidents, justice system diversions, and unauthorized firearm access.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Will serve City of San Rafael

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Pinole Crisis Intervention Awareness and Safety Initiative
ProjectAbstract: The City of Pinole seeks Byrne SCIP funding to implement a dual-focused project that enhances community awareness of Extreme Risk Protection Orders (ERPOs) and modernizes firearm storage infrastructure at the Pinole Police Department. The project includes public outreach at events like National Night Out 2025 and upgrades to outdated evidence storage using secure lockers and tracking tools. Together, these efforts aim to reduce gun violence, support crisis intervention, and promote safe firearm practices in the community.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Nevada County Sheriff's Office Co-Responder Mobile Crisis Team
ProjectAbstract: The Nevada County Sheriff's Office Mobile Crisis Team is a co-responder model of policing which is made up of two teams, each consisting of one deputy sheriff and one mental health clinician who are paired up to respond to mental health crisis calls in unincorporated Nevada County. Our teams are unique in that the clinicians are embedded with our operations division on patrol, participate in daily briefings with our deputies, and spend their shifts partnered with the mobile crisis deputies on active patrol. We work closely with behavioral health and NGO services for wraparound care.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Parlier Violence Prevention and Crisis Response Initiative
ProjectAbstract: The City of Parlier will implement a focused initiative to combat rising gang violence and illegal firearm activity threatening public safety. With limited staffing and no internal crisis team, Parlier will train officers in crisis negotiation and de-escalation, deploy overtime patrols to gun violence hotspots, and expand public education on firearm risks and community reporting. This project aims to build officer capacity, disrupt cycles of violence, and empower residents to help prevent gun-related crimes before they occur.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Domestic Violence Restraining Order Enforcement Task Force
ProjectAbstract: This project seeks to enhance the enforcement of DVROs and ensure firearm relinquishment compliance. By strengthening interagency collaboration, improving monitoring mechanisms, and providing survivor-centered support, this initiative will reduce the risk of firearm-related violence against victims of domestic abuse. Studies show that access to a firearm by an abuser increases the likelihood of homicide by fivefold.  This project aims to address gaps in enforcement and monitoring through a comprehensive approach.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Will serve the City of Los Angeles

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Testing Community Outreach and Media Strategies to Increase GVRO (Gun Violence Restraining Order) Awareness and Prevent Firearm Suicides in Marin County
ProjectAbstract: The Marin County DA's Office is partnering with local, state and national partners to address the growing gun violence problem of firearm suicides. After a deep dive into Marin data, a trio of media advocacy agencies will create a digital media campaign that promotes the 988 Lifeline and GVROs and strategically places messages to reach those at risk. Some nonprofit agencies will receive mini-grants and training to conduct GVROs presentations. Campaign materials and strategies will be replicated in two more counties.

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectAbstract: The City of Greenfield seeks support for the Road to Success Program, a pre-arrest law enforcement program for youth, a collaboration between the Greenfield Police Department and Sun Street Centers, a local nonprofit. The Road to Success uses evidence-based programming working with youth, referred by the Police Department, and their parents, to prevent escalating violent and drug-related behavior and justice system involvement and to support healthy pro-social behavior. The City will also purchase a large gun locker to assure safe keeping of relinquished guns.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Will serve the City of Greenfield

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Safe and Secure Firearms Modernization and Community Education Initiative
ProjectAbstract: The Imperial County Sheriff's Office has identified several areas of need within the SIU and proposes a project to address those areas by, Expanding our secure gun storage capacity & implementing new technology to store & track relinquished guns; Hiring an Evidence Technician to enhance the ability of the department to store, track & return relinquished guns; Train & certify staff as firearm specialists for safety, proper handling & educational purposes; Provide gunlocks & educational resources to the community, to raise awareness for safe gun storage practices

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: Victim Advocate to Raise Awareness and Reduce gun Violence
ProjectAbstract: This project seeks funding for a four-part initiative focused on training, outreach, and victim advocacy, particularly in domestic violence and firearm-related cases. Central to the effort is hiring a victim advocate with expertise in trauma recovery, advocacy, and legal systems. The advocate will assist in officer training on GVROs , lead public outreach, support victims directly, and build interagency networks. Emphasizing proactive, civil-based safety measures, the project aims to raise awareness, improve victim outcomes, and prevent revictimization in high-risk situations.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Will serve the City of Alameda

AgencyDept: Board of State and Community Corrections
ProjectTitle: City of Berkeley Gun Violence Intervention and Prevention Program (GVIPP)
ProjectAbstract: The proposed Gun Violence Intervention and Prevention Program (GVIPP) will implement a multi-faceted violence prevention and crisis intervention initiative that directly addresses the community's firearm-related needs. It will support the transition of the GVIPP from a pilot to a sustainable model by hiring a Crime Analyst within the Berkeley Police Department; expansion collaboration with Live Free for crisis stabilization services and deliver training for outreach staff; & integration of the Flock Safety's NOVA software to enhance firearm case resolution and investigative efficiency.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Will serve the City of Berkeley

ProjectTitle: CWA Public Access Upland Game Hunt Program
ProjectAbstract: Funding will assist CWA with managing food plots, pheasant stocking and administrative tasks to provide public upland game bird hunting opportunities on 2,545 acres. This would allow hosting 20 hunt days in the fall, and reach up to 24 hunters per date, totaling up to 480 potential hunters who will be allowed to harvest dove (during fall season) and pheasants.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Goose Lake holding in the Tulare Basin (Kern County) includes two properties; the Houchin and Badger Almond units. Sanborn Slough is located adjacent to Butte Creek Island Ranch in Butte County.

ProjectTitle: Novice Turkey Hunt Coordinator-Sacramento NWR Complex
ProjectAbstract: California Waterfowl will hire a coordinator to oversee the novice spring turkey hunt program. The coordinator will work with CWA staff and Sacramento NWR Complex staff to perform various hunt related tasks including conducting hunter safety meetings and organizing volenteers. The purpose of this project is to provide a high-quality and educational hunting experience for novice hunters at the NWR and to recruit, retain, and reintroduce hunters to the field. The Coordinator supports up to 14 public hunt days, directly engaging up to 21 hunter and 21 non-hunters.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The Sacramento National Wildlife Refuge is located primarily in?Glenn and Colusa Counties.
