AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Development of Diagnostic Tools to Support Site-Specific N Management Decisions in Organic Cropping Systems
RecipientName: Paul Zerbe, Soil Health Lab LLC
ProjectAbstract: Nitrogen (N) management in organic production is challenging because plants rely on soil organisms to mineralize N from fertilizers, and while models to estimate plant-available N are emerging, uncertainty remains high. This project will evaluate management history and a suite of soil properties for 120 organic vegetable fields in the Salinas Valley to develop and test a field-specific diagnostic tool to support N organic management for growers. The decision-support tool will aid in effective N management, support yield goals and profitability, and ensure regulatory compliance.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The target geographic scope for this project is organic vegetable production in California’s Salinas Valley. The main audience is organic growers and crop advisors, although conventional growers focused on soil health may also benefit. In addition, the project serves soil testing labs, fertilizer producers and distributors, regulatory agencies, and researchers.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Nitrogen Runoff and Leaching Loss from Fate in Nursery Production Systems
RecipientName: Chris Shogren, University of California Cooperative Extension
ProjectAbstract: Nitrate contamination is a concern for the CA nursery industry. Operations are required to estimate nitrogen (N) discharge, but plants are sold with fertilizer and substrate intact, making N removal estimation difficult. This project seeks to quantify N runoff and leaching from common combinations of irrigation (drip vs. overhead), fertilizer type (controlled release vs. water-soluble), and soilless substrates with varying carbon-to-N ratios. Findings will support the development of best management practices to improve efficiency, reduce fertilizer losses, and protect groundwater quality.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The audience for this project is California nursery growers, regulatory agencies including the State Water Board and Regional Boards, who require data to improve regulations related to nitrogen management in the nursery sector, and industry organizations that advocate for policies and practices that support economic and environmental sustainability in the nursery sector. The research will be done at the South Coast Research and Extension Center in Irvine and targeted outreach will be provided by Environmental Horticulture advisors serving northern and southern CA.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Nutrient Management: A Collaborative Approach between Agriculture and Regulatory Programs in the San Diego Region
RecipientName: Valerie Mellano, San Diego Region Irrigated Lands Group Science and Policy Advisor
ProjectAbstract: Agriculture in the San Diego area has long grappled with nitrate contamination of surface water. In response, the San Diego Region Irrigated Lands Group (SDRILG) and Regional Water Board are focusing compliance efforts on educating growers on best management practices (BMPs) that address this issue. This project aims to 1) analyze the BMP needs collaboratively with regulatory program staff and 2) support the SDRILG in providing data-driven outreach to educate its grower members and support implementation of the most effective BMPs for the unique agricultural operations in the region.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The meetings and workshops will take place in the mid to north county locations of San Diego County where the most agricultural production occurs. Classroom-style meetings will be held at at public locations, offices and field demonstrations will occur at greenhouses and orchards. Outreach for these meetings will occur through email, online, by phone and postal mail, and trainings and outreach materials will be available in Spanish and English.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Thompson Land Management Equipment for Increased Capacity for Forest Health and Fire Prevention
ProjectAbstract: Thompson Land Management seeks funding to purchase a Tiger M726G Mulcher with a Tigercat 4061-25 Head, boosting mastication capacity for hazardous fuels and forest health projects, including high-priority WUIs. TLM, a growing Northern California business, currently treats 3,600 acres annually with two mulchers. The new equipment will increase treated acreage to 4,000?"6,000 per year, as each unit covers about 10 acres per day. One new employee will be hired to operate the machine.
CountiesServed: Butte; Colusa; El Dorado; Glenn; Lassen; Mendocino; Modoc; Placer; Plumas; Shasta; Siskiyou; Sutter; Tehama; Trinity; Yuba

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectAbstract: The Forestry Challenge is a four-day academic event for high school students focused on technical forestry and current topics. Since 2003, it has expanded to six events across California. Students learn about forest ecology and management, exploring how forests support water, recreation, wood products, and wildlife. The program builds understanding of forest-community connections, introduces natural resource careers, and engages youth in critical thinking on issues like wildfire, insects, and forest health.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Mad River Mass Timber Facility Expansion
ProjectAbstract: Mad River Mass Timber plans to expand its Humboldt County facility with a high-capacity finger jointer and integrated processing, building on its 2024 CAL FIRE-funded R&D grant that proved dowel laminated timber (DLT) can be made from regional species. The project moves MRMT from pilot to commercial production, up-valuing 10?"15 MMBF of lumber and creating 13?"20 jobs annually. As California’s first vertically integrated mass timber producer, MRMT will help meet low-carbon building goals while supporting forest health.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Forestry and Natural Resources Career Mentorship Program
ProjectAbstract: The Forestry and Natural Resources Career Mentorship Program, active since 2020, supports California community college and university forestry students by pairing them with professional mentors to ease the transition into forestry careers. Funding will sustain a Program Manager to oversee daily operations, including program rollout, mentor-student coordination, workshops, training, fundraising, and surveys to guide improvement, with support from a volunteer Steering Committee.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Forest Improvement, Resilience and Employment (F.I.R.E.) Bootcamp
ProjectAbstract: Conservation Corps North Bay will launch the F.I.R.E. Bootcamp, an intensive training program for 48 young adults from underrepresented communities. Delivered in 8 cohorts, each participant receives 96 hours of hands-on instruction in CPR/First Aid, sawyer skills, chipper operation, and pile burning, including biochar production. The program includes certifications, career workshops, and a career fair. F.I.R.E. Bootcamp builds a skilled wildfire mitigation workforce and supports forest health and resilience in the North Bay region.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Equipment Purchase for Expanding Fuel Reduction Operations
ProjectAbstract: Diversified Resources, Inc., a trusted contractor in forest health and wildfire mitigation, seeks CAL FIRE funding to purchase a feller buncher with a masticating head. This equipment will expand fuel reduction capacity by 35%, enabling faster, large-scale treatments while reducing emissions by eliminating pile burning. The investment accelerates project timelines and supports CAL FIRE’s Forest Health Program goals, including climate resilience, wildfire prevention, and ecosystem restoration.
CountiesServed: Amador; Butte; Calaveras; Glenn; Lassen; Plumas; Shasta

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Building Northern California's Prescribed Fire & Forestry Workforce
ProjectAbstract: This 2.3-year project delivers prescribed fire, fuels management, and forestry workforce training via three components: an 11-month Prescribed Fire Apprenticeship (2 cohorts), an 18-month Fire Fellowship, and public field trainings, workshops, and NWCG courses. Led by ACR’s Fire Forward program, it creates 22 jobs, trains 230 workers, and issues 255+ certificates. The project builds a regional workforce and career pathways, emphasizing access to fair-paying jobs for low-income and marginalized communities.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectAbstract: A web-based learning system for the RPF exam in California to improve access to education, addresses the exam's complexity, meets the demand for qualified RPFs, and supports professional development and public safety. This is necessary to increase the number of RPFs to provide professional forestry services for implementing critical projects outlined in the Wildfire and Forest Resilience Task Force Goals.  It will augment the already successful and ongoing CLFA pilot program.

ProjectTitle: Foster Youth Services Coordinating Program Technical Assistance Provider
RecipientName: Los Angeles County Office of Education
ProjectAbstract: The FYSCP Technical Assistance Provider (TAP) is selected through a competitive process to provide support to each county offering these services to foster youth. The FYSCP TAP must demonstrate the:    Expertise with the FYSCP and continuous improvement;    Ability to foster collaboration among county agencies though interagency agreements which address school stability and information sharing;    Capacity and willingness to support data gathering and analysis processes; and    Ability to support online meetings and resources sharing among county FYSCP Coordinators.

AwardAmountNotes: This replenish grant provided the Noyo Harbor with oil spill response equipment to help protect its economic resources and sensitive sites during an oil spill.
ProjectAbstract: N/A

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Reducing Orchard Nitrate Leaching to Groundwater with HFLC and AgMAR: Ground-Truthing and Guiding the ILRP Assessment Tool
RecipientName: Thomas Harter, University of California, Davis
AwardAmountNotes: Matching funds comprised of $8,000 from the University of California (UC) Davis Gustavsson Endowed Chair and UC Agriculture and Natural Resources (ANR) and $60,000 from a United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) National Institute of Food and Agriculture (NIFA) grant.
ProjectAbstract: This project monitors water and nitrogen (N) fluxes into and out of a commercial almond orchard when the practice of high frequency, low concentration (HFLC) fertility management is adopted. The project will: 1. Evaluate the effect of Agricultural Managed Aquifer Recharge (AgMAR) in almond orchards 2. Assess irrigation and fertigation uniformity 3. Evaluate soil nutrient dynamics in young orchards 4. Implement on-site ET measurements. Project results will be communicated to the coalitions to calibrate modeling tools and with growers and consultants to inform irrigation and nutrient management.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The project is located near Modesto, CA. It serves nut growers in California, Irrigated Lands Regulatory Program (ILRP) coalition representatives, and regulatory agency personnel, particularly in the Central Valley. A secondary, broader audience is related to other orchard crops, including tree-fruit and citrus growers and potentially vineyard managers. The audience includes agricultural consultants, farm advisors, and industry representatives leading the Central Valley Salinity Alternatives for Long-Term Sustainability (CV-SALTS) and the state ILRP.

RecipientName: Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians
AwardAmountNotes: This grant provided the Shingle Springs Band of the Miwok Indians with oil spill response equipment to help protect its economic resources and sensitive sites during an oil spill.
ProjectAbstract: N/A

AwardAmountNotes: This grant provided the Lake County Fire Protection District with oil spill response equipment to help protect its economic resources and sensitive sites during an oil spill.

ProjectAbstract: This grant provided the County of San Luis Obispo Parks and Recreation Department with oil spill response equipment to help protect its economic resources and sensitive sites during an oil spill.
This grant provided equipment to the San Rafael Fire Department to protect their economic resources and sensitive sites during an oil spill.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Developing Tools and Information to Enhance Water-Nitrogen Use Efficiency and Sustainability of Avocado Production Systems
RecipientName: Ali Montazar, University of California Cooperative Extension
AwardAmountNotes: In-kind match of 3% of salary for PI Montazar and 1% in salary from the co-PI and one supporter, who are also farm advisors.
ProjectAbstract: Avocados require careful water and nitrogen (N) management to ensure optimal yield and high-quality fruits. This is even more important due to uncertain water supplies, mandatory reductions of water use, and the rising cost of water. This study intends to (1) develop N-uptake and N-removal crop coefficient values (2) conduct an evaluation on the current leaching practices (3) develop data and adapt CropManage for avocado (4) evaluate Soil Solution Access Tubes, soil nitrate quick tests, and leaf analysis as tools for nitrate and salinity management and (5) disseminate tools and information.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The field experiments will be conducted in 15 commercial avocado sites in southern California. The PI’s large-scale irrigation study has been carried out in collaboration with seven cooperating farms in San Diego, Riverside, Orange, and Ventura Counties.

ProjectAbstract: The project will identify and permit actions to increase ecological function and floodplain connectivity of the Lower Sutter Bypass. Planning includes designs, permits, and monitoring plans for restoration of 1600 acres. The project will increase streamflow and river-floodplain connections from the Feather and Sacramento Rivers, and Butte Creek, while restoring riparian and wetland habitat to increase ecosystem productivity and species diversity in a migratory corridor.

ProjectTitle: Basso/Ingalls Restoration Project: Design and CEQA
AwardAmountNotes: Part of this grant ($106,951) is funded by the Fisheries Restoration Grant Program. Other match includes: the Grantee ($16,559), Applies River Sciences ($28,400), Stanislaus County ($31,393), Ron Zanker ($8,000).
ProjectAbstract: The project will create new spawning and rearing habitat for Fall-run Chinook salmon and O. Mykiss in the Tuolumne River in an area with extensive scraped dredge mining tailings. Floodplain surfaces would be lowered, improving juvenile salmonid rearing habitat.

ProjectTitle: Riparian Buffer Fencing on Iron Gate Reservoir and Copco 1 Reservoir
AwardAmountNotes: Part of this grant ($800,862) is funded under the Proposition 68 Habitat Improvement Grant Program. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service is contributing $125,000
ProjectAbstract: The project will install riparian buffer fencing on Copco 1 Reservoir and Iron Gate Reservoir to protect riparian habitat once the Copco 1 Dam and Iron Gate Dam are removed from the Klamath River. The riparian buffer fencing will prevent open-range cattle, feral horses, and deleterious ATV use in the reservoir footprint.  This will create optimal conditions for habitat to recover and preserve historic and cultural sites.

ProjectTitle: Ormond Beach Perkins Road Area Restoration Project
AwardAmountNotes: Part of this grant ($251,945) is funded under the Proposition 68 Habitat Improvement Grant Program.
ProjectAbstract: The project includes two primary objectives:  1. Restore, enhance and manage 41.5 acres of nationally decreasing wetland habitat; and,  2. Engage in community outreach and education, particularly with local disadvantaged communities, to facilitate restoration planning and stewardship of the area.

ProjectTitle: Enhancing Dune Habitat and Ecosystem Function within Northern Monterey County State Parks
RecipientName: San Jose State University Research Foundation
ProjectAbstract: The project will expand local dune restoration efforts to Moss Landing State Beach and Zmudowski State Beach. The project will remove invasive species, reestablish native dune vegetation, and encourage sand deposition using natural materials, to enhance habitat quality and increase coastal resilience.

ProjectTitle: Eel River Basinwide Restoration and Conservation Planning and Implementation
ProjectAbstract: This project will advance Eel River Basinwide restoration will develop a framework for Eel River program management, prioritize restoration and conservation actions to connect and protect wildlife corridors to advance 30x30 goals, develop a focal-species monitoring plan, and suppress and plan for the future suppression of non-native fish species within the basin to support aquatic species recovery.

ProjectTitle: Tribal Landscape for Climate Resilience and Watershed Restoration Project
ProjectAbstract: The project goals are to restore cultural and watershed resilience to lands impacted by the 2020 Bear and North Fire complex in the Middle Fork of the Feather River Watershed.

ProjectTitle: Recovery of the Foothill Yellow-Legged Frog in the Tuolumne and Merced River Watersheds
AwardAmountNotes: In-kind funding will come from Yosemite National Park ($16,320), Stillwater Sciences ($60,000) and the San Francisco Zoo $14,560.
ProjectAbstract: The project will protect and enhance the biodiversity of the Tuolumne and Merced River watersheds by improving aquatic habitat and increasing resilience of Sierran foothill species, such as the declining foothill yellow-legged frog (FYLF). Objectives are to: continue removal efforts of the invasive bullfrog from key dispersal areas threatening FYLF and other stream-dwelling species; and (2) translocate FYLF to suitable unoccupied habitats, increasing the resiliency of this declining species.

ProjectTitle: Los Peñasquitos Watershed Assessment & Invasive Plant Management Plan
AwardAmountNotes: City of San Diego and CA State Parks are contributing $500,000 in in-kind match.
ProjectAbstract: The project will conduct a comprehensive, multi-jurisdictional watershed assessment to map, evaluate and prioritize areas needing invasive plant treatment on a watershed-scale. Deliverables include the identification of enhancement/restoration opportunities for native riparian, wetland and transitional habitats within the watershed and identifying areas for source control of invasive seedbanks and propagules to support downstream efforts that include restoration of the Los Peñasquitos Lagoon.

ProjectTitle: Fish Passage and Habitat Improvements to Dry Creek Yuba and Nevada Counties, California
AwardAmountNotes: Grantee (Sierra Streams Institute) is contributing $7,000 in in-kind match. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is contributing $387,182.80. Sutter Buttes Regional Land Trust is contributing $23,988.20.
ProjectAbstract: In conjunction with the USAF-funded removal of Beale Lake Dam, this project will restore access to 15 miles of historic riverine migratory corridor for fall-run Chinook salmon and the federally threatened Central Valley steelhead and create 3.4 acres of improved spawning habitat. The project will remove a low flow crossing downstream of the dam site which severely limits fish passage, and will improve spawning habitat upstream through strategic gravel augmentation at four sites

ProjectTitle: Fish Passage Construction on Trabuco Creek
AwardAmountNotes: Part of this grant ($5,155,944) is funded under the Proposition 68 Southern Steelhead Grant Program. The Wildlife Conservation Board - $65,987.60. NOAA - $14,614,391.23. Department of Transportation - $22,138,275.19. Highpointe - $2,900,000.
ProjectAbstract: The project will remediate the last two barriers, at the I-5 and Metrolink bridges on Trabuco Creek, and permanently restore historic access of endangered southern California steelhead to 15 miles of upstream habitat and restore anadromy to the headwaters.

AwardAmountNotes: Grantee (Yurok Tribe) is contributing 160,000. The U.S. Bureau of Reclamation is contributing $3,016,943
ProjectAbstract: The proposed fish habitat restoration implementation project addresses degraded stream channel conditions along a 1-mile section of Weaver Creek, a coho bearing stream with high intrinsic potential, by alleviating channel incision and increasing floodplain inundation extent and frequency. These rehabilitation objectives create instream habitat for many special status species, bolster riparian habitat, and ensure a single threaded wet channel during summertime baseflow conditions.

ProjectTitle: Restore Wildcat Creek at Brook Road
AwardAmountNotes: Grantee (East Bay Regional Park District) is contributing $1,430,082 in in-kind match.
ProjectAbstract: Wildcat Creek is an important local tributary to the San Francisco Bay Watershed. Unfortunately, urbanization has dramatically altered its historical flow and impaired the water quality. As part of a multijurisdictional approach to improve watershed health, the Park District is restoring 8,500 linear feet of channel bed and bank, installing watershed-based native plants, and constructing two free-span bridges to keep park visitors, dogs, and maintenance vehicles out of the wetted channel.

ProjectTitle: MWCD - Parks Creek Flow Enhancement Through Diversion Modification
AwardAmountNotes: The Federal National Fish & Wildlife Foundation is contributing $1,521,468 in match.
ProjectAbstract: The project is located at MWCD's existing diversion on Parks Creek, a major tributary to the Shasta River. The project will provide year-round fish passage and install a compliant fish screen. As a result, MWCD's will be able to provide instream benefit and meet its commitment to the Upper Parks Creek flow strategy developed with CDFW and NOAA.

ProjectTitle: Upper Green Valley Creek Coho Habitat Enhancement Planning Project
ProjectAbstract: The project will finalize the engineering, design, revegetation, and permitting plans to install large woody debris structures in the creek. This project aims to improve climate change resiliency and habitat sustainability in the watershed. The ultimate goal is to develop an implementation plan that will improve rearing and spawning habitat for coho salmon in upper Green Valley Creek.

ProjectTitle: Streamflow Conservation Strategies for North Coast Timberlands
AwardAmountNotes: Mendocino & Humboldt Redwood Company is contributing $202,920 in match.
ProjectAbstract: This project will reduce the impacts of summer surface water withdrawals on high priority salmon streams managed by Mendocino and Humboldt Redwood Company. The project will implement water saving improvements associated with road dust abatement activities by installing eight groundwater storage systems and by re-surfacing 114 miles of native road. The combined benefit of this work is estimated to prevent the withdrawal of 1 million gallons from waterways, annually.

ProjectTitle: Rock Creek Culvert Removal Fish Passage Project
AwardAmountNotes: U.S. Bureau of Land Management is contributing $950,000 in match.
ProjectAbstract: The project will remove an abandoned railroad grade crossing in Rock Creek, tributary to the Sacramento River in Shasta County. Two 12-foot diameter by 320 linear foot culverts are covered by approximately 46,000 cubic yards of fill, spanning the width of the Rock Creek canyon. The crossing has been severely damaged as a result of 2018's Carr Fire. It is no longer functional, is a fish passage barrier, and poses a high risk of complete failure if not addressed.

ProjectTitle: Wood Creek Phase III: Felt Ranch Off-Channel Rearing Habitat
AwardAmountNotes: Grantee (Northcoast Regional Land Trust) is contributing $486,864. CDFW is contributing $14,200 in in-kind match. Point Blue is contributing $435,000. Humboldt County is contributing $20,000 in in-kind match.
ProjectAbstract: This shovel-ready project will create new anadromous salmonid stream habitat in a high-priority watershed (Voight 2020), enhancing 12 acres of wetlands and improving hydrologic connectivity to an additional 24 acres of protected wetlands. One culvert will be relocated to provide improved fish passage. The project will create a diversity of slow-water aquatic habitats in the stream-estuary ecotone for use by fish, wildlife, and vegetation, including non-natal rearing of Coho Salmon.

ProjectTitle: Upper Russian River Groundwater Dependent Ecosystem and Interconnected Surface Water Study
AwardAmountNotes: City of Ukiah is contributing $45,000 in in-kind match.
ProjectAbstract: This study will characterize surface water-groundwater interconnection and groundwater-dependent ecosystems that support Chinook salmon and steelhead in the upper Russian River and its tributaries. Geochemical, biological, and physical monitoring will be combined with hydrological modeling to characterize the spatial extent and timing of interconnection under management and climate scenarios and ecosystem impacts. Results will guide water resource management and conservation land acquisitions.

The project will produce designs, permits, and CEQA studies for removing obstacles to fish passage, restoring riparian habitat, and reducing impacts to receiving waters, while promoting water conservation and water security. The project will also conduct outreach and education to promote watershed restoration and assist a small business owner in a designated Severely Economically Disadvantaged Area.

ProjectTitle: Wildlife Restoration through Rescue and Removal of Abandoned Animals in Northern California
RecipientName: Noah's Ark Animal Haven and Rescue
ProjectAbstract: This project will address the threat to wildlife from abandoned domestic animals associated with cannabis cultivation in northern California. Predation by cats and dogs is considered one of the primary threats to wild birds and mammals, driving extinction and threatening biodiversity. California counties and tribal lands have experienced increased rates of animal dumping and abandonment with the downturn of the cannabis economy.

ProjectTitle: A Framework for Restoring California’s Watersheds: Training and Empowerment in Action
ProjectAbstract: The reclamation and remediation project will result in a study and framework, as outlined in Assembly Bill 2643, and train workforce development teams in California to conduct comprehensive reclamation of cannabis impacted lands. The project will complete the reclamation of 18 public land cannabis cultivation sites.

ProjectTitle: Town Creek Bioengineering and Education Project
ProjectAbstract: The restoration project is located in the Town of Covelo. The project includes planting living willow and cottonwood in addition to local streambed aggregate. The project will result in arresting and remediating bank erosion while improving riparian conditions and aquatic habitat. The riparian planting and monitoring efforts will include student participation from Round Valley Elementary and Round Valley High School. The project will further tribal, agency, and community partnerships as they work together to identify additional watershed restoration opportunities.

ProjectTitle: Amplifying Reclamation Through Outreach and Education
ProjectAbstract: The project will document cleanup and restoration of cannabis impacted lands through written content, videos, and photographs with an emphasis on local partnerships, non-profits, and Tribal reclamation crews.

ProjectTitle: Sediment Reduction on Cannabis Farms in Priority Northern Watersheds
ProjectAbstract: The project will reduce sediment delivery to streams from cannabis cultivation and restore degraded habitat across 41 priority watersheds in the Eel, Mad, Trinity, and Mattole watersheds. The project develops engineer designs, completes CEQA and permitting, and implements projects. Projects include upgrading stream culverts to allow for improved streambed function and species migration, fish-bearing stream bed and bank restoration, decommissioning onstream ponds that impede flow and contribute sediment, and revegetation.

The project will provide a feasibility analysis, planning and permitting, and 65% designs for restoring approximately 1.25 miles of lower Wilson Creek, a primary tributary to the Van Duzen watershed in Humboldt County. Designs will address riparian habitat and water quality, improve floodplain drainage efficiency, maximize sediment transportation capacity, return flows to the lower trans delta reach of the channel, create complex instream habitat, and provide fish passage. The Van Duzen watershed serves as critical habitat for several fish species protected under the Endangered Species Act.

ProjectTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Pest Diseases and Sustainable Management in Cannabis Sativa
RecipientName: Regents of the University of California Davis
ProjectAbstract: The project will improve our scientific understanding of phytopathological and phytosanitary threats to the California cannabis industry. The project will assess some of the other negative externalities of cannabis cultivation.

The project will remove toxic pesticides, refuse, and all infrastructure from up to 10 public land cannabis cultivation sites within the Monterey Ranger District, Los Padres National Forest (Ventana and Silver Peak Wilderness Areas). The project will mitigate the potential for direct poisoning of CESA listed species and other wildlife, remove sources of contamination within headwater streams, and monitor reclamation effectiveness.

ProjectTitle: Evaluation and Remediation of Illegal Hemp Cultivation
RecipientName: California Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectAbstract: The project will address environmental damage, including contamination and waste, from non-compliant hemp cultivation sites. The project will develop and implement a comprehensive program to identify, remediate, and monitor non-compliant hemp cultivation sites and facilitate compliance.

ProjectTitle: Rancho Sequoia Road and Sediment Assessment
ProjectAbstract: The planning project will result in a comprehensive assement of road networks in the Eel River Watershed, including the Rancho Sequoia Road network. The project also includes capacity building and educational workshops on road maintenance best management practices for cannabis cultivators and other landowners. The project will result in 100% design plans, CEQA studies, and environmental permits for implementing road improvements that benefit steelhead, Coho salmon, and other aquatic species.

The planning and implementation project will result in the recontouring and restoration of oak woodland habitat previously impacted by grading and cultivation. The project will enhance native species habitat and improve habitat connectivity.

The project will replace a culvert that is a barrier to all life stages of anadromous fish. The project includes installing a bottomless arch culvert and minor channel realignment using a stream simulation approach.

ProjectTitle: Mainstem Ten Mile River Habitat Enhancement (Phase 2)
ProjectAbstract: The implementation project will result in large-scale instream and off-channel/floodplain habitat enhancement for coho salmon in the lower maintstem Ten Mile River. Five fish habitat enhancement features will be constructed per final project design plans. Cannabis grant funding will supplement funding awarded by WRGB (Phase 1) and NOAA (Implementation).

ProjectTitle: Sustaining Cleanup, Restoration and Remediation Within Traditionally Underserved Communities
AwardAmountNotes: Although matching funds are not required, most CRGP grant funded projects provide some commitment of matching funds and/or in-kind services
ProjectAbstract: The project will increase the scope and scale of cleanup, restoration, and remediation of cannabis-impacted lands and communities by addressing social and institutional barriers within traditionally underserved communities. The project includes facilitating partnerships among impacted landowners and conservation entities through in-person and virtual community outreach; research-based education regarding environmental impacts of cannabis cultivation; and developing and implementing tools and resources to build capacity and sustained success among CRGP grantees.

ProjectTitle: Non-Lethal Monitoring Methods to Understand Pollinator Community Diversity and Rare Species in Cannabis and Harvested Forests
RecipientName: National Council for Air and Stream Improvement
AwardAmountNotes: Although matching funds are not required, most CRGP grant funded projects provide some commitment of matching funds and/or in-kind services
ProjectAbstract: The project addresses the need for non-lethal monitoring systems for pollinator populations, particularly for rare and threatened bumble bees. The project develops sensor-based systems using computer vision and machine learning to enable automated species-level identification without lethal capture. The project is focused on mixed cannabis and forest landscapes. Data are collected on pollinator behavior, population dynamics, and habitat use.  The project assess how landscape composition influences pollinator behavior.

ProjectTitle: Southern Coho Salmon Captive Broodstock Rearing and Coastal Monitoring Project
RecipientName: Monterey Bay Salmon and Trout Project
AwardAmountNotes: Although matching funds are not required, most CRGP grant funded projects provide some commitment of matching funds and/or in-kind services
ProjectAbstract: The project will maintain the viability of critically endangered coho salmon populations south of San Francisco Bay . It will produce up to 30,000 smolt Central California Coho salmon for release to targeted watersheds and  rear to maturity 380 coho salmon from each annual spawning event.  A portion of the juvenile fish produced  will be tagged using passive integrated transponder tags to facilitate tracking released fish. The project includes partnerships with the Muchia Te’ Indigenous Land Trust and Amah Mutsun Tribal Band and it includes extensive outreach and education efforts.

ProjectTitle: Bioacoustic Monitoring and Analysis to Support Wildlife Conservation in California
RecipientName: Regents of the University of California, UC Berkeley
AwardAmountNotes: Although matching funds are not required, most CRGP grant funded projects provide some commitment of matching funds and/or in-kind services
ProjectAbstract: The project will conduct acoustic monitoring co-developed with Tribes in Humboldt, Siskiyou, and Tulare Counties and assess patterns of wildlife occurrence, including responses of gray wolves and their prey, to cannabis agriculture and other land uses; provide acoustic monitoring for California Spotted Owl and other forest species in 29 counties; and expand the use of the Wildlife Soundhub acoustic data platform. The project will improve our understanding of the impacts of cannabis cultivation on wildlife, provide solutions, and contribute to species and habitat conservation.

ProjectTitle: CA Sentinel Site Network: Long-Term Native Species Monitoring to Improve the Effectiveness of Assessing the Impacts of Climate and Land-Use Changes, Including Cannabis Cultivation
RecipientName: Regents of the University of California
AwardAmountNotes: Although matching funds are not required, most CRGP grant funded projects provide some commitment of matching funds and/or in-kind services
ProjectAbstract: The project expands the California Biodiversity Network’s Sentinel Site Network to 37 of the 41 University of California Natural Reserve System reserves. It adds 4 wildlife survey locations and a paired climate monitoring station at each reserve. The monitoring applies to the Cannabis Program’s California Environmental Monitoring and Assessment Framework terrestrial field methods and data processing protocols. All sites  have a permanent weather station, and a subset of sites have a Motus animal tracking tower, consistent with CDFW SSN sites.

ProjectTitle: Operationalizing the California Environmental Flows Framework to Inform Sustainable Cannabis Water Use Practices and Policies
RecipientName: Southern California Coastal Water Research Project (SCCWRP), Joint Powers Authority
AwardAmountNotes: Although matching funds are not required, most CRGP grant funded projects provide some commitment of matching funds and/or in-kind services
ProjectAbstract: The project  provides guidance for using scientifically defensible environmental flow recommendations to support healthy freshwater ecosystems. The project will improve the accuracy of existing streamflow predictions in statewide models; inventory existing flow regulations and evaluate whether objectives are being met. The project develops outreach materials to facilitate the application of California Environmental Flows Framework (CEFF) tools in support of sustainable water management.

ProjectTitle: Quantifying Dynamic Trends in Biodiversity and Wildlife Habitat in Response to Cannabis Agriculture, Land Use Change, and Shifting Climates Across California
AwardAmountNotes: Although matching funds are not required, most CRGP grant funded projects provide some commitment of matching funds and/or in-kind services
ProjectAbstract: The project will result in comprehensive, temporally dynamic assessments of wildlife populations and community health across the state that can be readily updated as changes occur. The project will develop an automated data processing pipeline for acoustic data; examine how species occupancy and diversity has changed over the last four decades; and explore how a range of future land use decisions will interact with projected climate changes to influence wildlife distributions in the state.

ProjectTitle: Promoting Effective Integrated Pest Management Practices for the Control of Grapevine Trunk Diseases
ProjectAbstract: This project aims to educate grape growers and other industry members about the importance of adopting preventative practices against the wood diseases that threaten California vineyards. Hands-on demonstrations and outreach activities will take place across the state. Beneficiaries, including grape growers, pest control advisors, and company representatives, will gain practical knowledge to help make better decisions for reducing the impact of trunk diseases. This project will support healthier vineyards, improve crop sustainability and increase profitability for California’s grape industry.

ProjectTitle: New Trainings and Online Resources to Improve Weed Management Practices Along Roadsides and Other Non-Crop Environments
ProjectAbstract: Non-crop weed managers working to reduce use of herbicide need training and resources. They face complex priorities and weed-related threats–such as wildfire–with limited guidance. Training helps minimize applicator risk and improve equitable access to resources. We will provide new trainings on localized weed control with herbicides and mowing, make short videos on these methods, add features to the online WeedCUT decision support tool, and establish ongoing scientific review of WeedCUT. Weed managers and the communities they serve will benefit from free training and robust online resources.

ProjectTitle: Advancing Receptor Interference Technologies as a Tool for Managing Key Insect Pests of Vegetables
ProjectAbstract: Western flower thrips and diamondback moth are important pests of lettuce and brassica crops in California. Management relies on high-risk chemistries that pose a risk to human and environmental health. We previously identified several bioactive peptides that bind strongly to receptors of these insects, which interfere with normal biological processes in the insects. Here, we aim to advance this work to develop biologically based insecticides. The work supports the need to develop new sustainable pest management options for key insect pests that threaten leafy vegetable production.

ProjectTitle: Improvement of Silica Gel Dust and Dust Mixtures as Safer Alternatives, and Development of a Lethal Harborage for German Cockroach Control
ProjectAbstract: The German cockroach negatively impacts health and wellbeing by generating asthma-inducing allergens, transmitting pathogens, and causing psychological distress. Lower-income groups are disproportionately affected due to a lack of resources. Conventional methods of controlling German cockroaches use hazardous insecticides that are often ineffective. This project aims to provide an alternative control strategy to control German cockroaches by improving the utilization of silica gel, a safer and low-cost physical insecticide, along with boric acid – a very low toxicity compound.

ProjectTitle: NemaBlock: RNAi Based Resistance for Walnut Orchards
ProjectAbstract: Root lesion nematodes (P. vulnus) are significant pests that impact the health and productivity of walnut orchards. Current methods for controlling these nematodes are limited, and there is a pressing need for new, effective strategies. This project aims to develop walnut rootstocks with enhanced resistance to root lesion nematodes by integrating host-induced RNAi constructs targeting key nematode genes. We will evaluate the effectiveness of these resistance rootstocks through both controlled greenhouse experiments and field trials.

ProjectTitle: Developing Cultural and Biological-Based Practices for Managing Navel Orangeworm and Invasive Carpophilus Beetle in Almond and Pistachio Orchards
ProjectAbstract: Explores alternative pest management methods for almond and pistachio's two most destructive insect pests, navel orangeworm and invasive carpophilus beetle. These pests could inflict >100 million USD in direct loss annually. This project intends to reduce the unnecessary use of chemical pesticides in orchards while increasing farm’s economic returns and benefitting a healthy community and environment. The beneficiaries of this project are nut crop growers in California, nut crop industries, researchers and pest control consultants, and the community residing in the Central Valley.

ProjectTitle: Restoring Nur (Chinook salmon) and the Winnemem Wintu Tribe to the Winnemem Waywaket (McCloud River) via Volitional Fish Passage
ProjectAbstract: The purpose of this project is to develop an Action Plan and advance the engineering design of a downstream migration guidance facility that will accommodate a range of fish passage strategies and may include volitional and non-volitional components in the lower McCloud River to support reintroduction of endangered Nur (Chinook salmon) into their historical high elevation, cold-water spawning and rearing habitat in the Winnemem Waywaket (McCloud River) above Keswick and Shasta dams.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Advancing Irrigation and Nitrogen Management of Cantaloupe in Southern California using Field Experiments and Remote Sensing
RecipientName: Amir Verdi, University of California, Riverside
ProjectAbstract: This project will enhance the sustainability of cantaloupe production in Southern California through field irrigation and nitrogen (N) trials and drone-based remote sensing. Two cantaloupe irrigation and N management field trials will be conducted to assess the response of one variety to nine treatments (3 irrigation levels × 3 N rates). Multispectral and thermal drone data will be collected and analysis of variance will be performed to determine the impact of the treatments on crop yield. Yield prediction models will also be developed. Results will be presented at grower meetings and events.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: The trial locations will be located at UCR Agricultural Experiment Station (UCR AES) in Riverside and the UCANR Desert Research and Extension Center (UC DREC) in Holtville, CA. The results will serve southern California melon growers, crop consultants and industry stakeholders, with particular emphasis on cantaloupe growers.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: North Fork Feather All Lands Forest Health
RecipientName: Sierra Institute for Community and Environment
ProjectAbstract: Sierra Institute, in partnership with the Plumas National Forest, private timberland managers, and local landowners, will use requested funds to improve forest health in some of the largest remaining green stands within the Dixie Fire footprint, including near Taylorsville and Greenville. Treatments will enhance resilience to drought, pests, and wildfires across diverse ownerships. This project builds on past treatments to boost forest health.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Upper San Joaquin Kaiser East Protection Project
ProjectAbstract: The Upper San Joaquin Kaiser East Protection Project protects the Southern Sierra's greatest resources of the upper San Joaquin River. This strategic location within the Sierra National Forest of Fresno County will protect green forests, meadows, watershed health, habitat for endangered species, businesses, and disadvantaged and tribal communities. Treatments include 1,250 acres of Fuel Reduction, Prescribed Fire, Pest Management, Reforestation, and Biomass Utilization.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Burney Hat Creak Forest Health Project Phase III
ProjectAbstract: The Fall River RCD is requesting $6,999,465.05 to implement a variety of forest health projects on federal and private lands in northeastern California. These projects will consist of an assortment of fuels reduction treatments. Project activities are designed to improve forest health at a landscape level, support local wood products industries, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, sequester and store carbon, reduce wildfire risk and reintroduce fire into a fire adapted ecosystem.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectAbstract: The Project is located west of Hwy 395 along the Mammoth Scenic Loop and near the June Mountain community on the Inyo National Forest. This landscape scale project will restore 2,062 acres across three different NEPA areas through commercial thinning, fuels reduction, prescribed burning, and biomass removal. The Project addresses overcrowding, drought, pest infestations, while enhancing forest health, protecting water resources, and increasing wildfire resilience in priority areas.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectAbstract: The project proposes fuels reduction treatments on 1,288 acres within the Eldorado National Forest. The project reduces the risk of high-intensity, large-scale wildfires, protects communities, improves forest resilience and enhances wildlife habitat within the upper Mokelumne River watershed entirely within the WUI. The proposed mastication and hand thinning treatments will reduce excess surface fuels in strategic locations along ridge tops and upper slopes that connect with past treatments.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Northern Mendocino County Forest Health Collaborative - Phase II
ProjectAbstract: The Project encompasses 867 acres in a fire prone, priority watershed for Coho Recovery in the South Fork Eel region, northern Mendocino County. This phase 2 project includes fuel reduction and reforestation treatments across two timberland properties, to increase fire resiliency, enhance forest and riparian refugia, improve wild food production, and provide access to a remote forest for community to engage in the recovery of a redwood forest, post decades of industrial timber management.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Southern Humboldt Forest Health and Wildfire Resilience Program
ProjectAbstract: This scalable collaborative program will restore forests and oak woodlands associated with three projects in Southern Humboldt: 1) two shovel-ready forest health projects located in Humboldt Redwoods State Park to build continuity to previous projects, 2) fuels reduction and prescribed fire treatments on industrial and private properties on the strategically and culturally important Mail Ridge and 3) community outreach and future project planning.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Arundo Removal & Restoration for Riparian Forest Health - Ventura River Watershed
ProjectAbstract: The Ojai Valley Land Conservancy proposes a landscape-scale riparian forest restoration project across 802 contiguous acres on Lion Creek, San Antonio Creek, and the Ventura River. This project will include invasive species removal (Arundo donax and other noxious species), reforestation with native hardwood trees and plants, and maintenance and monitoring (including early-detection, rapid-response protocol) to ensure successful outcomes for forest health and resilience.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectAbstract: Project is focused on Lake County, northern California. Proposed treatments include fuels reduction, prescribed fire, pest management and reforestation on 800 acres of very high fire-risk forestland. Treatment areas are being maintained and expanded from previously funded projects to ensure the sustainability of the initial investment. Project includes the planning of a CalVTP ProjectSpecific Analysis for a future funding cycle

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Connecting Landscape Scale Forest Health Projects in Santa Cruz County
RecipientName: Resource Conservation District of Santa Cruz County
ProjectAbstract: This project will fund 830 acres of forest management treatments strategically placed in a "ring" around populated areas in Santa Cruz County. Project activities include reforestation, invasive species removal, prescribed fire, thinning encroaching conifers, and mastication. These treatments will improve ecosystem health and reduce wildfire risk to low-income populations in the City of Santa Cruz, Aptos, Capitola, and the San Lorenzo Valley.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: Butte Creek/Buck Mountain Forest Health Project
ProjectAbstract: The project will increase forest health, diversity, and resilience across ~2,361 acres while facilitating long-term maintenance under the CalVTP/PEIR. Treatments (thinning, pruning, biomass removal, burning, etc.) focus on private forestlands and public rights of ways in eastern Humboldt County and complement fuels reduction efforts on adjacent public lands. The project is in a high firerisk area bordering State HWY 36; BLM; USFS; PG&E powerlines; and roads providing essential ingress/egress.

AgencyDept: Department of Forestry and Fire Protection
ProjectTitle: TreePeople San Bernardino National Forest Post-Fire Recovery & Resilience
ProjectAbstract: To mitigate the impacts of catastrophic fire on the San Bernardino National Forest (SBNF), TreePeople will implement restoration treatments to include site preparation, invasive weed abatement, multi-species reforestation, and rare conifer monitoring, across approximately 935 acres of fire scar sites. These efforts will be critical to recover forest health, by increasing carbon storage, improving watershed health, and promoting wildfire resilience.

AgencyDept: Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery
ProjectAbstract: The purpose of this plan is to address the reoccurring damage to the upstream terminus of the ACB  revetment system along the northern slope of the Pedley Landfill. A new revetment system design is  proposed to reinforce the revetment system at the terminus, protecting the landfill from erosion and  potential exposure. The new revetment system consists of a 2-ton riprap revetment system placed on  top of the repaired ACB revetment system, with the ACB revetment system acting as the riprap’s  drainage layer.
GeographicLocationServedNotes: Pedley Landfill (SWIS # 33-CR-0014)    Jurupa Ave and Van Buren Blvd.    Riverside, CA    92503

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Village Market Place Nutrition Incentive Program
ProjectAbstract: This program will leverage and build upon the existing work of Community Services Unlimited Inc. to increase the consumption of CA Grown produce by CalFresh eligible residents in South Central Los Angeles by offering incentives at our food retail social enterprise, The Village Market Place (VMP), and nutrition education.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Maximizing Impact: Market Match as a Tool For Health Equity and Economic Prosperity in California
ProjectAbstract: Market Match distributes $5,463,224 in healthy food incentives, matching $8,194,836 of CalFresh via 364,215 transactions at 269 California direct-to-consumer sites. This project will expand promotion strategies to increase the reach of Market Match in high-need regions, increasing healthy food purchasing in underserved populations. This will result in an estimated 11.2 million servings of fresh fruits and vegetables1 for low-income shoppers and an economic multiplier effect of $32.7 million for rural communities.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectAbstract: With More California is a nutrition incentive program that aims to build pathways to not only access more, but more different foods. This program will link food and nutritional security by increasing the consumption of California-grown produce as a way of diversifying household diets. With More California will be operated by and redeemable at With Love Market & Café, a grocery store and community space dedicated to healthy food access in South Los Angeles.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: San Jose Healthy Corner Store Program - Food Bucks
ProjectAbstract: The Food Trust seeks to expand its Food Bucks nutrition incentive program, offered in conjunction with the San Jose Healthy Corner Store Initiative (HCSI). For over a decade, The Food Trust has supported small food retailers through HCSI to procure, market and sell healthy foods through providing technical assistance and small equipment (i.e. refrigeration, shelving, etc.).

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectAbstract: The Shasta Market Match program will enable all five certified farmers markets operated by the Shasta Growers Association to provide $15 nutrition incentives to CalFresh shoppers for each farmers market visit. This project is a significant opportunity to address a critical need. Feeding America estimates that 72% of Shasta County is eligible for CalFresh.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Saticoy Farmers Market EBT and Nutrition Incentives Program
ProjectAbstract: The Saticoy Food Hub (SFH) launched the Saticoy Certified Farmers Market in 2024 to improve access to fresh, locally sourced produce in Saticoy, a USDA Food Desert and a Designated Disadvantaged Community. This program can support the most vulnerable community members and address food insecurity.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectAbstract: Farm Fresh LA supports a hyperlocal food economy by leveraging CalFresh dollars and connecting local growers and communities of color. This is a short supply chain network of neighborhood corner stores sourcing locally grown produce from immigrant growers of color to collectively support communities of color. Together, we are combating food apartheid by providing CalFresh households access to fresh produce, all while supporting the local economy.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: El Mercado Market Match/ Igualar Sus Beneficios
ProjectAbstract: El Mercado, a key initiative of the Community Health Trust of Pajaro Valley (CHT), is a seasonal weekly farmers' market running from April to October. Its primary goal is to tackle food insecurity and chronic illness by providing Pajaro Valley families with easy access to fresh, locally grown produce and essential wellness resources. El Mini Mercado is CHT’s year-round food pantry, located at the Diabetes Health Center in Watsonville. It offers a variety of fresh, seasonal produce and is open five days a week.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectAbstract: The Chico Natural Foods Cooperative (CNFC, the Co-op) will continue its existing, successful CNIP-funded matching program, which offers a discount to CalFresh shoppers at the Point of Sale on California-grown fresh produce at its Butte County brick-and-mortar retail location.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Avenue 33 Farmstand Nutrition Incentive Program for Locally Grown and Sourced Produce at a Weekly Community Farmstand in Lincoln Heights
ProjectAbstract: The Avenue 33 Community Farmstand works to help Lincoln Heights residents become food secure with nutritious food and cultivating community access where there are barriers, forming a food hub that supports local growers and businesses, and creates nourishing jobs.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectTitle: Expanding Double Up Food Bucks: Bridging the Gap to Healthy, Affordable Produce in Monterey County’s Low Food Access Areas
ProjectAbstract: The Monterey County Double Up Food Bucks program, a partnership between Aspire Health and the Blue Zones Project, aims to expand its efforts to improve access to healthy, farm-fresh produce in areas of Monterey County with limited food availability.

AgencyDept: CA Department of Food and Agriculture
ProjectAbstract: Acta Non Verba: Youth Urban Farm Project’s Beetbox CSA program will distribute 1:1 incentive to CalFresh customers for the weekly purchase of fresh, Bay Area-grown fruits and vegetables in East and West Oakland. We will reach at least 15 new CalFresh customers. The incentives will complement our nutrition education for Oakland youth, through farm-to-table cooking classes at our youth programs: Camp ANV (seasonal camps serving more than 200 youth each year) and No Limit Leadership Program (NLLP) for teens.

ProjectTitle: California Guaranteed Income Pilot Program for Older Adults
AwardAmountNotes: grant contingent on fundraising for evaluation w/in 6 months, which is anticipated approx. $250,000
ProjectAbstract: GiveDirectly will provide $1,200 per month for 12 months to 240 low-income seniors 60+ who are currently waitlisted for Housing Choice Vouchers or Project-Based Vouchers in San Joaquin County. The project aims to alleviate homelessness and housing instability through temporary cash aid and connection to the broader social safety net. Research will examine outcomes like housing, wellbeing, land ong-term stability.
